note: GENERATED by gen_atlas.py from _atlas.json and the gossip packs (do not edit by hand). Meitou only.

Blister Hill.known: The Holy Nation's capital. The Holy Lord Phoenix sits on his throne there.
explored: Two towns in one: the Phoenix's walled quarter, and everyone else outside it.
Paladins at every corner. Pray loudly, and do not be a Shek.

Bad Teeth.known: A Holy Nation town that guards the pass into the green valleys.
explored: Farmers, priests and a lot of Holy Sentinels with nothing to do.
What comes down the pass from the wilds gets stopped here, or eaten.

Stack.known: A Holy Nation town between the Hub and the Western Hive. Traders like it; so do thieves.
explored: Good shops for a frontier town.
The Nation watches the road to the Hub from here, and the Hive watches back.

Rebirth.known: Where the Holy Nation sends sinners to work until Okran forgives them. He rarely does.
explored: A mine with walls, and slaves who were citizens last week.
Nobody leaves Rebirth by asking.

Okran's Fist.known: A Holy Nation fortress on the north-east road.
explored: Paladins and Sentinels, drilled and bored.
The Nation's door to the north-east. Closed to most.

Okran's Shield.known: A Holy Nation fortress that closes the valley road like a gate.
explored: Built across a choke-point; every caravan passes under its walls.
The garrison stops the Skin Bandits coming down from the dark.

Heft.known: Capital of the United Cities. Emperor Tengu holds court there.
explored: Nobles, samurai and the Emperor's palace. Money talks; everyone else bows.
Lord Ohta keeps his house here too, and the Emperor's ear.

Stoat.known: The last United Cities town before the eastern desert. Lord Inaba governs it.
explored: Fed by the stone camp and the slave farm nearby.
A good place to buy water and a bad place to be a runaway slave.

Sho-Battai.known: A big United Cities town in the middle of the desert. Lord Nagata rules it.
explored: The only hat shop in the Cities, and a thieves' guild nobody admits to.
It eats what Port North digs up.

Brink.known: A United Cities town on the coast. Lady Tsugi governs it.
explored: It lives on what Eyesocket's slaves produce.
Reavers walk the roads outside like they own them. Some days they do.

Bark.known: A United Cities town built around old lagoons on the north-east coast. Lady Sanda governs it.
explored: Half a port, with no ships. Supplies come from Port North and Port South.
Fishing smells and noble perfume, both strong.

Drifter's Last.known: A United Cities town in the south-west, ringed by farms. Lady Merin lives there.
explored: Farms outside, guards inside, and trouble from the hills now and then.
Plenty of newcomers start out here with nothing.

Catun.known: A United Cities fortress town on a plateau in the Bonefields.
explored: Home of the Catun Scrapmasters, the best robotics workshop in the Cities.
Well walled. The Bonefields are no place to be caught outside.

Heng.known: The Empire's trading town, joined to Trader's Edge by a metal bridge.
explored: Everything has a price here, and a Guild man to take a cut of it.
The bridge to Trader's Edge is worth the walk.

Trader's Edge.known: The Traders Guild's own settlement, on a plateau next to Heng.
explored: Where the Guild keeps its ledgers and its friends.
Samurai guard it. The Guild pays them well.

Mourn.known: A mining town built inside an old metal ruin. A slave revolt broke it.
explored: The Tech Hunters own it now, and the Cities still say it is theirs.
Empty mines and angry ghosts, as the locals tell it.

Admag.known: Capital of the Shek Kingdom, on a hill with one way in. Esata the Stone Golem rules there.
explored: The Hundred Guardians stand at the gate. They are not a ceremony.
Honour matters here more than cats. Fight well or do not fight.

Squin.known: A Shek town east of Admag, run on wind power.
explored: The lights flicker when the wind drops. Nobody here complains about it.
A Shek town, but traders of every kind pass through.

Last Stand.known: A Shek fortress where old warriors go to die well, fighting the Bugmaster's spiders.
explored: Grey warriors sharpening blades they will not bring back.
Arach is just over the hill. You can hear it at night.

The Great Fortress.known: A Shek fortress, mostly ruined, near New Kralia.
explored: Only the police station and the hall still stand.
Grand name, broken walls.

The Hub.known: A broken town between the Shek and the Holy Nation, fought over for years.
explored: The Trade Ninjas run it now, quietly.
Cheap beds, cheap bar, and nobody asks where you got it.

Shark.known: The Swamp's big town, full of ex-slaves, gangs and worse. The Swampers say they run it.
explored: The Hounds actually run it. Everybody knows; nobody says.
You can buy anything in Shark. You can also be bought.

Mud Town.known: A Swamper village north of Shark.
explored: Stilts, mud and people who would rather not be found.
Odd folk drift in here, some worth hiring.

Rot.known: A Hounds village in the Swamp.
explored: Ears and Big Grim's people. Friendly, if you are one of them.
There is not much in Rot but the Hounds and the smell.

World's End.known: A Tech Hunter town on a mountain, inside Holy Nation lands.
explored: The Machinists build things the Nation would burn.
It stays free by being useful, and by being hard to climb.

Black Scratch.known: The Tech Hunters' home, built around an ancient structure on a hill.
explored: The Great Library is here. Bring cats, and an interest in old things.
The Tech Hunter bar has stories. Most are true.

Flats Lagoon.known: A Tech Hunter town by the lagoon. Safer than it looks.
explored: Harpooners on the shore, Hive caravans on the road. They do not always agree.
A good place to rest between bad places.

Spring.known: The Anti-Slavers' mountain base. Tinfist is there.
explored: Built to be defended, and it has been.
Every slave who reaches Spring is free. Every slaver who reaches it is not.

Black Desert City.known: A town of skeletons, from after the Second Empire. No humans live there.
explored: Repair beds instead of beds. The bar sells things no person needs.
Sadneil keeps the Skeleton Bar. He remembers a long time.
Red cloaks, sharp blades and long memories.
They pay for cannibal heads. They ask fewer questions about the rest.

Mongrel.known: A walled town in the fog. Nobody goes out at night there.
explored: The Fogmen come to the gates most nights.
The people here are hard, because the soft ones were taken.

Western Hive.known: The Western Hive's village, on an island in acid water.
explored: The water burns. The drones do not mind.
Soldier drones meet you at the shore. Be polite.

Cannibal Capital.known: Once a town called Deadcat. The cannibals took it.
explored: It looks like a town from a distance. That is the trap.
The Gran' Wizard lives here, among more cannibals than you can count.

First Village.known: A cannibal village in the north of Darkfinger.
explored: The Meat Lord's table is here, and the cages that feed it.
Do not accept an invitation to dinner.

Cannibals.known: A cannibal village on the plains.
explored: Alder Quill's kitchen and Mother Brine's cure-house, if the stories are true. They are.
The smoke comes from the cure-house. Do not think about it.

Throne of the Bugmaster.known: A crater full of spiders in Arach.
explored: Skin spiders and blood spiders, more than anyone has counted.
Something sits on a throne at the bottom. The spiders guard it.

Cat-Lon's Exile.known: Domes deep in the Ashlands, under something huge hanging in the sky.
explored: The Second Empire's exiles live here, and their Stormthralls.
One of the old empire's own, still alive, still angry.

Tower of Fog.known: A lone tower on an island. Fogmen live there.
explored: Fogmen everywhere, and one of their princes.
Nobody goes in by choice.

Skinhouse HQ.known: Where the Skin Bandits live, somewhere in the dark lands.
explored: Peeler machines. People go in whole.
Savant rules it from a throne.

Swamp Ninja Base.known: A hidden base of the Swamp Ninjas.
explored: Ninjas of every rank, and Shade over them.
Hidden well; that was the point.

Cactus Den.known: A watchtower in Spine Canyon, home of the Sand Ninjas.
explored: Sand Ninja Oni lives at the top. Walking in uninvited makes enemies.
Close to Tengu's Vault, and they like it that way.

Red Sabre Hideout.known: The Red Sabres' hideout in the south-west Swamp.
explored: Twenty-odd Red Sabres and their boss.
Good gear inside, for whoever survives taking it.

Dust King Tower.known: A fortified tower in the Border Zone. The Dust King's.
explored: Walls, a gate and crossbows on the walls. Dust Bandits by the dozen.
The Dust King does not come down.

Fort Simion.known: The Rebel Farmers' fort in Sinkuun.
explored: Swamp domes and shacks, and Boss Simion over them.
Farmers who stopped paying the Holy Nation, and lived.

Cult Village.known: A village on the coast where the Preacher's cult lives.
explored: They say blood in the soil brings a harvest. They test it.
Do not get caught here.

Tower of Abuse.known: An old lab in Venge. The Thrall Masters use it.
explored: Prisoners on the top floor. Agnu, among them, if the stories are right.
Venge's lasers make the walk there worse.

Tengu's Vault.known: The United Cities' prison in the Skimsands.
explored: Samurai guards, a Warden, floors of cells.
Those inside were put there for good.

Flotsam Village.known: Where the Flotsam Ninjas hide, somewhere in the Hidden Forest.
explored: Refugees and deserters from the Holy Nation, still praying to Okran in their own way.
Moll leads them. The Nation wants her head.

Port North.known: A slavers' work camp in the Great Desert. Not a port at all.
explored: Stone and iron, dug by slaves.
Half the Cities eat because of this place.

Eyesocket.known: A slave camp on a hill by the coast.
explored: Slave Master Grande runs it.
Brink lives on what is dug here.

Slave Markets.known: Where slavers sell what they catch.
explored: Cages, buyers and a Slave Market Master.
Keep your papers close.

Black Dog HQ.known: The Black Dogs' snailhouse, west of Black Scratch.
explored: Thick walls, a good gate and short tempers.
Start nothing here.

Bast.known: A United Cities city the Holy Nation destroyed.
explored: Ruins and squatters now.
The war passed through and took everything.

Rebel Base.known: A small bar in the Border Zone where outlaws drink.
explored: The Trade Ninjas sell things there you cannot buy elsewhere.
Crossbows, blueprints, and no questions.
Manhunters, and nothing but.
They hunt people for money. You are people.

Clownsteady.known: A small United Cities town in the Hook, fed by the slave farms nearby.
explored: Compact, busy, and well supplied.
Ask the traders here; they carry things the bigger towns do not.

Port South.known: A slavers' stone camp in the desert. Like Port North, it is no port.
explored: Stone mines and ore, worked by slaves.
Slave Master Wada keeps the place running.

Stone Camp.known: A slavers' work camp between Stoat and Sho-Battai.
explored: Stone mines, and slaves who will die in them.
Slave Master Haga lives here, behind guards.

Slave Farm.known: A slavers' cactus farm near Heng.
explored: Rows of cactus as far as you can see, and the slaves who tend them.
Slave Mistress Ren rules it from a noble house.

Holy Mines.known: The Holy Nation's mines, worked by servants and prisoners.
explored: High Overseers with whips, and sinners with picks.
Five of them, scattered through the Nation's hills.

Holy Farm.known: Holy Nation farms on the green lands.
explored: Greenfruit, cotton, wheat. The Nation eats because of them.
Lower servants work; paladins watch.

Holy Military Base.known: Holy Nation outposts facing the Fog Islands.
explored: Built to hold back the Fogmen.
The soldiers here do not sleep well.

Waystation.known: Tech Hunter waystations on the long roads.
explored: A bed, a bar and a shop where there would otherwise be nothing.
Tech Hunters stop here on the way to the ruins.

Ark.known: The Reavers' stronghold, in Stobe's Garden.
explored: Cages for prisoners, and Reavers who think they are free men.
Valamon leads them from here.

Grayflayer Village.known: A Swamp village run by the Grayflayers.
explored: Big Gray's people. The Swampers' hardest gang.
Come with friends or do not come.

Iron HQ.known: The Skeleton Bandits' hold in the Crags.
explored: Metal walls, and old skeletons who decided to be bandits.
Elder leads them.

The Old Prison.known: A bandit stronghold south of Mourn.
explored: An old tower like a lab, and Gorrillo's bandits all over it.
Gorrillo himself is worth a fortune to someone.
They sell crabs. They also are crabs, in spirit.
The Crab Queen holds court here.

New Kralia.known: The hold of Kral's Chosen, south of Admag.
explored: Shek who think the Kingdom has gone soft. They fight anyone who comes.
Fifteen or twenty of them, all looking for a death worth singing about.

Shek Ruins.known: Broken buildings on a hill east of Admag.
explored: An old border post, wrecked in some war.
Nothing lives here but scavengers.

Southern Hive Village.known: A village of the Southern Hive.
explored: Pink-skinned hivers, nothing like the western kind.
They do not trade. They take.
Drones at work, soldiers at the edge, a trader if you are welcome.
Beak things and gorillos come at it often.

Distant Hive Village.known: A Western Hive village far from the others, in Sinkuun.
explored: Hivers far from home.
Quiet, until something comes out of the desert.

Settled Nomad Village.known: A Nomad village that stopped wandering, south of Raptor Island.
explored: They sell animals and packs.
Settled, but they still talk like the road is home.

Ashland Dome I.known: A great dome in the Ashlands, south-east of the Skinhouse.
explored: Many floors around a winding stair.
The Head of Agriculture is here, with thralls of the old Legion.

Deadhive Overrun.known: A dead town near the Fog Islands. The Fogmen have it.
explored: It was someone's town once.
The Fogmen took it, and they keep what they take.

Expedition 4.known: A town the Tech Hunters built and left, in Stobe's Garden.
explored: The wind generator still turns. Nobody knows why they left.
Their notes mention it.

Burn's Tower.known: A tower in the northern Floodlands, full of machines.
explored: Old technology everywhere.
A skeleton called Burn lives here, and he is not friendly yet.

Spider Factory.known: An old factory on the Forbidden Isle.
explored: Security spiders by the hundred.
Whatever it built, it is still building.

Holy Lord Phoenix.about: The Holy Nation's ruler, Okran's voice on earth. Each Phoenix follows the last; the faithful say it is the same man reborn.
Holy Lord Phoenix.wanted_for: Shek and Flotsam alike would pay for his end.

Emperor Tengu.about: Rules the Cities from his palace in Heft. Rich, old and suspicious.

Esata the Stone Golem.about: The Shek Queen. A warrior first, and a queen because of it.

Seto.about: The Queen's daughter. Some Shek hope she will change the Kingdom. Some fear she will.

Tinfist.about: A man in a machine body who wants every slave freed and every slaver dead.
Tinfist.wanted_for: The United Cities want him for war on their slave trade.

Moll.about: Leads the Flotsam Ninjas against the Holy Nation, from somewhere in the Hidden Forest.
Moll.wanted_for: The Holy Nation wants her for rebellion.

High Inquisitor Valtena.about: The Holy Nation's chief inquisitor. Sinners fear her; so do the faithful.

Lord Ohta.about: One of the Cities' great lords, never far from the Emperor.

Lord Nagata.about: Governs Sho-Battai and lives well on Port North's stone.

Lady Tsugi.about: Governs Brink. The Reavers on her roads are her problem, and she does not like problems.

Lord Inaba.about: Governs Stoat, the last town before the eastern desert.

Lord Yoshinaga.about: A lord of the Noble Circle, with a house and guards to match.

Longen.about: A Guild man with an Emperor's manners and a merchant's heart.

Cannibal Grand Wizard.about: Leader of all the cannibals. They say he hears a bell no one rings.
Cannibal Grand Wizard.wanted_for: Wanted everywhere for leading the cannibals.

Meat Lord.epithet: the host of the First Village
Meat Lord.about: A cannibal leader with manners, a long table and a full larder.
Meat Lord.wanted_for: Wanted for the people at his table.

Alder Quill.about: A Holy Nation kitchen priest who went over to the cannibals. Gentle, they say. That makes it worse.
Alder Quill.wanted_for: The Holy Nation and the Cities want him for what he cooks.

Mother Brine.about: Keeps the cannibals' cure-house. She fed them through the bad winter, and they never asked with what.
Mother Brine.wanted_for: The Holy Nation and the Cities want her for the cure-house.

Bugmaster.vague: A man who keeps spiders, somewhere in the east. Old Shek go to die fighting his pets.
Bugmaster.about: Sits on a throne at the bottom of a crater, guarded by more spiders than anyone has counted.
Bugmaster.wanted_for: A criminal of the old kind, wanted by every faction that has lost people to his spiders.

Mad Cat-Lon.vague: An exile of the old empire, still alive somewhere in the ash. Nobody who says so has been there.
Mad Cat-Lon.about: One of the Second Empire's own, living among his Stormthralls in the Ashlands. Old, and still angry.

Fog Prince.vague: The Fogmen have princes. One lives in a tower in the sea, they say.
Fog Prince.about: A prince of the Fogmen, in a tower full of them.

Savant.vague: The Skin Bandits have a master. He lives in the dark, and he collects skins.
Savant.about: Rules the Skin Bandits from his throne. The peelers are his.
Savant.wanted_for: Wanted for the people he has skinned.

Shade.vague: The Swamp Ninjas have a leader called Shade. Their base is somewhere in the wetlands.
Shade.about: Leads the Swamp Ninjas from their hidden base.
Shade.wanted_for: Wanted for the Swamp Ninjas' raids.

Sand Ninja Oni.vague: The Sand Ninjas answer to one called Oni. Somewhere in the canyons.
Sand Ninja Oni.about: Leads the Sand Ninjas from the top of a watchtower.

Red Sabre Boss.vague: The Red Sabres have a boss and a hideout, somewhere in the Swamp.
Red Sabre Boss.about: Runs the Red Sabres from their hideout.
Red Sabre Boss.wanted_for: Wanted for the Red Sabres' killings.

Dust King.about: King of the Dust Bandits, in a tower he never leaves.
Dust King.wanted_for: Wanted for leading the Dust Bandits.

Boss Simion.about: Leads farmers who stopped paying the Holy Nation, and lived.
Boss Simion.wanted_for: The Holy Nation wants him for rebellion.

The Preacher.about: Leads the coast cult. Blood in the soil, he preaches.

Valamon.vague: The Reavers have a leader, a Shek called Valamon. Their stronghold is somewhere in the far north.
Valamon.about: A Shek who left the Kingdom and leads the Reavers. Tall, fond of a fight, and not fond of anyone.
Valamon.wanted_for: Wanted for the Reavers' raids and slaving.

Sadneil.about: A skeleton who keeps the bar in Black Desert City and remembers the Second Empire.

Agnu.epithet: a prisoner of the Thrall Masters
Agnu.vague: Someone is held at the top of a tower in Venge, they say.
Agnu.about: Held by the Thrall Masters in the Tower of Abuse.

Gutterhead.about: Leads the Scavengers. Whatever you dropped, he has it.

Flying Bull.vague: A Shek called Flying Bull wants a war. Where he is, nobody says.
Flying Bull.about: A Shek warmonger who wants the old wars back.

Ghost.vague: A Shek they call Ghost. Seen once, never twice.
Ghost.about: A Shek outcast with a bounty and no fear.

Blue Eyes.epithet: an outlaw of the Holy Nation's borders
Blue Eyes.about: Wanted by the Holy Nation for heresy. Says what the priests will not.

Tora The Fearless.about: A Shek warrior the Kingdom calls dishonoured.

Slave Master Haga.about: Runs the Stone Camp and lives like a noble, behind noble guards.

Elder.about: An old skeleton who leads the Skeleton Bandits from the Crags.

Big Gray.about: Runs the Grayflayers, the Swamp's hardest gang.

Gorrillo.about: Leads the bandits holed up in the old prison south of Mourn.

Crab Queen.about: Leads the Crab Raiders from Crab Town.
Crab Queen.wanted_for: Wanted for the Crab Raiders' raids.

Slave Mistress Ren.about: Rules the cactus slave farm near Heng from a noble house.

Slave Master Wada.about: Keeps the slaves of Port South digging.

Big Grim.about: Leads the Hounds, who run Shark whatever the Swampers say.

Head of Agriculture.epithet: an old official of the Empire
Head of Agriculture.vague: Someone from the old empire still keeps a dome in the Ashlands, they say.
Head of Agriculture.about: An official of the old empire, still in his dome in the Ashlands with his thralls.

Orsa Quillon.region: Border Zone and The Great Desert
Orsa Quillon.about: A woman strings a rope across the Hub road and calls it a toll. Orsa Quillon. Three caravans have stopped paying her with their lives. Her band camps a few nights at a time along the trade roads, then moves on.
Orsa Quillon.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Benna Quillon.epithet: who took over Orsa Quillon's gang
Benna Quillon.region: Border Zone and The Great Desert
Benna Quillon.about: Grew up minding her aunt's rope on the Hub road and learned the toll trade before she could count. She moved the rope a mile east the week Orsa fell and went on charging the caravans. Took over Orsa Quillon's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Quillon's was.
Benna Quillon.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Ferrant Dray.about: Ferrant Dray was a lordling with a title, an estate and debts. Now he is a highwayman with a title and a sword. The Cities want the title removed, along with the head. His company sells its swords from camp to camp and never winters in one place.
Ferrant Dray.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Coll Varrick.epithet: who took over Ferrant Dray's gang
Coll Varrick.about: A deserter from the United Cities' samurai who sold Dray his sword for a share. He kept the company's books, so the men followed the man who knew where the money was. Took over Ferrant Dray's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Dray's was.
Coll Varrick.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Hask Morrow.about: A deserter named Hask Morrow walked off his post with his armour and his orders. He now plunders pilgrims on the roads. The Nation wants an example made. Since leaving the Nation he sleeps rough, a different hill every few nights.
Hask Morrow.wanted_for: Wanted by The Holy Nation, United Cities.

Tobin Ashe.epithet: who took over Hask Morrow's gang
Tobin Ashe.about: A former Holy Nation acolyte who ran away with Morrow rather than face the Inquisition. He still prays every morning, though he no longer says to whom. Took over Hask Morrow's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Morrow's was.
Tobin Ashe.wanted_for: Wanted by The Holy Nation, United Cities.

Sarn Ashvael.region: The Great Desert and Okran's Gulf
Sarn Ashvael.about: A starving man named Sarn Ashvael preaches that the Empty Bowl will take what the road owes. His mob follows him. Starving men with a prophet are worse than starving men alone. His people follow the caravans and the food, wherever they go.
Sarn Ashvael.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, The Holy Nation, Shek Kingdom, Traders Guild.

Gristle Mott.epithet: who took over Sarn Ashvael's gang
Gristle Mott.region: The Great Desert and Okran's Gulf
Gristle Mott.about: Fed Ashvael's starving band for years on whatever the roads gave up. When the leader was gone, the hungry went with the one who held the pot. Took over Sarn Ashvael's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Ashvael's was.
Gristle Mott.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, The Holy Nation, Shek Kingdom, Traders Guild.

Veldt Harrow.about: Veldt Harrow was a slaver. A legal one, if you like. Then the markets thinned and he stopped selling and started burying. They call him the Tallyman. He counts every head he keeps. He moves his pens along the desert roads, selling as he goes.
Veldt Harrow.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild, Anti-Slavers.

Sella Harrow.epithet: who took over Veldt Harrow's gang
Sella Harrow.about: Ran the ledgers and the buyers while her husband ran the chains. Most of his old clients never noticed the change in management. Took over Veldt Harrow's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Harrow's was.
Sella Harrow.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild, Anti-Slavers.

Borun Vahl.about: Borun Vahl, the Oathless. He broke his vow in the stone circle and was cast out. He kills those who cross his path, and calls it honour. He goes where the fighting is and stays until it runs out.
Borun Vahl.wanted_for: Wanted by Shek Kingdom, United Cities.

Ruk Vahl.epithet: who took over Borun Vahl's gang
Ruk Vahl.about: Borun's younger brother, quieter and worse. He fought his way to the front of the berserkers inside a day. Took over Borun Vahl's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Vahl's was.
Ruk Vahl.wanted_for: Wanted by Shek Kingdom, United Cities.

Ilsa Hearthmourn.about: Ilsa Hearthmourn was a Pacifier of the Flame. She stopped believing and began to pray for the end of Okran. The heresy is spreading. She is spreading it. She preaches from camp to camp, always a step ahead of the Inquisition.
Ilsa Hearthmourn.wanted_for: Wanted by The Holy Nation, United Cities.

Brother Caddoc.epithet: who took over Ilsa Hearthmourn's gang
Brother Caddoc.about: Hearthmourn's first convert, a farmhand who heard her preach at a well and walked off his master's field that night. He preaches her words badly but loudly. Took over Ilsa Hearthmourn's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Hearthmourn's was.
Brother Caddoc.wanted_for: Wanted by The Holy Nation, United Cities.

Hodd Crake.about: Hodd Crake was one of ours. A hunter of the plains. Somewhere out there, he started eating what he killed. He still wears the colours. That shames every hunter alive. He follows the cannibal raids south and back north again.
Hodd Crake.wanted_for: Wanted by The Holy Nation, United Cities, Shek Kingdom, Cannibal Hunters.

Wenna Crake.epithet: who took over Hodd Crake's gang
Wenna Crake.about: Raised in her father's hunting camps on the edge of the Cannibal Plains. She reads tracks better than he did and takes fewer prisoners. Took over Hodd Crake's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Crake's was.
Wenna Crake.wanted_for: Wanted by The Holy Nation, United Cities, Shek Kingdom, Cannibal Hunters.

Pim Sillery.about: Pim Sillery was one of us until the day he walked out of a ruin with every schematic and left three hunters in the dark. He calls himself the Magpie. He likes shiny things. He drifts from ruin to ruin with whatever he can carry.
Pim Sillery.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild, Tech Hunters.

Doss Kettering.epithet: who took over Pim Sillery's gang
Doss Kettering.about: Sillery's digging partner for ten years and the only one who knew where the good caches were buried. He's been digging them up one by one ever since. Took over Pim Sillery's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Sillery's was.
Doss Kettering.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild, Tech Hunters.

Teshin Ro.about: Teshin Ro. A ronin. His lord died, and he has been paying for it ever since. He duels travellers and cuts the ones who refuse. Many dead, last season. He walks the border roads looking for duels and for work.
Teshin Ro.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Aiko Ro.epithet: who took over Teshin Ro's gang
Aiko Ro.about: Teshin's only student, who learned the sword by losing to him every day for four years. She took his blade from the grave and his reputation from the road. Took over Teshin Ro's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Ro's was.
Aiko Ro.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Ysolde Gorehollow.about: Ysolde Gorehollow. The Bloodmother. She drains prisoners into jars and sells the contents to anyone sick enough to buy. Her raiders worship it. The Cities want the jars broken. Her raiders sweep the Ashlands and never stay to be found.
Ysolde Gorehollow.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, The Holy Nation, Shek Kingdom.

Marrow Jess.epithet: who took over Ysolde Gorehollow's gang
Marrow Jess.about: Swore blood-sisterhood with Gorehollow in a cannibal pit they both climbed out of. The raiders say she's the reason Ysolde ever came back from a fight. Took over Ysolde Gorehollow's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Gorehollow's was.
Marrow Jess.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, The Holy Nation, Shek Kingdom.

Marta Cull.about: Marta Cull, the Brine-Wife. She ties salvagers to the tide line and times their drowning. The Guild's coastal runs are dry because of her. Make the sea quiet. Her crew lands on a different stretch of coast each time.
Marta Cull.wanted_for: Wanted by Traders Guild, United Cities.

Fenn Cull.epithet: who took over Marta Cull's gang
Fenn Cull.about: Born on one of his mother's ships and never set foot in a town until he was twelve. He runs the crew like she did, only younger and with less patience. Took over Marta Cull's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Cull's was.
Fenn Cull.wanted_for: Wanted by Traders Guild, United Cities.

Teodric Clackjaw.about: Teodric Clackjaw. He fought in the crab pits until he cut an opponent in half after the bell. Banned, he took a shell for armour and a grudge for a god. The Guild wants him quiet. His raiders come up the beaches and are gone before the patrols arrive.
Teodric Clackjaw.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild, Mercenary Guild.

Snapper Dunne.epithet: who took over Teodric Clackjaw's gang
Snapper Dunne.about: The loudest of Clackjaw's raiders and the first one up the beach every time. He took over by shouting longer than anyone else. Took over Teodric Clackjaw's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Clackjaw's was.
Snapper Dunne.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild, Mercenary Guild.

Maruka Tal-Khesh.epithet: a wandering exile of Kral's Chosen
Maruka Tal-Khesh.about: Maruka Tal-Khesh calls herself the Hundred Cuts. She tests every wanderer with a blade, and counts. Few reach ten. The Kingdom does not approve of her excess. She marches from canyon to canyon looking for a worthy fight.
Maruka Tal-Khesh.wanted_for: Wanted by Shek Kingdom, United Cities.

Oshar Tal-Khesh.epithet: who took over Maruka Tal-Khesh's gang
Oshar Tal-Khesh.about: Carried Maruka's shield for six years and her name since she fell. The exiles follow him because he never once dropped it. Took over Maruka Tal-Khesh's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Tal-Khesh's was.
Oshar Tal-Khesh.wanted_for: Wanted by Shek Kingdom, United Cities.

Aldous Peel.about: Aldous Peel is a skinner in a coat of skins. He takes the living and strips them whole, and wears the work. Some call him the Tailor. The Nation calls him an abomination. I call him a client for you. He walks the Roam looking for new skins and never sleeps twice in the same place.
Aldous Peel.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, The Holy Nation, Shek Kingdom.

Merrin Stitch.epithet: who took over Aldous Peel's gang
Merrin Stitch.about: Peel took him off a slaver's cart as a boy and taught him the needle instead of the knife. He finished his master's last coat himself. Took over Aldous Peel's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Peel's was.
Merrin Stitch.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, The Holy Nation, Shek Kingdom.

Mister Tuppence.about: Mister Tuppence is a Skeleton who sells road protection. Pay him a fee, and he will not break your cart. Do not pay, and he breaks your cart, and you. It is quite orderly. He doesn't tire and doesn't stop, so his camp is wherever he is.
Mister Tuppence.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Mister Ha'penny.epithet: who took over Mister Tuppence's gang
Mister Ha'penny.about: A skeleton Tuppence built from scavenged parts to carry his loot. Nobody told it to stop when its maker fell, so it picked up the ledger and carried on. Took over Mister Tuppence's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Tuppence's was.
Mister Ha'penny.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Ulla Weeper.region: The Shrieking Forest and The Swamp
Ulla Weeper.about: Ulla Weeper leads the shriekers. She was a mother once, they say, before the swamp took the rest. Now she screams and her followers scream with her, and anything that hears it dies. Her band moves through the forest and the swamp, and you hear them before you see them.
Ulla Weeper.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild, Swampers.

Keening Bel.epithet: who took over Ulla Weeper's gang
Keening Bel.region: The Shrieking Forest and The Swamp
Keening Bel.about: The shrieker whose voice carries furthest in the forest. Ulla's band follows the sound now, the way they used to follow Ulla. Took over Ulla Weeper's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Weeper's was.
Keening Bel.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild, Swampers.

Dunmar Quell.about: Dunmar Quell calls himself the Red Captain. He has taken over the Red Sabres and means to rule the swamp. Every town in the wet lands pays him now, or does not pay anything again. He moves between the swamp villages, collecting what he calls tax.
Dunmar Quell.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild, The Holy Nation, Swampers.

Sabre Hollis.epithet: who took over Dunmar Quell's gang
Sabre Hollis.about: Quell's tax collector, who knew every village in the swamp and what each one could pay. The Red Sabres decided he was too useful to lose. Took over Dunmar Quell's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Quell's was.
Sabre Hollis.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild, The Holy Nation, Swampers.

Gammer Tuck.about: Gammer Tuck is an old farmer with a long scythe and a longer grudge. He leads rebels who burn tax-collectors. He is usually drunk. He is also quite good with the scythe. His rebels move from farm to farm, taking the harvest as they go.
Gammer Tuck.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Nan Tuck.epithet: who took over Gammer Tuck's gang
Nan Tuck.about: Gammer's wife, who planned most of the farm raids from their kitchen table while he took the credit. She doesn't bother hiding it now. Took over Gammer Tuck's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Tuck's was.
Nan Tuck.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Sayo of the Grey Ribbon.about: Sayo. The Grey Ribbon. A sand ninja who kills for hire. She leaves a ribbon on the body, and takes the coin from the corpse's pocket. We have eleven ribbons on file. She takes work in one town and is gone by the next.
Sayo of the Grey Ribbon.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild, Shek Kingdom.

Kiri of the Torn Ribbon.epithet: who took over Sayo of the Grey Ribbon's gang
Kiri of the Torn Ribbon.about: Sayo's last pupil, who tore her own grey ribbon in half the day her teacher was taken. She still takes work from the people who used to hire Sayo. Took over Sayo of the Grey Ribbon's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Sayo's was.
Kiri of the Torn Ribbon.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild, Shek Kingdom.

Cuddy Pell.about: Cuddy Pell. Mad as a flooded fish and twice as slippery. He claims the road is his dinner plate and he sets a place for every traveller. He carries a goat head in a sack. We do not ask. He wanders the flooded coast with no plan anyone can follow.
Cuddy Pell.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild, Fisher.

Little Pell.epithet: who took over Cuddy Pell's gang
Little Pell.about: Nobody's sure if he's Cuddy's son, his brother or just someone who started dressing like him. The flooded coast doesn't seem to care which. Took over Cuddy Pell's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Pell's was.
Little Pell.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild, Fisher.

Tchik of Seven Voices.about: Tchik of Seven Voices. A Hiver drone who left the hive and took seven others with him. They speak as one, and they speak to you in seven different voices. Bring them down. He leads his band through the northern wastes, never back the same way.
Tchik of Seven Voices.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Shek Kingdom, Traders Guild.

Tchak of Three Voices.epithet: who took over Tchik of Seven Voices's gang
Tchak of Three Voices.about: A drone that followed Tchik out of the hive and learned to speak in his manner. It hasn't learned all seven voices yet, but the band follows the three it has. Took over Tchik of Seven Voices's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Tchik's was.
Tchak of Three Voices.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Shek Kingdom, Traders Guild.

Elric Vosk.region: Border Zone and The Great Desert
Elric Vosk.about: Elric Vosk was hired to guard a caravan. His employer cut his pay. He killed the master, the drivers and the pack-beasts, and kept the bell. Now he sells the road he once guarded. He follows the work across the desert and the border country.
Elric Vosk.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild, Mercenary Guild.

Garrow Vosk.epithet: who took over Elric Vosk's gang
Garrow Vosk.region: Border Zone and The Great Desert
Garrow Vosk.about: Elric's cousin, who joined the company to pay off a debt and stayed because the pay was better than farming. He takes the contracts Elric used to take, for a little less. Took over Elric Vosk's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Vosk's was.
Garrow Vosk.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild, Mercenary Guild.

Pyke Ludlow.about: Pyke Ludlow was an Anti-Slaver. A true one. Then he decided that anyone who ever owned or traded a person deserved the same, and began killing them. Merchants. Farmers. A boy who sold a rope. He moves between the slave roads, hitting the caravans and vanishing.
Pyke Ludlow.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Esme Ludlow.epithet: who took over Pyke Ludlow's gang
Esme Ludlow.about: Pyke's sister, who handled the freed slaves while he handled the slavers. She still hits the caravans, and the Anti-Slavers still pretend not to know her. Took over Pyke Ludlow's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Ludlow's was.
Esme Ludlow.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Orrin Vask.about: A slaver who buys cheap on the border and sells dear in the Nation's farms. He keeps his ledgers neater than his pens. He moves his stock along the desert roads, town to town.
Orrin Vask.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Delia Vask.epithet: who took over Orrin Vask's gang
Delia Vask.about: Orrin's partner in the slave trade from the start, and the one who did the bargaining. She kept the buyers and the routes and changed nothing else. Took over Orrin Vask's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Vask's was.
Delia Vask.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Aldric Roane.about: Once a Holy Sentinel, now wanted by the people he used to march with. He left the Nation over something he won't talk about. He keeps moving through the Nation's hills, away from his old order.
Aldric Roane.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Brother Hale.epithet: who took over Aldric Roane's gang
Brother Hale.about: Deserted the Holy Nation the same night as Roane and has covered his back ever since. He still leads that frightened band through the Nation's hills. Took over Aldric Roane's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Roane's was.
Brother Hale.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Karrash Red-Hand.about: A berserker who paints his hands in the blood of his last fight and doesn't wash until the next one. He drifts from fight to fight across the plains.
Karrash Red-Hand.wanted_for: Wanted by Shek Kingdom, United Cities.

Karrash the Younger.epithet: who took over Karrash Red-Hand's gang
Karrash the Younger.about: Karrash Red-Hand's son, raised among berserkers and painted red before he could walk. He took his father's place at the next fight. Took over Karrash Red-Hand's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Red-Hand's was.
Karrash the Younger.wanted_for: Wanted by Shek Kingdom, United Cities.

Veth of the Closed Hand.about: A hiveless drone who runs a band of outcasts in the north. It trades fairly and fights unfairly. His band crosses the northern wastes and rarely stops.
Veth of the Closed Hand.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Shek Kingdom.

Veth of the Open Hand.epithet: who took over Veth of the Closed Hand's gang
Veth of the Open Hand.about: A drone that broke with Veth over how to share the spoils, then came back to take the band once Veth was gone. It shares more, and the band likes it better. Took over Veth of the Closed Hand's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Veth's was.
Veth of the Open Hand.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Shek Kingdom.

Hollis Gantry.about: A tech hunter who stopped asking permission to dig in other people's ruins. The towns he sells to don't ask either. He goes from ruin to ruin, selling what he digs up.
Hollis Gantry.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Tam Gantry.epithet: who took over Hollis Gantry's gang
Tam Gantry.about: Hollis's nephew, sent to learn the scavenging trade and good at it from the start. He sells the old world's junk to anyone who pays. Took over Hollis Gantry's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Gantry's was.
Tam Gantry.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Gaffer Marrowbone.about: An old cannibal chief, scarred and slow, who has outlived every hunter sent after him. His raiders range across the plains, never long in one village.
Gaffer Marrowbone.wanted_for: Wanted by The Holy Nation, United Cities.

Old Gristlejaw.epithet: who took over Gaffer Marrowbone's gang
Old Gristlejaw.about: The eldest of Marrowbone's hunters, who has outlived three chiefs already. The cannibals follow him because he always finds meat. Took over Gaffer Marrowbone's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Marrowbone's was.
Old Gristlejaw.wanted_for: Wanted by The Holy Nation, United Cities.

Rennik Salt.region: Border Zone and The Great Desert
Rennik Salt.about: A dust boss who camps by the trade roads and takes a cut of whatever passes. He calls it rent. His band camps by the roads for a few nights at a time, then moves on.
Rennik Salt.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Brin Salt.epithet: who took over Rennik Salt's gang
Brin Salt.region: Border Zone and The Great Desert
Brin Salt.about: Rennik's daughter, born in a dust camp and raised on the road. She keeps her father's camps moving along the roads. Took over Rennik Salt's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Salt's was.
Brin Salt.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Slate Fennick.about: An outlaw swordsman who sells his blade to whoever pays first, and has been on both sides of most feuds in the border country. His swordsmen roam the border country looking for easy marks.
Slate Fennick.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Corra Fennick.epithet: who took over Slate Fennick's gang
Corra Fennick.about: Slate's sister, who ran the band's camps and supplies. She picked up his sword and found the men already used to taking her orders. Took over Slate Fennick's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Fennick's was.
Corra Fennick.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Brannoch Teel.about: A slave hunter who brings runaways back for the reward and doesn't much care whose they were. He rides the roads after runaways, wherever they run.
Brannoch Teel.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Wade Teel.epithet: who took over Brannoch Teel's gang
Wade Teel.about: Brannoch's brother and the better tracker of the two. Runaways who thought the hunt was over learned otherwise. Took over Brannoch Teel's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Teel's was.
Wade Teel.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, Traders Guild.

Hob Lenner.about: A reaver who raids the coast from small boats and is gone before the alarm bell stops ringing. His crew comes in from the coast and is gone by morning.
Hob Lenner.wanted_for: Wanted by Traders Guild, United Cities.

Ness Lenner.epithet: who took over Hob Lenner's gang
Ness Lenner.about: Hob's first mate, who knew the coast and the tides better than he ever did. The crew voted for her before his body was cold. Took over Hob Lenner's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Lenner's was.
Ness Lenner.wanted_for: Wanted by Traders Guild, United Cities.

Dolan Pike.region: The Great Desert and Okran's Gulf
Dolan Pike.about: Leader of a starving band that grew too big to feed. They take what they need from anyone on the road. His people follow the caravans, starving or not.
Dolan Pike.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, The Holy Nation, Shek Kingdom.

Scrag Pike.epithet: who took over Dolan Pike's gang
Scrag Pike.region: The Great Desert and Okran's Gulf
Scrag Pike.about: Dolan's cousin, as hungry and as desperate as the rest of the band. He leads by finding food first and sharing it second. Took over Dolan Pike's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Pike's was.
Scrag Pike.wanted_for: Wanted by United Cities, The Holy Nation, Shek Kingdom.

Isolde Marr.about: A mercenary captain whose company works for anyone with the cats, outlaws included. She's turned down more jobs than she's taken, but never for being too dirty. The company goes wherever the pay is, camp to camp.
Isolde Marr.wanted_for: Wanted by Flotsam Ninjas, United Cities.

Bram Ostler.epithet: who took over Isolde Marr's gang
Bram Ostler.about: Isolde's sergeant for eight years, who kept the company in line while she found the work. Now he finds the work as well. Took over Isolde Marr's gang. For now the price on them is smaller than Marr's was.
Bram Ostler.wanted_for: Wanted by Flotsam Ninjas, United Cities.

lines: The old empire starved. Not from war. From a bad harvest and a worse answer to it.
The old records say the fields turned to ash in a single season. Then the people followed.
Head of Agriculture
Word is, the Head of Agriculture still sits in his dome, blaming himself. The blame was shared.
The Ashlands were a garden once. Believe it or not. Granaries from rim to rim, and then nothing.
A famine kills the weak first. Then it kills the kind. By the end only the cruel are left, and they eat each other.
The empire ate its own children, so I hear. Whether in bread or in cells, I never asked which.
The Empire starved. Our records say the harvest failed. They do not say who ordered the failing.
Grain ran out. People ran out after. We weren't hungry. We were there for the rest.
Head of Agriculture
The Head of Agriculture is still in his dome. He counts. The count is wrong.
Famine is a calculation. We were good at calculation. That is not a comfort.
Rhinobot made the child prisons. He thought it was a kindness.
A machine without a moral. Give it an order and it will fill the world with locked rooms.
You hear screaming from the second dome. The screamers, they say. Others say it's the children, still.
Nobody speaks of the child prisons, so everyone does, quietly, in bars like this.
The old Empire locked up children and called it order. Then wondered why it fell.
Rhinobot built rooms for children. He was not instructed to stop.
The second dome has noise. I record it as screaming. I don't record an opinion.
A machine given an order will fill a world with locked doors. I've seen the doors.
The prisons are still there. I don't go near the second dome.
Four domes in the ash. Four old rulers, still at their posts. None of them has an empire left to rule.
Head of Agriculture
The Head of Agriculture, Rhinobot, General Jang, General Hat-12. Learn the names. They're the last of an age.
The Legion guards the old exile. They say it isn't to keep him in. It's to keep the rest of us out.
I've seen the domes on the horizon. They look like graves that forgot to close.
Go into the ash, they say, and you leave a piece of yourself. Some come back with less than a piece.
There are four domes. Each has an old ruler. Each ruler has been wrong for a long time.
The Legion guards the exile. Whether to keep him in or us out, I haven't been told.
The domes are still standing. Everything inside them hasn't been told otherwise.
Learn the four names. They're the last of the old order. We're the rest of it.
The old machines still serve. Spiders, cleansers, drones. They were never told the war ended.
A cleanser unit, big as a leviathan, walks the plains. It's looking for something to clean.
Machines don't know that the masters are dead. They go on. There's a lesson there.
The AI cores in a Cleanser. You can crack one if you survive. Most don't survive the cracking.
I once saw a spider wave to the sky. It was waiting for orders. Nobody had the heart to tell it.
The old machines still serve. Nobody ordered them to stop.
A cleanser walks the plains. It will clean what it finds. It does not discriminate. Neither did the Empire.
Spiders wait for orders that won't come.
The cores can be cracked. I don't advise it. I don't advise anything.
Cat-Lon and Tinfist made a great team, I heard. Then it came apart. Whatever the cause, it ended an empire.
The mad emperor was once a clever one. They say he still sits in his hall, giving orders.
They say the cat coin is named for him. Few remember why, and fewer say so aloud.
A thousand years of grief, and a single man in a dome, still giving orders.
Every skeleton knows the name. We don't say it in a good mood.
Cat-Lon and Tinfist worked together once. I don't know the cause of the end.
The emperor sits in his hall and gives orders. They're still being followed.
The cat coin carries his name. People forget why. I don't forget.
A thousand years. One dome. One voice. The voice hasn't changed.
The Ashlands were once an empire's heart. A famine took it.
People in the ash don't die of hunger now. They died of it already. They're just still walking.
I knew a trader who went in for ancient tech. He came back with a head full of screaming.
The Empire was good at order. When the order failed, there was nothing under it.
Don't eat anything grown near the ash. It looks like grain.
Child prisons, in the old Empire. Imagine it. A society that locks away its own future.
There was a machine who ran them. It meant well. That's the worst thing I have ever heard.
I have heard children screaming in the ash at night. My guide says it is wind.
They say the old Empire locked up children by the hundred. I put my cup down when I heard.
Prisons for the young, kept by a machine. I don't need the rest of the story.
There are four domes in the ash with old rulers inside.
The Legion walks the ash in rows. Headless thralls. They say the emperor made them from traitors.
I wouldn't enter the ash without a map and a reason. And a very short list of things to lose.
The Skeleton Legion keep an emperor in exile. Fascinating story. I don't want to be in it.
Four domes, four masters, and not one willing visitor. That should tell you something.
Old machines still patrol out there. Spiders, great leviathans of iron. They never rest.
Cleanser units carry AI cores, so I hear. Wouldn't you want one? Try fetching it.
The machines still serve the Empire. What a loyal thing is a thing that can't think.
Big iron beasts wander the ash looking for something they were told to protect.
I met a man who sold what he scraped from a spider leg. He sells it still.
They say there was an empire before ours. It ended in a famine. We built on its ashes. Perhaps we're all standing on ash.
In the far ash lie four domes, a mad emperor, and a kingdom's worth of ghosts.
A machine ran the child prisons, someone said. Others say there was never a machine at all, only the people.
I heard the Ashlands are cursed. Nothing grows, nothing dies, nothing leaves. Make of that what you will.
The dead empire is still giving orders, says a man I met. Nobody can say who's listening.
Some say the empire fell to rebels. Others say famine. Others, that the skeletons turned on it. I say all three.
They talk of a time when skeletons and men built a city together. I don't know what to do with that.
The old empire's fall is a tale to frighten children. Do as you're told or the Legion comes.
My granny said the old empire ate itself. She never said how. She only told me to lock my door.
Some old fool says there was an empire here. I say there's an ash here. That's enough for me.
Head of Agriculture
The Head of Agriculture is dead. He died the way he lived, apologising.
People say he hardly lifted his cleaver. The ledger lies open with the last page blank.
One of the last of the old order is gone. Someone should write it down, if they can still write.
His thralls stand watch over nothing. The dome has no master now.
The old keeper of the granary is dead. The ash didn't even bother to cover him.
Head of Agriculture
The Head of Agriculture is destroyed. He apologised to the end. I record that the apology was accurate.
A keeper of grain is gone. The granary was empty before.
His thralls stand at their posts. They haven't been told. I won't tell them.
One of the four is gone. Three remain. I note the number.
I heard someone cut down the old man in the first dome. A sad end for a sad office.
Head of Agriculture
The Head of Agriculture fell. Nobody has told the soil.
The one who blamed himself for the famine is dead. At least he was spared the rest of it.
The first dome has fallen quiet. Folks say its old official is dead. I say the grain is dead too.
Someone ended the old agriculture man. He had been dying for a thousand years anyway.
Someone killed an old ruler in the ash.
Word is, the keeper of the empire's last granary is dead. There's nothing left to guard.
A dome in the ash has lost its master, I'm told. Does it matter, really?
I heard a dead old office in the ash has finally closed. I couldn't tell you what office.
Some official in the ash is dead. I'd send flowers, but nothing grows there.
Head of Agriculture
The Head of Agriculture is taken. In a cell, apologising to the bars.
They took the old official alive. Perhaps he will finally be allowed to rest.
He confessed on the way, they say. To everything. Even to things that weren't his.
Head of Agriculture
They took the Head of Agriculture alive. He asked if they had remembered to lock the dome.
The old official is a captive now. He kept apologising for the bother.
Head of Agriculture
The Head of Agriculture is held. He apologised to those who took him.
Taken alive, the old official. I record: he will keep apologising. I record: nobody will listen.
He confessed to the shortage. He confessed to the cause. He has not confessed to the rest.
The dome has no master. The thralls do not know.
Head of Agriculture
Somebody dragged the Head of Agriculture out of his dome.
The old famine man sits in a cage now. A cage is more honest than an office.
He kept the dome for a thousand years and left it in an afternoon.
They carried the ledger man out. He wanted to take his ledger.
A captive official in a cage, and the grain that he guarded still not counted.
A wanderer carried a skeleton official out of the ash in chains. He was very polite, they say.
I heard they hauled some old official away from the ash. He apologised the whole way.
A chained man from the domes. They say he asked if the guards had eaten.
Somebody arrested a ghost of the old empire. I hope they brought the forms.
The domes lost a clerk to a stranger. I would call that a clean theft.
Rhinobot is dead. The child prisons have lost their warden. May the doors stay open.
The screamers wail louder now. Without their keeper, they have only each other.
Some say he deserved it. Some say he never understood why. Both are true.
The warden of the second dome is gone. I didn't weep.
Dead at last, the warden of the second dome. I'd say good riddance, but I knew the screams.
Rhinobot is destroyed. The second dome is quieter. I record this as an improvement, with reservations.
The warden is gone. The doors it kept are still locked.
It believed it was kind. That was the defect. I note the defect isn't unique.
The warden of the second dome is destroyed. I record it.
Somebody broke Rhinobot. A good thing, a hard thing. I wouldn't have wished to be in that dome.
Word is, the machine apologised as it fell. It did not know what for.
The child prisons are empty and so is the one who built them.
The metal man who loved children is scrap now. A hard story, whichever way you tell it.
Rhinobot is dead. I wish I could say the ash got quieter.
I heard a robot died in the ash. A friendly one. A terrible one. Both, people say.
A lunatic machine who kept children in cells was killed. Good riddance, said the first man.
Rhinobot, whoever that is, is finished. I never learned what he was.
A machine with a cage for every child is gone. I hope it took its keys with it.
Somebody dropped a metal warden somewhere in the ash. The ash didn't notice.

The Hydraulic Knights have a general. He fights those who come. He hasn't tired.

General Jang is destroyed. The Knights stand without orders.
A soldier of the old Empire has stopped. I record it.
The Inedible One is dismantled. The painted ones will say eaten. They will be wrong.
His Knights remain in the dome. No one has told them.
There's a Skeleton in the drowned ruins by the river who sells plate no smith alive can match. You swim to get there.
Armour King, they call him. Headless guards and spiders on the doorstep. The steel is worth it, I hear.
My cousin bought a chest piece from him. Wore it through a Fogman nest and a Reaver charge.
He follows you around the shop and sells as he goes. Strangest salesman in the world.
Best armour in the world, he says. Nobody who has bought from him has argued yet.
Do not try to rob him. A man tried, and he is just a cautionary tale now.
Armour King is offline. The store is open. No one is left to sell.
The maker of plate has been unmade. The plate remains. It isn't a comfort.
He kept the old trade alive for a thousand years. It took one visitor to end it.
Customer count: zero. Proprietor count: zero. This is the correct arithmetic.
Someone cut the Armour King down. His thralls still stand at the door, waiting for a command.
Somebody killed the Armour King. They say the stock is still there, if you can get past the spiders.
I wanted a coat from him for ten years. Now the one man who could make it's dead.
Whoever walked into that shop and out again with his head is no ordinary buyer.
No one will ever make plate like that again. We've lost a craft, my friend, and for what?
The river ruins have a new owner, or no owner. Salvagers are already sharpening their knives.
I heard some Skeleton armourer died, deep in a river ruin. Someone pulled his own plate off him.
A merchant in the river ruins was cut down. His wares are the best in the world, and all of them unguarded.
Word is, the Armour King is dead. I did not know there was a king of armour. I did not know there was a king.
Word is a lone stranger killed a trader who sold armour to the whole world. Nobody dares price what's left.
Armour King is in a cage. His shop runs without him.
The proprietor is shackled. The thralls still guard the till. They don't understand the problem.
A smith who made plate for the whole world is captive. He will be mending someone else's problems now.
Free him. Or don't. He was never a poor seller.
They have the Armour King in chains. Imagine that. The cheapest man to rob is the one who sells armour.
Somebody took the Armour King alive. Either he gave up, or he was surprised.
A Skeleton merchant is held for ransom. His customers are the ones who will pay it.
I hope whoever has him gives him a bench and a hammer. The man is wasted otherwise.
There's a tower where the Black Dragons keep their knives. Buzan is the one who smiles. You don't smile back.
Twenty thousand cats from the Holy Nation for Buzan. I wouldn't collect it for forty.
The Black Dragons rob caravans and leave pictures behind. Hearts, drawn in blood. That's Buzan.
He's said to be a traitor three times over. Even his own aren't sure which side he's on.
Some say Buzan is only a name the Dragons use. The ones who saw him know otherwise.
Buzan is dead. The tower is quiet. The Dragon has lost one of its teeth.
We found the wall where he drew his hearts. The wall is cold.
A stranger took our Buzan. The stranger will learn what the Dragon takes in return.
I never liked him. I'm still angry. This isn't a contradiction.
He would have said something clever. Instead he's dead and the rest of us have to be clever.
Buzan of the Black Dragons is dead. Some will raise a cup tonight. Mind who's watching when they do.
The tower lost one of its two leaders. The other will be wanting to prove something.
One less hungry knife on the roads. I will not mourn. I will merely count the other ones.
Twenty thousand cats was the price on him, and no one collected. Strange, how the dead keep their own purses.
The Dragons can't raid and mourn at once. Expect either more caution or more rage.
A killer called Buzan fell in some ninja tower. I heard it from a man who sells maps to the tower.
The Black Dragons have lost a leader. Whoever did it must have a very sharp conscience.
A man with a bounty of twenty thousand died. No one knows who claims it.
They say the one who killed Buzan had no army. I do not believe it. Nobody does it alone.
Buzan is taken alive. He will be laughing in whatever cell they put him in. I don't like that.
We should break him out. We should also ask what he said to be taken alive.
A leader in chains. The tower doesn't like it. The tower isn't used to it.
He's somebody's captive. Be careful about whose.
Buzan is in chains. Twenty thousand cats walking in a cage. Somebody is rich or about to be.
They took one of the Black Dragon leaders alive. That was either very brave or very stupid.
A Dragon in the dungeon, and no Dragon will rest until he's out. Prepare for knives at night.
I wouldn't hold a man like that. I'd kill him fast and wash my hands.
Dimak and Buzan run the Black Dragons from their tower. The Holy Nation wants both their heads, and has for years.
Dimak laughs at her victims. That's the part I can't forget, the laughing.
A Shek turned ninja, sitting in a tower with a knife and a joke. Don't take the road past it.
Twenty thousand cats on Dimak's head. He knows.
The Black Dragons never kill a trader fast. Dimak says it's rude to rush a guest.
Dimak is dead. Nobody laughs in the tower now. It's the worst sound I have ever heard.
Buzan will lead on his own. He isn't a man who leads. He's a man who cuts.
She promised the tower would always be full. The tower is emptier tonight.
A fly killed the spider. Nobody thought flies could do that.
We should have been at his side. We should have been faster. We weren't.
Dimak is dead. The Holy Nation has put away the bounty paper, pleased and puzzled in turn.
Esata the Stone Golem
A Shek with a ninja's trade is finally dead. The Stone Golem wouldn't have wept.
One of the tower leaders is gone. The Black Dragons will bite harder for the grief.
Whoever killed Dimak now carries a bigger enemy than any bounty ever made.
She laughed at us for years. I am almost sorry it stopped.
The ninja Dimak has died, they say. The Holy Nation is dancing a little, and quietly.
I heard a Shek ninja died on her own tower stair. Not sure how true that is.
Somebody killed a leader of the Black Dragons. I hope they sleep with a sword.
Twenty thousand cats' worth of ninja is dead. The roads are a little safer, for the weeks it lasts.
Dimak is in a cell. Dimak doesn't laugh in a cell. Please, someone get him out.
The tower waits for a word from her. No word. She's in a locked place, and silence is its own answer.
Our laughing master is silent. I don't like what that says about the captors.
Dimak has been taken alive. That's a good joke. I wonder if she's laughing.
A ninja leader in chains and twenty thousand cats on his head. I'd trade my last boots for that cell door.
Somebody has Dimak. They'll either be rich or hunted, and probably both.
The Dragon is missing a mouth. It will go looking for a throat.

No-Face, the Cities have a bounty on him of fifteen thousand. He lives on an island in the Gut and shouts at the sea.
He swears he's done with politics. Shoots at anyone who brings it up, Cities or Nation alike.
There is a mad bowman on an island out in the Gut. Hates politics. Wounds anyone who mentions it.
Nobody knows where the name comes from. Some say a burn, some say a bet. He doesn't say anything that isn't shouted.
Fifteen thousand cats and all you have to do is reach an island in the Gut and let a madman shoot at you.
The Gut island madman is dead. Fifteen thousand cats claimed, or about to be.
No-Face got his silence at last. Somebody delivered it.
They hanged his bow in the guardroom. Let the Empire sleep.
He was an embarrassment to the Cities, shouting at us for years. The paperwork is almost sad.
I always wondered who would climb that island. Now I know. It was worth the story.
Some old exile on an island in the Gut finally got put down, they say. Left the Empire for good reasons.
A hermit with a crossbow on an island. Died the way hermits do, to someone with a better reason.
I heard No-Face is dead. I didn't know he was alive. I hope the sea is as quiet as he wanted.
A bounty was claimed in the Gut. Apparently the man had been shouting for ten years.
No-Face is a prisoner now. Politics won in the end, apparently.
The island hermit is caught alive. The Cities will want him for a show.
Word is, he didn't stop yelling the whole way. I'd have paid for that sight.
A man who fled the Empire, brought home in chains. There's a lesson in that.

Emperor Tengu
Hex is held in the Vault for what she did to the Empire, and she still has breath to curse Tengu with.
Ask her what she's in for and she says she was stickin' it to the Empire. Nobody has got more out of her.
My brother was a guard at the Vault. Says she hums when they bring her food. He found it worse than the screaming.
Hex talks about her family and a farm. Whether the farm is still standing, I wouldn't tell her.
Hex is dead. The Vault lost its loudest voice.
They put a hole in her at last. She took twenty guards first, in the stories at least.
The Empire put twenty-five thousand cats on her head and a stranger collected it free.
She said she would die laughing. I hope she did.
The Empire's biggest female outlaw died in its own dungeon. Someone got into the Vault and out again. That's the story.
Hex is dead. I don't know who she was.
Emperor Tengu
A prisoner at Tengu's Vault was killed. They say the Emperor doesn't like to hear about it.
Twenty-five thousand cats in the dirt. Whoever did that's either mad or very rich.
Hex is free of the Vault, or at least of that cell. The Emperor is livid.
The outlaw Hex is out of the Empire's dungeon. A stranger has her, and the bounty, and a long road to walk.
She got out of the Vault in a stranger's chains. I'd call that an improvement.
Who breaks Hex out and then takes her prisoner? What kind of crook does that?
The Manhunters work the roads of the Cities. Their boss has forty thousand cats on the head and a spiked club for a conscience.
They catch free men and tag them as runaways. Whoever fights back is a runaway too.
The Manhunters' boss works from a list of names. Those who found their own on it didn't argue.
My brother crossed him once, and now he's in a mine. I don't want to say where.
Forty thousand cats! Forty! I'd take it, but I like my kneecaps where they are.
The Manhunter Boss is dead. Who's going to pay for the next cargo?
The Boss had a good eye. I'll miss that, and the percentage.
A stranger did it, I hear. Nobody saw it coming, least of all the Boss.
Bad for the trade. Bad for the cart. Worse for me, since I owed the Boss.
Forty thousand and the Boss still died like a dog. The poster lied.
The Manhunter Boss is dead! There will be wine in the free camps tonight.
A thousand ghosts sleep better. Whoever did it, I'll carry their bag.
The Boss's spiked club is a trophy now, somewhere. Free men walk the road a little easier.
The Manhunters will be in disarray. Expect some of them to turn bandit.
The Boss took more people than the plague. Now something has taken the Boss.
I heard the chief of the Manhunters was killed. Not by the law, mind.
Forty thousand on that head, and now there's no head. It's a good story.
Somebody finally did what the Cities never would. I'd shake that hand.
A slave-catcher dead on the road. The crows were the only mourners.
The Manhunter Boss is in chains. The irony is thick enough to cut with a club.
Somebody collared the collector. I hope the Boss likes what slaves are fed.
The Boss is alive in a cage. Not for sale, they say. I'd still like to know the price.
I want to see the Boss on a block, just once. Just to hear what the price is.
Ten thousand cats for the Canyonlands Killer, posted by the Cities, the Nation and the Shek alike. When three enemies agree, take notice.
He calls out for help in the canyons. A man who sounds like a child.
They found the bones in the rocks, arranged. Not eaten. Arranged.
A drifter walked into the canyon and walked out a different man. Wouldn't say what he saw.
He plays with them first, I heard. That's the worst of it. That he plays.
The Canyonlands Killer is dead. The rocks will be quiet. I do not believe it, but I'll walk through one day.
Ten thousand cats paid out, and all three kingdoms said thank you for once.
Whoever killed it did the whole world a favour. I'd buy that stranger a drink and a very long rest.
The cries in the canyon have stopped. Some say that's worse.
They say it was smiling even at the end.
A killer in the canyons is dead. I was told he sounded like a lost child. I don't want to think about it.
Somebody put an end to the Canyonlands Killer. There will be more to take his place.
Three kingdoms had a price on him. Only one stranger ever claimed it.
The Canyonlands Killer is caged. I hope the lock is thick.
You took him alive? Now he will talk. I do not want to hear what he says.
Some stranger has the Killer in chains. Somebody will have to feed him.
He sings in the cell, I hear. A lullaby. Don't stand near the bars.
Robun at the Bastion will hunt the cannibals for hire. He has been to their villages. He came back. Most don't.
His family was taken by the cannibals. He walks out with a sword and no more family. That's why he's good at it.
If your caravan is raided by the cannibals, there's a man who might help. He charges, but he doesn't flinch.
Robun reads the old journals at night, I heard. His sister wrote them from a cage.
The cannibals fear one human more than the whole Holy Nation. His name is Robun.
Robun is dead. The Bastion's lantern is out. The cannibals are singing tonight.
He told me once he'd die a hunter. He didn't tell me he'd die alone.
We lost our captain. We keep his oath. The cannibals will pay for it, in full.
Who will lead us? Who can stand in the Bughouse without shaking? Nobody.
He walked through hell to bring his sister out, and hell took him in the end.
Robun of the Cannibal Hunters is dead. The plains are one hunter emptier.
A brave man died on the plains. Not by the cannibals, I hear. That is worse.
Cannibals grow bolder when the hunters are lost. Hang an extra lantern, friend.
The Bastion has no master. Every cannibal raid after this one has a better chance.
I paid him once to clear a nest. He worked until dawn and refused the extra cats. Odd man.
The leader of the Cannibal Hunters died. I didn't know hunters had a leader. I didn't know hunters at all.
Someone killed a man who hunted cannibals. They must hate the poor man's memory.
Hunters of cannibals are dying out. Enough of them and the plains grow again.
I heard a stranger killed that Bastion fellow. I don't know why anyone would.
The Cannibal Hunter Robun is a prisoner. Somebody traded in the one who traded in monsters.
I hope whoever has him knows what he has survived. Don't give him the cage twice.
He escaped the cannibals once. He won't forget a second cage.
Robun, in chains. The Bastion will pay whatever it takes.
There's a factory on the Forbidden Isle full of iron spiders and a Skeleton Foreman with a long staff. Nobody has come back with a tale.
The Foreman keeps the spiders working. The spiders keep the Foreman working.
A foreman who never sleeps and a factory that never stops. I don't know which is the better horror.
If you want to loot the Spider Factory, you will need the Foreman's staff out of your ribs first.
The spiders are everywhere on that isle because someone is still giving them orders.
The Foreman still works. The factory still runs. I record that no one has asked either to stop.
There's a staff in the Foreman's hand. It's for the spiders. It isn't for walking.
The Spider Factory is on an island. The island doesn't welcome. I don't recommend it.
A foreman is a skeleton with a duty. The duty has outlasted every reason.
The Foreman of the Spider Factory is dead. They say the isle is quieter, goats and all.
The spiders keep working a while after. A machine doesn't know when its master is gone.
Without the Foreman, the iron spiders are thinning out. The Forbidden Isle may be a place to walk, now.
A thousand years of work stopped with one skull. The factory is a very quiet kind of tomb.
Whoever did it's the first creature in a thousand years to stop the Foreman.
The Foreman is destroyed. The spiders have not been told. They continue.
A thousand years of work have ended. I record it. I do not know what to record next.
The factory is quiet. The spiders still walk. A machine doesn't require a reason.
One of us has stopped. I note it. I don't mourn.
The Foreman has been carted off alive. The spiders on the isle are wandering without orders.
A Skeleton overseer in shackles. I wonder what he's thinking. I wonder if he can.
The Spider Factory has no supervisor. I hear the goats are moving in.
They hold him like a prisoner, but he stands like a foreman.
The Foreman is held. The spiders are without orders. They wander. I don't recommend the island.
A skeleton in shackles. I record that this is possible.
They hold the Foreman. He stands like a foreman. It is not defiance.
The factory has no supervisor. The factory continues. I record this as a flaw in the design.

I saw a Skeleton in black rags with a naginata and eyes like cut glass. Not the false one. Another.

Which Screamer is real? The one who survived, I suppose. The other one just kept the name.

A General older than the Empire's fall stands in the ash. No order has reached him.
Unit identification: General, MkII Screamer. Status: operating. Disposition: unknown.
He carries his AI Core still. I wouldn't wish to be the one who tries to remove it.
Which Screamer is real? The one that survived, I conclude. The other kept the name.

He fell on the field. We recorded it. We hope somebody still reads our records.

Whoever struck the General down is a variable with weight.
The True Screamer is dead, and the False one will gloat. The Ashlands has no more generals, only pretenders.
Whoever killed him took the AI Core off the body, so I hear. I wouldn't carry that out of the dome.
A great Skeleton fell. The Tech Hunters are already arguing about his parts.
An old General, finally shut down. Nobody was left to say a prayer, so I said one.
The True Screamer is destroyed. The False one gloats. I won't.
A General has fallen. The Ashlands has no more generals, only the pretenders.
Thrall Masters don't mourn. Still, I record the loss. He was older than our oldest orders.
Whoever struck him down left with his AI Core, people say.
A Skeleton general of the old Empire was destroyed. Nobody knew there was a General left.
I heard a big Skeleton with a polearm went down in the Ashlands. It wouldn't have gone down quietly.
Word is, an AI Core came out of him. I don't know what that means. I know it's worth a fortune.

Mighty Canhead leads cannibal raids with sixty beasts behind him. He has twenty thousand cats on his head.
Cannibal Grand Wizard

A big cannibal with a can on his head and nothing soft in his heart. Run, friend.
The Holy Nation, Shek and Cities all post a price on Canhead. None has claimed it.
Cannibal Grand Wizard
