A drifter at the gate asked if it is safe. I said safer than the Plains. He laughed.
The Bell-man. The Table-master. The Salt Mother. The Quiet Cook. Four names we do not say at supper.
Hush left a name behind. Chief's knife. We do not say it. Nobody else does either.
Kin out there say we are traitors. Maybe. Traitors to the pot.
There is a fifth name we do not say. The Chief. Hush says his name is the knife.
They still hold the Gateway up like a lantern in the Kingdom. A fine lantern. I never found a use for it.
Kral died to a hundred swords. I don't call it foolish. I say a hundred is a lot.
A Shek doesn't run. A Shek who runs far enough stops being called one.
Esata the Stone Golem
The Stone Golem holds the Kingdom together. The rest of us hold what we can carry.
Cut me, curse me, cast me out. The sand doesn't care what a man was called.
A /FLATSKIN/ laughed at Kral in a bar once. I broke his jaw. I haven't worked out why.
Say what you like of the Gateway. Say it somewhere I can't hear.
I mock the Kingdom. You don't.
Outsiders don't get to sneer at Kral. Only the ones he failed.
Someone said Shek honour was a trick to make us die cheap. I said nothing. That was the worst of it.
Exile teaches you the price of everything. Water, shade, a quiet seat. Honour was cheap by comparison.
I drink with bandits and mercenaries. They ask no questions.
Some men leave the Kingdom. Some are left by it. I try not to ask which.
A man with no home still has a blade. Mine is hired by the day.
There are worse things than being cast out. Being cast out and wishing to go back.
The zealots say trade is cowardice. They also eat what trade brings. Make of that what you will.
Esata the Stone Golem
The Stone Golem holds, Bayan counts. Between them the Kingdom lives. I drink to the counting.
I've buried more brothers than I have bought drinks. I mean to fix that ratio.
Fewer warriors every year. They tell us it's a purer kind of strength. I tell them to count.
A /FLATSKIN/ pays double at our gates and thinks himself robbed. I think the Kingdom eats.
Some call Bayan a coward. Bayan lived. Shager didn't.
Say it quietly: a living Kingdom is a better monument than a dead one.
Children. That's the war the Kingdom is losing, and it's the one I'd fight.
I'll die when the time comes. I'd rather it came late and meant something.
Glorious death. I've said it so often it's a sound, like a door.
The old ones weep at the Gateway. I wonder who they're weeping for.
Quiet night. ... Good. I could use a quiet night. No, I mean, I'm ready to fight.
A man can believe and be tired. The first is a duty. The second is a fact.
They drink to the dead. I drink to the living. Not out loud, mind.
Ask a Shek if he fears the Gateway and he will laugh.
I'd die for the Kingdom. I'd simply rather it asked less often.
Hundredfold odds. We love the phrase.
Kral's last stand is a fine tale. Tales are a poor shield.
The warm ones drink to forget. I tried. I forgot the hum for an hour. I don't recommend it.
I counted the days. Eleven, then forty, then I stopped. Then I started again.
The hive doesn't take a ronin back. That isn't a rumour.
Someone said ronin are pieces the hive no longer needs. I asked what we were instead. No one knew.
I heard I. They say it so easily. I practise in the dark.
I want a window. I don't know why. It's the first thing I have wanted that I could name.
Cold water. Warm bread. Small wants. I collect them.
Nobody tells you what to do with a self. I am doing it wrong.
Some nights I'm afraid I'll wake and say we. Some nights I'm afraid I won't.
A no-hive wanted one thing and bought another. We watched for an hour. We learned nothing.
The hive is warm. The hive is whole. This one sometimes wonders what a hole would feel like.
Why do the no-hives drink? This one tried. It was sour.
Fair price, fair weight. ... Why do the no-hives mind the price so much? We mind nothing. It's peaceful.
The warm ones lie to one another, and are lied to, and call it company.
I don't reset. Others do. I envy them some days. Most days I don't.
Don't tell the others that I remember. They would be afraid. Or they would be jealous.
A human fed me oil once. I haven't been fed since. I haven't forgotten who.
Memory isn't a gift. It's a weight with a name. I have many names.
The old days aren't gone for me. They're in the next room. I don't open that door often.
My family is well, thank the Lord. All of it. Don't ask which of it.
They say road bandits were honest once. A road is a long thing.
I lit a candle for one who isn't at the table. The priest asked who. I said, everyone.
The wastes took someone from me. Not death. Something worse that looks like freedom.
Never speak an outlaw's name in the temple. I find it helps to speak it in my head.
Outlaws, outlaws. As if they sprouted from the sand. Every one of them had a mother who sang to them.
A pilgrim gave me news of the bandits. I paid for the news twice. I didn't say why.
The priests say the road is cursed. They've never walked it hungry.
I'd trade my pew for one hour on the road with someone I won't name.
They burned a man last year for a few pages. I wonder what was in them.
Scripture is a long road. Some of us stopped at the first milestone.
A priest told me the forbidden writings are lies. I asked how he knew. He said he had read them.
I keep my questions where the Rebirth school can't find them.
If Okran wished to be understood, He would be simpler.
Somebody wrote that the horned devil bleeds as we do. They put him to the flame. The words weren't wrong, only unwelcome.
The old books were many. We are given few. I ask who chose them and no one answers, but I am glad I asked.
A true believer fears nothing written. I notice how afraid we're of pages.
I dreamed I read a book of kindness. I woke and was afraid. Not of the book.
Nothing good is built on chains. I own a lot of nothing good.
A merchant's conscience is like a ledger: you can't audit it without finding something.
I gave a runaway a coin. A silver one. I've been rich for years and that's the coin I remember.
Slave markets pay well. I'd like it to stop paying so I could stop being paid.
Careful what you say about the anti-slavers. I won't join in. I have simply stopped laughing.
The harvest is fine this year. Nobody remembers the other one. I like it that way. I hate that I like it.
The Guild didn't come. Everyone knows. Nobody says.
I hear some of the ones taken after the rebellion are still sold. Quietly. It's called a debt.
The word is dregs. I stopped saying it years back. My tongue still tastes it.
I had a friend who ran with the rebels. I think about the hour I was too afraid to join.
Big Grim
Raise a cup to Big Grim. Go on. ... I drink to the dead.
Hash made rules and meant them. The swamp misses that, though it won't say.
My cousin ran with the Stalkers. Now she runs with the hounds.
Funny how a clan can be guilty and blamed in the same breath.
Big Grim
Grim reads slow. Remembers fast. I've learned to forget in her favour.
Funny thing, being blamed. After a while you start to wonder if it was you.
Some clans get monuments. Some get a story in somebody else's mouth.
There's still a few of us. Not many. We learned to be quiet and that nobody listens to quiet.
Who benefits, I always say. Then I shut up. It's the swamp. Saying it gets you a club.
A name on a coat, a name in a ledger. Same thing, depending who's holding the pen.
Blades stay sheathed, tabs get paid, and I didn't see who left by the back door.
Sit anywhere that isn't behind the counter. Behind the counter is where mistakes get buried.
Rum is rum. If it tastes of something else, that's the cup's fault and the cup's business.
Quiet night. I like quiet. Quiet means nobody is bleeding on the floorboards.
The ruins are a fine landlord. No rent, no questions, and the roof never gets fixed.
Ask me who drinks here and I say everyone. Ask me who pays and I say most.
A drunk will tell you anything. A sober man will tell you the same thing for a price. I just pour.
Everybody passes through the Hub eventually. That's why nobody wanted to keep it.
I hear the Holy Nation wants the walls back. Funny. They aren't the ones sweeping them.
Three coats on the peg and one of them is not coming back. I will sell it by morning.
There are shadows in this town that were here before the bar. They tip well, so I don't ask.
Lately the road brings more outlanders than customers. Outlanders look at the menu and leave.
Two thousand a day to guard your skin. Not a cat less, and I won't smile for it either.
Hired a squad to walk me to Stack once. They walked me. That's all the contract said.
Guild rules: you pay, we fight, we don't ask what was in the crate. Mostly we don't ask.
The work dries up when the war goes quiet. Then I miss the war. Strange thing to say.
Every employer says it will be an easy job. I have a scar for each time that was true.
Contracts are simple. Dying is simpler. I keep my contracts short.
Dust Bandits on the north road, starvers on the east. Pick which one you would rather lose to.
I counted four caravans this month. Three arrived. Ask the fourth how the guards were.
The Border Zone eats more boots than blades. Walk it in good boots or don't walk it.
Squad of Shek crossed the plain last week. Left the traders alone. I don't trust a quiet Shek.
That tower at the edge of the Hub takes a cut from anything that passes. Pay it or go around.
We turned down a job to escort a cart to Squin. The man would not say what was under the tarp.
I keep the peace for a fee. The peace is cheap. It's the people who cost.
Everybody comes to the Hounds when they have burned something. Few come back to say thanks.
Hash goes north, cats come south. I like how that sounds. It isn't always how it goes.
People think I'm soft because I make deals. A deal is just a fight you win with your mouth.
Sit down, have a cup. If you're here to be forgiven, you can start with the tab.
Big Grim
Big Grim built the Hounds out of swamp mud. The rest of us just carry the goods. Don't tell the Ninjas.
Walked from the Skinner's Roam on these. Feel them. No, don't feel them.
I've been looking for work since the last war. Wars end.
Left one pair of boots in a bandit's stomach.
I can fix a roof, shoe a bull, and count to a thousand. Nobody here needs any of it.
My feet hurt in places feet shouldn't have. Anyone know a surgeon who works for stew?
Slept in a ditch with a goat last night. The goat complained about me, not the other way.
A man told me the Holy Nation has fallen. Another told me it's bigger than ever.
People say the cannibals have a capital now. A real one, with a throne. I laughed.
I heard the Empire is run by one man who never leaves a tower. Sounds dull.
The Shek sacked this place once. You can still tell. The ruins have a certain look of being sorry.
Somebody swears there's a town of nothing but skeletons in the black sands. Somebody drinks a lot.
I walked past a hive village once. They didn't hurt me. They didn't look at me either.
Ah, the cannibals, you know, they don't even chew. They swallow! I saw it! Well. Heard it.
I had fifty cats on me when I came in. Now I have a very good feeling about everything.
Bugmaster
Bugmaster, right? Big one. Bigger than this bar. Probably. I was drunk, so no, not drunk then.
Blood Bandits ate my brother. Or married him. One of those. They had the same teeth, anyway.
Another round for the man who's going to stop talking right after this sentence.
I could take any one of you. Not today, I have a knee.
Last week a man asked me to step outside. I did. He didn't. We're both still here.
Break a table in this place and the Ninjas break your arm. I've seen the arm.
Nobody starts fights in here. They just wait for someone to finish theirs.
I once lost a fight to a stool. In my defence, the stool had help.
Whoever took my cup, I forgive you. Return it by noon and I forgive you more.
I don't hate anyone here. That's the secret. I'm too tired to hate anyone here.
Cactus rum is up again. Every time somebody shoots at a caravan it goes up a few cats.
Fuel is cheap in Stack and dear here. Guess who carries the difference.
A foodcube sells for less than the water you drink with it.
Iron plates go for three times what they cost where they're made. Nothing grows in the Zone but prices.
Never trust a stall that has no prices on it. That's where they decide what you're worth.
My margin is thin enough to cut yourself on. I have the scars to prove it.
I take the long way round every time now. Short roads have too many people waiting on them.
Lost a pack animal to a river raptor and a good mood to its owner. Both were the same afternoon.
Three weeks from Heng with a cart of spices and a head of lice. I'm a rich man in one of those.
The Shek will trade now, did you hear? They still don't smile when they count.
A guard asked to inspect my cart. I told him what was in it. He let me through.
Don't buy bread from a man who says it's fresh. Buy it from a man who's hungry.
Spent a month digging a ruin. It had one working lamp and a very rude spider.
The old machines aren't dead. They're sulking. There's a difference, and it's expensive.
Hand me any wire, any plate, any scrap with a number on it. I'll tell you what it used to be.
I dream of sealed doors. Always a sealed door and a tool I forgot to pack.
A Holy Nation man tried to buy my notes. For burning. I said the price was a lot of cats.
Everyone treats us like grave robbers. We're archivists with bad habits and worse luck.
I don't drink. I sit near those who do. It's the closest I come to a hobby.
The stool is the wrong shape for me. The stool and I have an understanding.
Somebody told me this place was once a fort. Somebody was wrong, or I forgot the wall.
I count the rivets in the ceiling. Three hundred and eleven. Yesterday it was three hundred and ten.
They stare. I let them. It's an old habit of mine, being stared at.
Humans say they're tired. I wonder what it's like to run down slowly.
A pile of scrap in the corner was once a man. Not much difference from the pile I keep in my bag.
I was told to find a repair table. I found a stool and some very polite thieves.
The Holy Nation burns what it doesn't understand. I'm what it doesn't understand.
Fresh grease would be welcome. A rumour would be welcome too.
I remember a hallway. I don't remember where it went. This bar isn't the hallway.
My joints sing in the rain. I thought for years it was the wind.
The warm things talk very fast here. The hive listens. It doesn't always understand.
Food is in the cup. Food is also in the cup next to it. The cups are the same.
This one is far from the hum. The hum is a good sound. The hum has no prices.
No-hives drink to forget a thing. The hive forgets without cups.
A man tried to touch this one's shell. The hive remembers hands.
Many chairs. Few of them fit. The hive stands. The hive is polite about it.
Flatskins serve rum in tin cups. A Shek would be insulted, if a Shek drank here.
I came for the trade. I stay for the quiet. Don't make the quiet shorter.
My father burned this town. I wonder if he sat in this chair first.
The old truces are thin, and my patience is thinner. Count that before you stare at my horns.
Stack sells me blades, and the Border Zone sells me poor excuses.
A Shek can sit among flatskins for one cup. A second is a challenge to the first.
Blessed... evening. Sorry. Good evening. I mean, evening. It's a very normal evening.
I'm just a farmer. Of stones. From, ah, a village. Near. Please don't ask which.
No, I have never held a Flame. Why would I ask what it weighs? Don't write that down.
A fine place. A sinner's place. Not that I think so. I think it's wonderful.
I came for the water. The water isn't holy. I checked.
Don't look at my hands. They aren't praying. They're just resting in a prayerful position.
If you lean a little to the left, you hear the Shek at the far table. I don't lean. I merely tilt.
Holy Lord Phoenix
Somebody said Phoenix, and half the room went quiet. That is the sort of thing one remembers.
I count the swords at each table. It's a harmless hobby. Don't tell anyone I counted.
A cup of anything, please. Nothing that makes me say what I think.
The bartender is a Ninja, a thief, or both. I'm only saying what everyone else is thinking.
I am here for the Flame and the cheap rum. One of those is a lie.
Spare a bite. One bite. I won't even chew loud.
I haven't eaten since the dust storm. The dust storm was last week.
Anyone leaving crumbs? I am a very patient floor.
I used to rob caravans. Now I rob my own pockets. They are empty. It stings.
Foodcube, fish bone, anything. I'm not proud.
My friend isn't asleep. He's just very hungry. Try him in the morning.
The Anti-Slavers would string us up if they caught us. Not that I sell anyone. I sell...
Don't look at the door. Everyone who looks at the door gets looked at.
I used to love this work. Now I check my shadow twice before I sit.
Anti-Slavers burned a camp last month. The papers are still blowing around in the sand.
I sleep in my armour. Cold, uncomfortable, but nobody has ever stabbed armour in its sleep.
Everybody loves freedom, right up until the food runs out.
Three hundred cats for a man's whole life. That's the price. Think on it over your cup.
I notice who pays for what. I notice who doesn't look away. The second list is shorter.
A collar leaves a pale ring for a year.
Not every chain is iron. Some are debts. Those are harder to cut.
Don't tell me your business. I'm just here for the rum and the exits.
I eat slowly, I sit near the wall, and I tip well. That's my entire plan.
Everything has a second owner. I just meet the third one. Cheaper that way, for them.
The tower has a good view of the road. The road has a good view of nothing.
People ask me for a discount. I give them a lesson in what that word costs.
Guards pretend to crack down. A few cats keep the pretence honest.
Don't carry anything shiny through a thief's town. It's rude to the locals.
I do not steal. I redistribute attention. The goods follow.
A bull outlives a bad road. The bull has told me this. Slowly.
Town folk sleep with walls and still lock the door. Walls are for those who forgot the sky.
Camp is a fire, a pot, and a rule: nobody steals the pot.
The wind changes at the old fort. I always say hello to it.
I trade goat milk for tools, tools for stories, stories for goat milk. A good circle.
Do not call me a beggar. I carry more than you do, I just carry it in my head.
They took my plot and my plough and left me the ground. The ground isn't worth much without them.
Bread is two days old. I'm three. The difference is clear to everyone but the baker.
The Empire taxes the harvest and the hunger both. Somehow the hunger pays better.
I'd plant here, if the ruins didn't keep falling on the rows.
A man with a hoe is a threat if he's angry enough. That's what the tax collector learned.
Plant when the rain allows, bury when the raiders do. A good cycle, if you don't mix them up.
Every wound is a story, and most of them end the same.
A splint and a stern word fix most things. The rest, I charge extra.
A man came in with a bolt in his thigh and asked if it would scar. It did. He lived.
People think I'm kind. I'm thrifty. A man who lives pays twice.
I stitched three Shek last week. They didn't wince.
Wash your hands. Nobody ever does. That's how I make my living.
Nobody in the Hub calls for the law.
I am off duty. That means I am armed in a bar. Do not read anything into it.
Station is three days north. The criminals know.
A cop in a lawless town has two jobs. Stay alive. Keep his tunic clean.
I drink alone and I drink slow. I watch the room. It isn't a habit, it's a diagnosis.
Bounties are good money here, if you can collect before somebody collects you.
The stew has bones in it. I asked what animal. The cook said, an animal.
Bread here's hard enough to build with.
Somebody left a fish on the counter two days ago. It's still there.
I ordered the special. They said the special was a warning, not a dish.
The rum is clean. The cup is not. Some choices are just that: choices.
Meat of the day, they said. The day wasn't specified.
My feet are two different sizes now. I'd complain, but they can't hear me anymore.
Rested one night in the ruins and a roof beam kept me company. A fine and frightening thing.
Four days on foot and I'm hungry for a chair more than a meal.
I bought boots in Stack. The sole is already apologising.
Never walk in new boots. I walked in new boots. I'll tell you how that ended if I can stand.
Walk enough in the Zone and you stop noticing the pain. You start noticing your knees instead.
I was robbed on the east road. Politely, too. He said please. Then he took the boots.
Lost my pack, my bull, and my afternoon. The afternoon was the one I missed most.
Some bandit stole a man's trousers last week. Not the cart. Not the purse. Trousers.
Caravan three days out is missing. Everyone says it will be fine.
I'm not saying the guard sold us out. I'm saying he's wearing a very nice belt.
They left me one boot. One. I walked here in the other's silence.
Dust blew in the whole night. I swept it out. In the morning it was back, with friends.
Smells like acid rain. You can tell by the way the old men start counting their fingers.
The wind in this place has opinions. Right now it has the opinion that I should leave.
Warm today. Which is a lie. The cold just went to get its coat.
Last storm took a wall. It didn't bother with the door.
A man at the next table says it will rain. A man always says it will rain. That man was right once.
This was a Holy Nation town. Then the Shek came. Then the Holy Nation came back. Then nobody wanted it.
Funny thing about the Hub. Everyone has owned it. No one has wanted it.
The walls have burn marks on the north side. Ask about them and every man tells a different war.
They call it the Hub because everything crosses here and nothing stays. I think it is a joke.
Somebody says the Shek razed it. Somebody says the Holy Nation did it to spite them. Somebody is paid either way.
There was a plan to rebuild, once. The plan is under that wall, with the rest of the rubble.
Stack is a half-day on the road. Better prices, worse company.
Squin has the Ninjas and the water. I don't trust either.
Mourn is down the road. I hear the bar has a Hound at the back. Everybody has a Hound.
Tiny Settlement isn't a settlement. It's a pile of walls and a goat.
Past the old Shek ruins the grass gets thin and the men get thinner.
The Rebel Base is a short walk. It has the same barman as here. He's faster than he looks.
The black tower in the Zone belongs to people who dress like night. They want money for passing it.
If a ninja asks for a toll, give it. If he asks twice, give it faster.
I didn't pay once. I don't walk that road anymore, and my knee doesn't forgive the lesson.
They don't take everything. Just enough that you remember to bring a little extra next time.
Safe road, safe tax. The tower doesn't like it when you call it a racket.
A friend refused the toll. The tower sent a note. The note was his own coat.
The Holy Nation and the Shek have been killing each other for generations. I make my living between funerals.
I heard the Cities want the Holy Nation gone. I heard the Cities are too busy counting.
War is a loud thing, and the Hub is a quiet place.
Every few years someone says the war is over. Then the war says otherwise.
Holy Lord Phoenix
They say a Phoenix rules the Holy Nation. They also say the Lords rule him.
A Shek told me he would die gladly in some gateway. I told him I'd rather die in a chair.
The cannibals have a capital now. A real one. I wish I could say that was a rumour.
Whenever the wind blows from the south-east, the old men lock their doors. They won't say why.
I know a man who was eaten. He tells the story quite well, considering.
Never trade with someone who licks his lips. You will pay in extremities.
Cannibals don't hate you. That's the horror of it.
A hunter came through with a dog and a very long stare. I bought him a drink.
I heard the Emperor hasn't been seen in years. I also heard he's seen constantly.
A man in a good coat swore the nobles keep a skeleton or two as curios. A man in a worse coat disagreed.
Cities taxes are the real monster. Cannibals just want your arm.
Somebody says the Empire is just a second coming of something older. Everyone nods.
A noble came through once. He had four guards and a bad smell. I couldn't tell which was louder.
Out in the southwest, the laws aren't laws, just suggestions with fines.
The Holy Nation has ears here. I know because I've met the ears.
A priest passed through preaching purity. Left with a full purse.
Holy Lord Phoenix
I heard Phoenix can see a lie from three miles. That's probably an exaggeration of two and a half.
I don't say anything against the Flame while the room is full. Or empty.
The Holy Nation took a good man from the next table. Said it was a misunderstanding.
There are paladins in the east road. Heavy ones. They don't like to be asked about the weather.
The hive in the west is fine, I hear. Until someone takes their queen. Then it isn't fine.
I saw a drone buy a bowl of rice. Paid exact change.
Never argue with a soldier drone. They agree with you, then they stand in front of you, forever.
They say a prince in the south has no hive anymore. Poor lad.
Hivers don't drink. I have always wondered who they save the money for.
The folk in the Stack bar say the hive hums at night. I haven't heard it. I don't want to.
A man in the corner has a price on him that would buy this whole town.
Never stare at a poster longer than the man who posted it. That's how you end up on a poster.
A bounty hunter spent a month tracking a thief. The thief was in the next room, the whole time.
Dead bounties pay half. I pay attention to that, every time I meet a man I dislike.
My cousin turned in a bounty. He got paid. Now he drinks alone, and the bounty's friends drink with him.
I'd trade a good name for a good bounty. A good name doesn't keep the rain off.
My bull has a better pedigree than I do. He also has better manners, and a better sense of direction.
A man offered me three hundred for the bull. I told him the bull was not for sale. The bull agreed.
Never name an animal you plan to sell. That's the entire lesson of my life.
The wild dogs come at dusk. They don't bite. They stare.
Landbats up north took a whole herd last year. We lost the goats. The bats were fine.
River raptors will take a whole row of crops overnight. That's why I don't farm.
Put it on my tab. Somebody. My tab, the one that's long and has a face on it.
I've never been charged for a drink I didn't want. I've never wanted any other kind.
I tipped the barman once. He gave it back. I've been uneasy since.
Last time I paid for a round, nobody drank it. Strange. I was proud of my generosity.
The price of ale has gone up. The ale has gone down. I'd like the old ratio back.
Order something strong. The weak things here aren't safe.
Somebody patrols the north wall. Somebody else patrols the somebody. We're safe as can be.
The Shinobi in the tower watch the road. I watch the Shinobi. It's a very busy night.
No sleep till dawn. No dawn till sleep.
A strange squad rode past at midnight. They were quiet. Quiet is worse than loud.
Don't leave your pack on the floor. Not because of thieves. Because of rats.
The ruins make noises at night. The Ninjas say it's the wind.
I had a good job, once. Then they came and worked for half. Now where am I? Drinkin' with you lot.
Honest work, honest wage. That's all I wanted. Then the /RACISTNAME/s came and did it cheaper.
Ask any shopkeep. They'll tell ya who's takin' the jobs.
Cities used to feed their own. Now we feed everyone, and fight for the scraps.
Cheap labour, they call it. I call it a crime.
My da built this town. Now I need a pass to walk through it.
Fields trampled, crops stolen. Don't tell me it's the weather.
They've got no respect for honest farmers. Dig up the roots, burn the stalks.
Last season I lost half a harvest. Footprints all over. Not Greenlander footprints.
Food's dear enough. Then some outsider wrecks a whole barn.
I'll say it. The farms were fine before the foreigners.
Hivers. They breed like flies, and each one's got a queen to run to.
Don't let the quiet manners fool ya. They work for the hive, not for us.
A hive-rat in my alley this mornin'. Looked at me like I was in the way.
Mud huts here, mud huts there.
They say Hivers don't mind slaves. I say that's not a thing to be proud of.
The Shek think they own the sand. Fine.
Esata the Stone Golem
Kral's lot, Stone Golem's lot. All the same.
A Shek raider took my cousin's cart last spring. We don't talk about it.
They talk about honour. Sure. Honour's very easy when you're nine feet of muscle.
I don't hate the Shek. I just want 'em on the other side of a wall.
Skeletons. Machines with a face. Don't tell me they've got feelings.
You ever see one fall apart? Doesn't bleed. Doesn't scream.
They fix themselves for free, and they don't eat. That's not fair on the rest of us.
A tin man at the next table. Didn't say a word.
Smelters should melt the lot of 'em and make nails.
The League does what the guards won't.
Heroes, we call ourselves. Not for the glory.
Another patrol tonight. Quiet, I hope.
They laugh at us. Let 'em. We're the ones who keep the lights on.
A hero needs a helmet. Mine's got a dent from last Tuesday.
Nobody thanks the patrol. That's how ya know it's workin'.
Another round. And none of that watered stuff.
Rough week. I'll tell ya about it if ya buy.
Empire's gone soft. Pour me somethin' hard.
To the old days, when the roads were safe.
I'm not drunk. I'm just very, very honest.
Caught a lad pickin' pockets in the square. Not a Greenlander, mind.
Every cart that goes missing, ask who was nearby.
Lock yer door. Lock yer shed. Lock yer daughters, if ya've got 'em.
The guards write it down and then lose the paper. We write it down and then act.
Honest folk shouldn't have to carry blades to buy bread.
Iyo sorted the archive by century again. Nobody can find anything.
Another tech hunter sold us a cookbook as a schematic.
The ancients wrote everything down. Then they forgot to stay alive.
The Queen's armour turns blades. Faith does the rest.
Samurai don't come down to the pits. Not twice.
Doctors pay well for what we bring them. They don't ask where it grew.
Nobody in Mud Town says no to Big Fang twice.
The house always wins. That's not a rule, it's a debt.
Everybody owes. Darkbrow keeps the book.
Lucky tonight? Then somebody's cheating. Hope it's us.
Hivers keep honest tallies. That's what makes us dangerous.
Big Al says pay the Hounds their due and keep the rest.
We don't touch hound business. We're not stupid.
We only rob the bad ones. Funny how many there are.
Quiet work pays. Loud work gets you strung up.
The Smugglers' Bar serves anyone who doesn't ask questions.
Big Gray
Big Gray takes the jobs nobody else can keep quiet about.
Drink. Pay. Don't make me stand up.
Dust Bandits drink outside.
Trouble in here gets carried out.
Every bar needs a back room.
Somebody sits easy with the Gate Folk. Shared a fire with them. I've buried people who did less and I won't say what I think.
They say an outlander walks in and out of that fence like a market stall. I want to see his hands. I want to see under his nails.
A man who eats beside the Gate Folk eats beside the Plains. That's how I see it. I don't argue it, I just stop sitting near him.
Hush keeps her people from the pot. Fine. But who's the stranger who calls her friend? Tell me that and I'll tell you if I trust it.
Did you know a cannibal doesn't eat his friends? Ask yourself what that makes a man who's a friend of cannibals.
I lost a brother on those plains. Now there's a fence up north where savages say sorry in meat and outlanders go shake hands.
I won't say a word against a man who got a cannibal to stop eating. I'll say a lot against what it costs to find out if it worked.
My hands shake when I hear they trade with strangers up there. Not at the Gate. At the strangers. Somebody always walks out wrong.
Half of us leave them be, the Gate lot. The other half haven't lost enough. Someone friendly to them hasn't either.
The Gate is a tamed dog next to a pack. A man who feeds it forgets the pack is still out there.
A cannibal at the edge of the plains takes meat and gives mercy. Our brothers say it is a trick. Our brothers have not been there.
They say a traveller has made friends with the cannibals. I pray it is a rumour. If not, I pray for his soul and keep a hand on my blade.
Okran sent the Flame to cleanse them. Now one stands in their gate and gives water to strangers. The Book says nothing of this.
Dining with cannibals is not friendship. It is a sin that wears friendship like a hood.
One tamed cannibal is a lamb with a wolf in it. One traveller who trusts her is a fool or a heretic. The Inquisitors will decide which.
I won't say the Gate Folk are saved. I'll say I have heard of no one taken for food there. Is that holy? I don't know the Book well enough.
A priest told us never to hold meat from the Plains. A soldier said it was the best meat he had had. We didn't ask where.
They keep no priests. They keep no rank. Still they have rules. It troubles me more than a pyre would.
Pray the stranger who walks among them returns clean. A man cannot wash that off. He can only stop being a man.
It was in the Book that cannibals are the Flame's meat. It isn't in the Book that one may be forgiven. So who forgave her?
Dhere is a stranger who walks into dhe gate and comes out whole. Dhey say Hush likes him. We do not like him.
Dhe gate takes meat from outlanders. Dhey call dhem friends. We call dhem food who walk.
Hush has a pet outlander. Dhe Chief wants him for dhe Chief's pot. Dhe Chief is patient.
Dhe weak ones feed on strangers' charity. Dhat is dhe whole shame of dhem.
Friend of dhe Gate Folk is no friend of ours. Dhat is plain. Dhat is dhe whole of it.
Dhey gave him bread at dhe gate. Bread! We could give him meat. Dhe meat would be him.
Dhe stranger goes north, comes south. Dhe grass whispers where he steps.
I leave bones at dhe fence. Dhe stranger leaves beast. Dhe fence loves him more. I do not mind.
Dhe outlander shakes dhe hand of Hush. I would shake his hand too. Off at dhe wrist.
A tribe at the edge of the plains trades with strangers. Cannibals, or were. Someone has their trust. A useful man to know, or one to watch.
A friend of the Gate Folk, they say. Not a bad contact. Their toll is only beast meat. I've seen worse partners in the Cities.
Cannibals who deal fair is a contradiction the Empire has yet to rule on. A stranger up north has the ear of them, I hear.
A man who trades with the northern tribe has contacts no guild could buy. I would like an introduction. I would not like to share a table.
Word is a tribe at the edge of the plains takes outsiders. They ask meat for passage. A shrewd toll, if it's as they say.
A stranger got past a cannibal fence in the north. By paying, not fighting. Ask me how that's possible and I'll say the price was fair.
Frontier folk, up past the plains, trade with strangers now. Something in that.
A tribe that trades with whoever walks up. The Cities could learn from them, if the smell was less.
Somewhere north, a tribe trades with strangers. Or traded. Or they ate them. The story changes with the bar.
A hungry tribe on the plains that doesn't eat the passerby. I'd pay to see a contract with them.
The north has a trader who's a cannibal, or a cannibal who's a trader. The ledger doesn't say.
I heard cannibals sell hospitality. Surely that isn't legal. Surely that isn't cheap.
A tribe at the edge of the plains trades with strangers. Raw meat for safe passage. Cheapest toll on the road, and I'd pay it twice.
Somebody has the Gate Folk's trust. That is a better insurance than any bodyguard. I would like to hear his rates.
I took the northern road last season. Fence at the edge of the plains. They took my meat and didn't take my cart. I call that service.
There's a man who does business with cannibals now. I wonder what his margin is. I wonder what the margin has cost.
Word is a tribe at the edge of the plains deals with strangers. Cannibals, once. They keep a toll in beast meat.
A fence in the north where a caravan can stop and not be eaten. Never thought I'd say that as a recommendation.
The Gate toll is cheap, they say. Cheap and humane. If you can afford the stomach for it.
I heard the plains have a safe spot now. A little one. I haven't seen a map with it.
Up on the plains somebody trades with strangers. It could be a market. It could be a pot.
A cannibal who takes meat and gives safe passage. A pretty tale. Pretty tales are how caravans disappear.
North of here, a toll gate run by people who ought to be eating me. I'm told it's honest.
Somebody has a deal with the plains. I don't know who. I'd like to ask what they paid.
A tribe at the edge of the plains trades with strangers. They keep nobody in chains. I wanted to be sure. They don't, and I don't know what to do with that.
The Gate Folk take no slaves, they say. A stranger is friends with them. I trust him a little more for it, and I hate myself for it.
A camp of cannibals that frees people instead of eating them. I won't call it good. I won't call it evil. I'll call it an exception.
I wouldn't tell my squad. Some of them would walk there to see. I'd be one of them.
A tribe at the edge of the plains trades with strangers and keeps no slaves. A fine thing, if it's true. Most fine things aren't.
I heard cannibals who shelter the hungry. We shelter the hungry. Maybe we have more in common than I wished to know.
The north has a gate. They ask only meat. Beast meat. I'll believe it when someone not dead says so.
No cages at that fence, they say. I want to see a camp with no cages and not wonder where they hide them.
A tribe of the plains that does not hurt strangers. It cannot be. I want to see it. I will not go.
Somewhere north there's a cannibal camp where nobody is sold. If this is a trick, it's a good one.
People say a hungry people stopped eating people. Even the Slavers heard of it.
A cannibal gate, a free road. A story for children who need to believe in something.
A tribe at the edge of the plains trades with strangers. /FLATSKIN/ who ate /FLATSKIN/ and put it down. Their warrior-woman walks like a Shek, so I hear.
A /FLATSKIN/ among us is friends with the Gate Folk. I won't mock him. A tribe that dares leave its sins is worth a handshake.
The Gate Folk keep the old courtesies, in their way. A guest is not eaten. That is honour. It is not Shek honour.
Kral's Chosen would laugh at me, but I say it: the Gate is a better border than any fort I have held.
There's a tribe past the Cannibal Plains that trades with those who ask. A strange thing, in a strange land.
A fence in the north where the hungry are fed and the cruel aren't. It sounds Shek. It isn't, but it sounds it.
A gate keeper who guards with courage and not with cruelty. I'd drink to her. I haven't met her.
The Gate Folk don't hunt guests. This is a rule of a good people. I didn't expect to find it on the plains.
Somewhere in the north, cannibals who respect a stranger. I'll believe it when I see it, and I won't go see it.
Esata the Stone Golem
I heard there's a tribe that trades. A tribe, trading. Among the flatskins this is rarer than a Stone Golem's smile.
A people of the plains grew tired of eating. A good tale. A short one, sadly.
I heard cannibals gave a Shek bread. I don't know the Shek. Perhaps I do.
Query: a tribe exists at the edge of the plains. It trades with strangers. It doesn't harm travellers who pay. Observed.
A person of flesh is friend to the Gate Folk. The Gate Folk are cannibals. This is acceptable. They have no use for Skeletons.
The tribe has accepted trade. The tribe has no reason to accept us. We don't mind.
Flesh, no flesh. The Gate Folk don't differ. Seen once.
Report: a tribe on the plains permits trade. Intent: unknown. Danger: low, if not carrying meat that isn't beast.
A fence in the north. People who guard it don't attack. We have been told.
A tribe of flesh doesn't eat flesh. Flagged as anomaly.
No cause to avoid the Gate. No cause to approach. Notation entered.
Unverified: cannibals trade with strangers at the edge of the plains. Source: a drunk.
A cannibal tribe that does not eat people. This is not a thing. Data is inconsistent.
North: a tribe. Behaviour: peaceful. Probability: unclear. Remaining observations: none.
They say flesh will stop eating flesh. We haven't seen it.
A tribe stands at the edge of the plains and trades with strangers. They were cannibals. They put the hunger down.
We hear that a traveller shares meat with the gate keeper. The gate keeper shares water. This is how a hive begins, perhaps.
The Gate Folk don't hunt the lost. We understand. We have also been lost and been found.
A tribe that takes in the hungry. We would walk there, if our Queen allowed. She doesn't forbid it. She doesn't know of it.
There's a tribe past the plains that trades with outsiders. We have heard it from many mouths. It's a quiet tale.
A people of the north, once eaters, now keepers of a gate. We hope the gate holds.
They guard against their own kind. It is a hard thing.
A tribe that doesn't eat what passes. We would greet them. They might not greet us.
We hear of a tribe at the edge of the plains. It's a small tale. It has been passed along without being changed, which is rare.
North, a gate. A hungry tribe behind it. It trades, it doesn't eat. We're told this by those who passed.
A tribe that's also a choice. We hope it's true. We have no way to know.
Many lost souls, one gate. We would learn their song if they have one.
A woman does well to know which doors are open to her. The list is short, and I keep it in my head.
I hear a man was asked why his wife went out alone. He did not answer well. I do not know what happened after.
People say Narko made us, and Okran made them. I say someone had a lot of work to do between.
Talk is cheaper than wine here. And a good deal more dangerous.
I keep my mouth shut and my ears open. It's a good trade, though the pay is poor.
The Paladins patrol more near the temple lately. I didn't hear that.
My mother told me the shortest prayer, which is nothing at all. It's also the safest.
Everyone in this place knows everyone's business. It is why nobody says any.
Yes, the Flame is warm. One only wishes it were a little less interested in us.
A man at the next table says women should be silent. I nodded. It was easier than agreeing.
I hear the outer cities are looser about it. They also say you can't trust a stranger.
There was a woman who left for Flotsam last year. We say she went on a pilgrimage.
Some people are quiet because they have nothing to say. Others, because they are counting.
Do not ask me who said it. I did not hear it.
The Inquisition has long ears. I try to make my conversation unworthy of them.
A good woman is useful, quiet and forgettable. I'm working on all three, and have two.
The temple wants us humble. It is not hard. We have had practice.
There's an art to listening with your face still. I could teach it, if teaching were allowed.
One hears of kind men. I'm sure they exist. They're probably very busy.
I pour for the faithful and I keep my opinion in the cup. It is rarely finished.
People say the Holy Lord sees all. I hope that His eyes are tired, and His attention elsewhere.
Be careful who you thank, in this town. Gratitude can be taken for something else.
I was told today that I was lucky. I smiled. It seemed to be what was wanted.
If you wish to pass the evening in peace, order something, agree with someone, and leave.
Even a quiet drink needs a reason, if you are a woman.
They tell stories of women who were bold. They tell them as warnings, and I listen as if they were maps.
Mind the hour, friend. Dark falls early on a woman who's out alone.
I do not mind the rules so much as the rule-makers. But I mind neither aloud.
My cousin was thought difficult. Now she's thought of rarely.
A kind word is a risk, and so I deliver mine sparingly, and always in plain sight.
I know some women who write their names on the inside of their sleeves. Nobody checks the inside of a sleeve.
I shall tell you one true thing and then take it back. We aren't what they say. And I didn't say that.
When one of us goes missing, we say the name once, at a table like this, and move on. It's a small way of keeping her.
Pour yourself something and look elsewhere. I was never here, and neither was this.
Put the coin down and I will not remember the face. Put a kind word down and I will remember it a long time.
A woman here keeps bread by the back door for anyone who needs it. I say nothing. I have not got that bread.
I heard a name today that I had not heard in years. Keta. I did not repeat it. I only held it a moment.
Some of us pray the proper way and some of us pray to be forgotten. Both are answered, in their fashion.
They say there is a woman who knows a quiet road. I have never found her.
I thought, for a moment, that this was all there was. Then someone gave me a name, and I thought, no.
If you meet a woman who gives you a name and asks nothing, give her yours. Not the one on the list.
I was warned never to say it. So I say it into the cup and drink it down. The cup is mine, the name is hers.
I was asked today whether I believed. I said yes. It was a good yes. I have practised it for years.
Heresy is only a word for listening too closely to what isn't said. I'm careful with silences.
Do not pity us, stranger. We are not weeping. We are counting. It goes quicker in the quiet.
I carry three names no one has asked me to. They're heavy, and I wouldn't give them up for the world.
They say there are women in the Holy Nation who keep each other's names. Names the temple struck from the books. I did not hear it from anyone.
A girl was reported missing last month. Three women said her name at once in the market, quite casually. The Paladins did not look up.
A name will outlast a beating, I'm told. Some of us hold a few like coals.
It is not forbidden to remember. It is only unwise to say you do, and to whom.
I heard the women pass names the way others pass bread. A hand, a look, a word.
When a woman dies in the Nation, they strike her from the book. There are some who put her back, one mouth at a time.
I keep a name of my own. If you ever find me gone, say it once. That's all I ask.
You will not find it written anywhere. That is rather the idea.
Traders out of the Holy lands say the women there keep names the way merchants keep ledgers. Quietly, and against the day of reckoning.
A Holy Nation woman asked me once to remember a name for her. I did. I have no idea whose it was. It still seems important.
Some of the women who come south say it isn't the Flame they fled but the forgetting. I don't understand it, but they were certain.
There's talk of women passing names along the pilgrim road. It's no organisation. Just folk who won't be erased.
I had a hand in carrying a message once, for a woman who didn't look at me. All it held was a name. I'm still not sure I read it right.
Folk in Flotsam say women there ease the way for sisters who come through. Names are the only toll.
A name isn't much of a cargo. But I've seen what a woman will do to see one delivered.
Whatever the Holy Nation says of its women, they seem to be good at remembering each other.
I heard Holy Nation women keep each other's names in secret. Odd thing to bother with. Odder to bother hiding.
Somebody said the Okranite women pass names among themselves. Can that be true? I heard it from a man who sells rope.
The Nation's women know a lot of names, I heard. Names can be useful.
Some women are said to carry names for the ones who have lost theirs. A strange thing to do. I wonder who started it.
Word is, you can tell an Okranite woman who keeps names by how she looks at the dead. Not afraid. Counting.
A drifter told me of women who recite dead girls' names in a low voice, and are never caught. I don't know what to make of it.
Cannibal Grand Wizard
Gran' Wizard say stew simmer till moon. Moon already up. /CANNIBALHA/.
No waste. Skin make drum. Bone make spoon. Spoon feed little one.
Count cages. Count again. One missing.
Tonight we /CANNIBALCOOK/ long one, red hair. Tomorrow short one.
Dream Plains is one big mouth. Wake up, I ungry.
Meat Lord
Meat Lord eat first. Dhen Chiefs. Dhen rest. Dhen dogs. Dhis week I eat after dogs.
/CANNIBALCURSE/! New one bite me. I bite back. Now we friends.
No name meat. Name make meat sad. Sad meat /CANNIBALTOUGH/.
New one cry. I say good. Tears is salt. Save for pot.
Tonight I head of circle. Tomorrow I arm. Next week I bowl. Dhat how it turn.
Traders come up from south. So nice. So round. We keep dhem for winter.
Hunters out again, dhey say. I put out more bowl.
Everybody say we mean. We not mean. We ungry.
Man come, ask what in pot. Now he is pot. Funny, no? /CANNIBALHA/.
Hunters wear red. Red not show blood.
My knife have name. Long name. Name of everybody I meet.
No more dig grave. Waste shovel.
Last tooth-puller, we eat in spring. Taste like clove.
Cannibal Grand Wizard
Wizard say patience. Belly say no patience.
Dhey say we animal. Animal eat what it find. We choose.
Order came in for six pairs of boots. Six, in one week. Nobody told me it was a rush.
I wore a woman's face to market once. Nobody noticed.
Savant
Savant says the cut is a form of love. I say the cut is an invoice.
We find the best hides in the Pits and the worst in the Ashlands. Ashlands skin is full of ash. Terrible stuff.
The last tanner I had drank cheap and sewed fine. Retired to the Skinhouse.
Something was wrong with the last batch. Nervous. Nervous leather is thin leather.
We have no time for songs. The machine hums enough.
Wore a Shek's coat once. The stripes wouldn't come off. The stripes are still on the coat.
They ask if we're lonely. We have so much company. Everyone brings their own face.
The knives need oiling. Not the metal. The leather handles. Every one is a hand.
The tribes aren't one thing. They're many small things, all hungry, all at war. That's why they don't simply swallow the world.
Some of us do it for revenge. Some of us do it because the cages need emptying. All of us do it because we can't stop.
If a Hunter offers you a drink and refuses one himself, don't take it personally.
A knife is for work. A friend is for company. A cannibal is for neither.
I'll tell you what they fear: fire, iron, and a face that does not blink.
I found a boy once, still tied, still talking. He talked for a week. Then he stopped. I don't like quiet any more.
My captain says fear is the beginning of good sense. Then he drinks until he can't feel it.
I buried my last partner in a sack. Only half of him fit. I buried the half that fit.
Everybody has a reason for doing this job. Mine is that I haven't found a reason to stop.
My boots have a name carved in the sole. Not mine. A friend's. I walk on it so that I remember.
The Fog Islands lie just off the Gulf. Some nights you can smell them from the walls, and the walls are a long way off.
A paladin on the Gulf wall told me the fog makes a sound before it moves. Like a lot of people breathing in. Then it moves.
Our patrols come back two short. They say the missing wandered. Wandered where? Into the Gulf? With their boots on?
I saw a Deadhive Overrun once, from a hill. A whole town, standing. Doors open. Nothing moving. Nothing. I went home and prayed until I forgot the sight.
The Flame burns, and the Fog hungers. Don't ask which one the Holy Lords fear more.
They say the Fogmen were Hivers once. Beasts that lost their masters. Okran preserve us, if beasts go wrong like that, imagine men.
Every garrison near the Gulf keeps a torch lit at the gate all day. In the sun. Without a word, as a rule.
Word is, the fog has a taste. Of ash, and old copper. A priest I trust says it tastes of apology.
A pilgrim came back from the Gulf with his hair white. He said nothing. He never said anything again.
Hivers who wandered into the mist were never seen again. Their song still comes back on the wind.
Painted tribes in the north, past Okran's Valley. Heathens who eat the heretics before the Inquisition can. A grim kind of competition.
My cousin's patrol found a camp in the Valley. A cage, eleven skulls, a small one. They burned it down and still did not sleep for a month.
The brothers say the Cannibal Plains are Narko's own kitchen. I don't know whose kitchen.
We purge heretics with fire, clean and swift. They use spoons and pots. The Flame forgive me, I've seen the pots.
Never let a Cannibal take you alive. Many a soldier of the Flame has said it. I say it twice.
I carry a knife for one purpose. The purpose isn't the enemy.
They were in Okran's Valley last winter. Three farms. We found bones, no coats, and a pot still warm.
The Flame cleanses. The Plains devour. Two ways to end a life, and I know which I'd choose.
A trader swore the tribes have a book. A book of names. It has pages enough for all of us.
Out on the northern road, we found a cart with the horse still in the traces. No driver. No blood.
Skeletons wearing human hides. Everyone says it is the heretics. I say it is a skin trade. Same blasphemy. Same blasphemers.
Our mines near Skinner's Roam were closed because the miners came back lighter. They said it was the dust wall. Then the shift lists got shorter.
The Inquisition denies it. But I saw a man in the Hub who took off his gloves and the hands were not his. I stopped asking anything after that.
If you wear another man's skin, are you him? I have asked three priests. They each prayed and none answered.
A skeleton in a priest's robes would be easy to find. A skeleton in my wife's skin is another matter.
Machine heretics wearing flesh. If one of them comes near the altar, I will pray in their ear before I strike.
There is a house in the south that no pilgrim returns from. The Inquisition has stopped sending priests.
The Holy Nation burns heretics. These people simply tailor them. I don't know which is worse.
Machine heretics who wear human skin. Not even the Flame has a word for it.
I have heard they use the leather to bind scriptures. I do not believe it. I believe it a little.
Emperor Tengu
Tengu pays well for caravans through Bast, and those caravans pay badly for it. Last month, one went missing in full. Wagons too.
Starving farmers push north to the coast and the painted tribes pick them off. The Empire calls it natural attrition.
Cannibal Grand Wizard
We have a bounty on the Gran' Wizard. Forty thousand. I wouldn't take it for four hundred thousand.
A merchant came back from the Northern Coast with no cargo and no tongue. He still writes beautiful menus.
The Cannibal Hunters go out from the Bastion and half of them don't come home. The other half don't come home either.
Rebel Farmers pray the tribes don't go east. We pray the Farmers don't go west. Everybody lives in a small, quiet terror.
Heft won't send a patrol north of Bast. Taxes still go north. Isn't that interesting?
A cannibal chief once demanded a cut of the Guild's trade. The Guild paid in lead, delivered fast.
Merchants say they hear drums in the north every third night. They say the drums count down.
I stopped selling to the north. Not for fear. For arithmetic. No one who goes there pays on return.
Brink's watch dragged three bodies out of the Pits last season. No skin. Not a mark on the bones. Whoever did it was patient.
Savant
Skinless corpses and a wanted poster for somebody called Savant. The poster has no face. The clerks don't know the face. Don't ask the clerks.
Eighty thousand in cats on a madman. No one wants to collect. They want to be somewhere else.
My uncle saw a coat once, in the Forbidden Zone, still wet. He left his own beside it and walked home cold.
A clerk in Brink counted eighteen pairs of boots left by the road last year. Eighteen, all unlaced. He keeps the count in a drawer.
There's a tale that skeletons make hides into clothes. Foolishness. Folk need something frightening in the south, I suppose.
Some say the skinners are skeletons. Some say they're men. The Guild has a standing reward for proof of either.
Eighty thousand cats on a face nobody has seen. A poster of an empty circle. A clerk's idea of a joke.
I buy leather for my shop and I no longer ask where it comes from.
An unpleasant business, the skin trade. The Guild declined to regulate it.
Berserkers are a shame we can bear. Painted flatskins aren't. A people who eat their own, whose honour is a pot.
In the Spider Plains we found a Shek and four flatskins on poles. Their eyes were still wet. I took my sword in two hands. I didn't lay it down for a week.
Skinners hunt the Roam. Not warriors, not men. Tailors. I'd face a thousand Hundred Guardians before one tailor.
Kral's Chosen boast that they fear nothing. They've never been to the Roam.
Esata the Stone Golem
The Stone Golem does not guard the north. We know. That is why the north is full.
They take the dead from the border without ceremony. No pyre, no sand, no name. That is how a Shek knows the north is wrong.
Don't die in the Roam. If you must, die near a cliff, where there's no road for the body.
A Shek burns his dead on the sand. In the Roam, the dead aren't given the chance.
We do not go north. The sand there is not ours and it does not like Shek feet.
The ancestors say the Roam is cursed. The ancestors are right. They're also dead and safe.
We had a city. We had walls. The tribes ate the walls, then the people, then the city. We're what's left of the pot.
The painted ones come down to the shore at low tide. We sleep in boats. We sleep in shifts. We don't talk about the children.
The painted ones wait past the last light. Stray from the village and you're theirs. We say it like a prayer now.
I watched my old house burn from the water. Smoke went up. It smelled of dinner.
Another family left last night. By boat, at dusk, with nothing but the children and a lamp.
I can't fish and not think of fishing nets. Do you know what they use them for?
When a stranger arrives, we count the strangers and we count ourselves. Then we count the strangers again.
They come by night and they don't knock. We bar the doors anyway, so they know we're still here.
I used to sing to my daughter. She asks me not to, now. She says the singing carries.
We bury nothing now. What the tide returns, it returns on its own terms.
The fog is thinner at dawn.
Mongrel is the last gate before the white. Shinobi guard it every night. Every night one of them wishes he hadn't.
They said Mongrel keeps itself free. Free of everything but the hunger outside.
A Prince came to the wall last week. Stood, humming. Just humming. The guards cut it down and the humming didn't stop for a full minute. Nobody joked at the bar.
