There's a crew out there that's killed more than the fog. Don't ask me where they are.
Grave-Fillers. Even the scavengers can't keep up.
That crew they call the Unbroken. Four hundred fights won between them.
The Unbroken. Knock them down, they get up, they win anyway.
Nobody bets against the Unbroken any more.
Orsa Quillon
Orsa Quillon wants two cats a head and your cart's best wheel. Pay the first one fast.
She was a carter's wife once. Now she counts every wagon like it owes her husband.
The Toll-Widow's rope sits across the road past the Hub. Go around and you meet her friends.
Quillon never robs you. She only taxes you until you have nothing, then she stops.
My brother refused her toll. We found the cart.
Quillon is working the hills again, the woman with the rope. Drifters swear she hums while she does it.
Orsa Quillon
Somebody on the Hub road killed a Shek courier for skipping the toll. Orsa Quillon's rope, they say.
A widow's rope and a dozen Dust Bandits who answer to her, and the Guild still won't send a proper escort.
Avoid the crest past the Hub after dusk. Quillon's lantern means the toll is open.
She taxes the poor, never the Guild's armoured wagons. Clever or cowardly, I can't tell.
There's a woman in the desert who charges road tolls with a rope and a grudge.
They say the Hub road has a widow on it who never lets a wagon pass free.
Quillon, I think. Some tollkeeper in the dust. Pay her or go around, whichever is longer.
A rope across the road and a lantern. That's all a traveller is told of her.
The rope is cut. Quillon is dead and someone has already hung a new one.
People say she fell with her lantern still lit. The road past the Hub is quiet for the first time in years.
Orsa Quillon
Orsa Quillon finally paid a toll of her own. I only wish I had seen it.
A hundred wagons and not one mourner. Funny what a widow earns.
Quillon is in a cage. Imagine, being charged for the road she thought she owned.
They locked up the Toll-Widow. Her bandits scattered like dropped coin.
Somebody caught her alive. Rumour says she asks every guard for his toll through the bars.
Orsa Quillon
Orsa Quillon caged, and the Hub road open. Brings a tear to a carter's eye.
Ferrant Dray
Lord Dray accepts tribute, you understand. If you aren't offering it, he accepts it anyway.
He bows to everyone before he cuts them. Manners were the only thing his father paid for.
Ferrant Dray
Ferrant Dray wears a signet ring that opens no doors anymore. He thinks it still does.
Heard him demand a bow from a farm girl at sword point. Then he took her mother's ploughshare.
Ferrant Dray
The flats are Dray's court now. You'll know his hired men by the polished boots.
Some ruined noble is calling himself a lord of the northern flats. Wears a cape in this heat.
Ferrant Dray
Dray, they call him. Titled, drunk on it, and quick with a blade.
A noble gone bad is worse than a bandit born. He knows how to be cruel politely.
Ferrant Dray
Ferrant Dray was an Empire man once. Now he sells his own army's leftover insults.
Hired swords, a signet ring, and the manners of a gutted fish.
Somewhere north there's a lord with no land who robs travellers in full court dress.
Ferrant Dray
They say a noble house collapsed and its third son took to the road. Dray, or Dreyne.
A cape, a sword, a title nobody honours. That's the gossip, anyway.
Imperial blood on the north road, charging fees.
Ferrant Dray
Ferrant Dray is dead and his ring is missing. Somebody's wearing a dead house on their finger.
Ferrant Dray
Lord Dray bled out in the flats like any peasant.
The fallen noble fell the last time. His hired swords went home to their mothers.
He died owing the Cities, the Guild and his tailor. In that order.
Ferrant Dray
Lord Dray is in irons. They say he demands his meals be served on a tray.
The Cities have a nobleman in a cage. They say he complains about the draft.
Ferrant Dray
Ferrant Dray, caged. It was always going to be either the sword or the stocks.
He claims diplomatic immunity from inside a cell. His guards enjoy it very much.
Hask Morrow
Hask Morrow is a Sentinel who stopped believing. He still takes the offerings, mind you.
I heard he wept when he first robbed a pilgrim. By the fifth, he did not.
The deserter in Okran's Pride keeps his Holy armour on. A mockery, or a habit.
Hask Morrow
Morrow sent a message to the Fist. It read: you left me hungry.
Hask Morrow
If you meet a Sentinel on the road with no patrol and no orders, it is Morrow.
A Holy deserter is preying on pilgrims. Good. Let them eat each other.
The Nation has a rotten Sentinel it can't catch. Funny how its holy fire misses.
Hask Morrow
Morrow, was it? Took his armour and his fear and went rogue.
Pilgrims come into the Cities with stories of a Sentinel who prays while he robs.
A deserter has the Holy army embarrassed. I buy a drink for whoever finds him.
Some Holy soldier lost his faith and now his purse is full. Typical priesthood.
I heard a deserter stalks the pilgrim roads in full Holy plate.
Hask Morrow
Morrow. A Sentinel gone off the rails. They say the Nation hasn't had a deserter before.
A Holy man who steals from the Holy. It's the oldest sin there is.
Hask Morrow
Hask Morrow is dead. The Fist pretends it never knew him. The pilgrims are praying for him anyway.
The deserter fell in Okran's Pride. They buried the armour with him, the shame of it.
Hask Morrow
Morrow wanted a quiet death. Got a loud one.
The Nation sings of a good example. I sing of a hungry man put down.
Hask Morrow
Morrow is in chains, not in Holy ones. The Nation's furious that someone else got him.
A deserter in a cage, praying out loud. His captors do not interrupt him.
Hask Morrow
Hask Morrow caged. The Fist will want him back for a different kind of lesson.
They have the Sentinel. I hope the Holy Nation never gets him back, honestly.
Sarn Ashvael
Sarn Ashvael blesses you before he strips you. Swears it's for your own good.
They sing in the desert at dusk, hungry ones. You'll know it's him by the sermon.
The prophet of the Empty Bowl says every full belly is a theft. Mine is quite empty, but he doesn't believe it.
Fed a caravan crew to the sand and prayed over them.
He was a baker once, people say. The bread lie is the cruelest part.
A prophet of hunger is gathering mobs. No bowl will ever be full enough for him.
Sarn Ashvael
Sarn Ashvael, they call him. Walks the bone edge with a hundred hungry mouths behind him.
I saw his followers fight over a dead rat like it was communion.
He tells them the desert owes them, and the strong are the debt.
Starving men with a sermon are the worst kind of armed.
Some prophet is starving bandits into a cult. They say he never eats.
A starving preacher walks the east desert. Don't share your bread.
Sarn Ashvael
Ashvael, was it? A holy man for the hungry. He should have stayed holy.
Out in the dust a man blesses the hungry and they follow him into knives.
The prophet of the Empty Bowl is dead. His mob won't stay a mob for long.
Sarn Ashvael
Sarn Ashvael, finally full of nothing. They buried him in the sand, half his followers fighting over the shovel.
I pity the hungry ones left. A prophet is easier to follow than to forget.
He preached about bowls until the blade came. May his be full.
Sarn Ashvael
Ashvael is caged. His followers wait outside the walls and sing.
They caught the prophet alive. He sermonises through the bars on the sin of waste.
Sarn Ashvael
Sarn Ashvael in chains. The mob hasn't scattered. It waits, and it's hungry.
A prophet in a cage still has an audience.
Veldt Harrow
Veldt Harrow sits at the roadside with a book and a pen. You hope he's waiting for somebody else.
He taps the page twice for each prisoner. If he taps once, you weren't worth the ink.
The Tallyman bought a family and buried the grandmother alive to save the food. Marked it in the book, I heard.
I saw him once from far off. Writing. Always writing, never looking up.
Harrow keeps wet ground behind him. Whatever is out there, I won't look.
The Tallyman. That's what they call him now, the slaver who buries. Lord, I hope he never comes this way.
A slaver turned murderer is worse than both.
He still wears the old slaver coat, polished. The ledger never gets muddy.
Harrow's hunters never complain. I think they're afraid to.
Wet roads, a ledger, a pen. If you see them, go the other way.
There's a slaver who stopped trading and started counting. That's all I'll say.
Out in the flood country a man writes down the dead.
Some slaver killed his own market. They call him the Tallyman.
A butcher with a book. Nobody can tell me where the pages end.
The Tallyman is dead. They found a ledger, half burned, with more names than the Cities ever had.
Veldt Harrow
Veldt Harrow bled on the same road he buried people on.
I hear the pen is still in his hand. No one wants to take it.
No more taps. The flood roads are very quiet tonight.
Harrow is caged. Every guard avoids his eyes, and he writes anyway.
They caught the Tallyman alive. He is asking for fresh paper.
Veldt Harrow
Veldt Harrow under a lock. For the first time in years the ledger isn't in his lap.
He counts the bars now. He says there are always more than there should be.
Borun Vahl
Borun Vahl was the best of his circle, once. Now he is the thing mothers do not name.
The Oathless will not take your purse. Only your name and your life, in that order.
He cut the stone mark from his own arm and threw it at a priest's feet.
I saw Vahl in the canyons. He didn't draw. He didn't need to.
A flatskin asked him for passage and he gave it, and cut him down on the other side. His honour is a knife.
Some oathless Shek roams the dry mountains. He duels travellers for their boots and kills the winners.
Vahl, people say. The Kingdom won't discuss him.
A Shek with no mark and no master. A rare and dangerous creature.
Even other Berserkers keep their distance from Vahl. That's a high bar.
Borun Vahl
Borun Vahl keeps his scabbard empty. He draws from the air, so I hear.
A Shek exile hunts the canyons. It isn't a story I enjoy.
Some Shek lost his stone and now fights without rules. They call him the Oathless.
Vahl, I think. He doesn't take prisoners, nor coin.
A warrior without a creed in the mountains. Keep your blade sheathed and your mouth shut.
The Oathless is dead. Kral's kin are quiet. Even Shek who hated him say it was a clean death.
Borun Vahl
Borun Vahl fell in the stones. Somebody carved a mark on his arm afterward. Mercy, or insult, who knows.
He won't be named in the halls, but he will be remembered in the sand.
A broken oath, a clean blade.
Vahl is caged, and the Shek do not know whether to be ashamed or relieved.
The Oathless sits in a cell. Even the guards salute him, and then wonder why.
Borun Vahl
Borun Vahl alive in a cage. A Shek in chains is a terrible thing to watch.
They say he won't eat. He says only the free may break bread.
Ilsa Hearthmourn
Ilsa Hearthmourn leaves candles at the edge of our fields. Nobody dares to touch them.
She was the hardest of the Pacifiers. Now she tells children the Flame is only fire.
Her voice is calm. That's the horror of it. The heretics are usually shouting.
A pilgrim told me he followed her out of the Pride for a day and a night. He hasn't spoken since.
People say she lights her candles from a flame no priest blessed.
A Holy apostate is spreading talk. I know that look. The Nation is afraid of a candle.
Ilsa something, a Pacifier who changed her mind. The Holy Nation has no humour about that.
I hear she sits with the pilgrims and tells them they are people, not tools. Dangerous words.
A candle in the dark and a woman who used to beat heresy out of men.
Ilsa Hearthmourn
Hearthmourn, they call her. The faithful call her worse.
A Holy woman has turned against the Nation. They say she carries a candle. That's all I know.
Some apostate lights a candle at every camp. The Holy Nation won't say her name.
Ilsa Hearthmourn
Hearthmourn. A good name for a heretic. A very bad one for a victim.
I heard a Holy killer woke up one morning and chose peace.
Ilsa Hearthmourn
Ilsa Hearthmourn is dead and the Nation is lighting candles of its own. I don't know what that means.
They burned her candles after. The fields smell strange.
The Candle Heretic is gone. Her followers walk in circles looking for another.
An apostate in the dirt. The Nation sings.
Ilsa Hearthmourn
Hearthmourn is caged. The Nation wants her back so very badly.
They have the Candle Heretic alive. Imagine the questions the Inquisitors have prepared.
Ilsa Hearthmourn
Ilsa Hearthmourn is in a cell, and she's still lighting candles. Where does she get the wax?
She asked her guard if he was happy. He cannot sleep now.
Hodd Crake
Hodd Crake taught me to skin a bonedog. I won't be at the table when he eats.
The Long Appetite leaves clean bones. Neat, almost. Like he's being polite.
He still wears the Hunter's colours. It frightens the real ones more than the cannibals.
A hunter on a hunt will tell you the smell tells him. Crake says it tells him what to order.
We found his old camp. Three cooking pits, and a tally on the wall. Not cannibal marks. Hunter marks.
A Hunter gone bad, out on the bone plains. That breaks even a cannibal hunter's heart.
Crake. Used to be one of those bastards in the Bastion. Now he eats what they send.
A man who hunts cannibals and becomes one. Poetic, if you like cold poetry.
Carries a cleaver as long as my arm. It isn't for the hunting.
The Pride would pay to see him gone.
Some cannibal hunter turned sides. That's all anyone tells me.
A man called the Long Appetite is wandering the bone plains. Nobody wants to meet him.
I heard the Hunters lost one of their own to the thing they fought.
A hunter with a cleaver and a lonely smile, they said. Stay on the roads.
Hodd Crake
Hodd Crake is dead. The Hunters buried his colours separate from his body.
The Long Appetite fed the plains one last time. I won't mourn him.
I heard they found his tally on the wall, longer than any cannibal chief's. The Bastion burned it.
A hunter gone wrong, put down by a stranger. Perhaps that was the best way.
Crake is caged, and the Hunters can't decide whether to kill him or study him.
They have the Long Appetite alive. Don't feed him anything in front of him.
Hodd Crake
Hodd Crake in chains. He smiles at the guards. They stopped eating in front of him.
The Hunters want him dead, the Cities want him alive, and he wants dinner.
Pim Sillery
Pim Sillery steals a man's boots, then comes back for the laces. Unpleasant, but never lethal.
The Magpie leaves little glass beads where he lifted something. As a joke.
He lifted a power core from a sleeping Tech Hunter and sold it back to her for double. She was grateful.
Never leave anything shiny out near the Graveyard. The Magpie sees it from a mile away.
Pim Sillery
Sillery talks to himself as he steals. Argues with himself, actually.
There's a thief who steals only metal that glints. They call him the Magpie. Pim, is it?
He took a whole robot arm out of a ruin and swapped it for a dummy.
The Magpie is clever. That's what makes him dangerous. He knows the ruins like his own pockets.
I wouldn't hire him. Even for free. Not if he's the one counting.
A scrap thief out there with a dozen pockets and a taste for plans. The Hunters want him bad.
Some thief out west steals tech for fun. They call him the Magpie.
A Tech Hunter went rogue and now robs ruins. Quite the nuisance.
Heard of a scrap thief called Pim who steals more than he sells. Odd, that.
A man with a hundred pockets, the story goes. Nobody tells me why.
The Magpie is dead. His nest was full of shining bits no one will claim.
Pim Sillery
Pim Sillery had a hundred pockets and every one was empty when they found him.
I heard his last act was to try to steal the knife that killed him.
No more stolen plans. The ruins feel safer already.
The Magpie is caged. They emptied his pockets and counted forty items. Nobody knows where thirty came from.
Pim Sillery
Pim Sillery behind bars. He has already stolen the guard's keys twice, they say.
They caught the Magpie, and the Hunters want their plans back. He claims he lost them. He didn't.
A thief in a cell. Let's see how long the lock lasts.
Teshin Ro
Teshin Ro doesn't shout. He only says your name, and asks if you'll draw.
The ronin cut down a Holy deserter at a well and drank from it afterward. Sat there until dusk.
He told me once that he lost his lord in a war nobody remembers. I believed him, and was sorry.
His sword is old. His coat is older. His habits are the oldest of all.
Ro leaves the dead sitting upright with their eyes closed.
A ronin walks the northern flats, challenging whoever he meets. The Cities fear him.
Teshin Ro
Ro, they call him. Teshin Ro. Worse than a bandit, because he's sorry afterwards.
I heard he cried at a funeral. His own victim's. He's that kind of man.
He bows before and after. Never in between.
A swordsman with no lord and no hurry. I almost wish him luck.
There's a ronin in the desert who duels every traveller. That's all anyone knows.
A masterless swordsman, so I hear. Even the Shek avoid him.
Teshin something. A man who fights because he forgot how to stop.
A ronin walks, a dead man follows. It is a story told at night.
Teshin Ro
Teshin Ro has fallen. They say he was smiling at the end.
The ronin's sword is gone. Some say it was buried with him, others that it was sold. I hope it was buried.
Eleven men and one more. Ro settled his account at last.
The wind is calm over the northern flats. Strange how loud that is.
Ro is in a cell, and he refuses to eat until someone fights him fairly.
The ronin lets himself be caged. Says it's the only way to rest.
Teshin Ro
Teshin Ro in chains. He thanked his captors. They didn't know what to say.
A caged swordsman is a very quiet thing. The guards are afraid of the silence.
Ysolde Gorehollow
Ysolde Gorehollow has a laugh like a kettle. You hear it before the screaming.
Every raider in her nest wears a vial around the neck. Her blood.
I walked into her camp once to trade. The jars on the shelf were labelled by name.
She sings to the dead. They aren't interested.
Ysolde Gorehollow
Gorehollow has no army. She has a congregation.
A woman is bleeding travellers into jars out in the ashlands. They call her the Bloodmother.
Ysolde Gorehollow
Gorehollow, was it? Her raiders are getting bolder. Every month a caravan is short a crew.
She trades her jars to Skin Bandits.
The ashlands have always been hungry. Now they have a mother.
I heard her nest smells of iron. Not rust. Iron.
They say there is a mother in the ash who drinks the road dry.
A bloodraider matriarch. Nobody tells me which jar is whose.
Ysolde Gorehollow
Gorehollow is a name you'll know in a bad dream.
A woman and a jar collection. The ashlands aren't kind.
The Bloodmother is dead. They're still breaking jars in the ash. Some of them weren't empty.
Ysolde Gorehollow
Gorehollow's laugh stopped. The ravens left the nest the same hour.
I hear her congregation sat in her camp for days afterward, waiting for her to come back.
The ashlands have lost their mother. They haven't lost their hunger.
The Bloodmother is caged. She asks the guards for their names.
Ysolde Gorehollow
Ysolde Gorehollow lives, in irons. Her raiders watch the walls and sing.
They caught her alive. I don't like how calm she is.
A mother in a cage. The ash is waiting.
Marta Cull
Marta Cull measures the tide on her fingers. She knows how long a man holds his breath.
Mother Brine
The Brine-Wife has a whistle. When you hear it, the Reavers come. It sounds like a gull.
She doesn't shout. She hums, and stands very still, and waits for you to move.
I lost a cousin to her tide line. She sent back his boots.
People say she was a salvager once. Then the sea took her husband and she took the sea's side.
Mother Brine
A Reaver woman called the Brine-Wife is drowning crews on the south coast.
Cull has a way with a rope and a tide chart.
She ties them above the waterline and lets the sea decide.
The coast is dangerous enough. Now it has a hostess.
Reaver ships and Reaver dead. Cull has made it worse.
There's a woman on the south coast who drowns people on a schedule.
Mother Brine
The Brine-Wife, they say. Terrible name, terrible woman.
A Reaver matron who counts tides. I'll never sail south.
Cull. A name the sea whispers, I'm told.
Mother Brine
The Brine-Wife is dead. The tide has left her camp unwashed, which seems unfair.
Marta Cull
Marta Cull drowned in the end, I heard. On dry land. How's that for sea justice?
No more gull whistle. The shore feels quieter and cleaner.
The south coast breathes again. A little.
Cull is caged, far from any water. She asks for a bucket and hums.
Mother Brine
The Brine-Wife is in irons. Her Reavers wait in the surf.
Marta Cull
They caught Marta Cull. The sea hasn't forgiven them.
A Reaver woman behind bars, and every guard checks the ceiling for leaks.
Teodric Clackjaw
Teodric Clackjaw snaps his teeth when he thinks. Then he kills the thing he was thinking about.
He won't rob you until you've lost a fair fight. His fairness is an insult.
I saw him bow to a corpse before he looted it. Shell polished like a spoon.
He has a bell strapped to his back. Rings it to start. Rings it to end. There's no bell in between.
The crabbers follow him because he wins. That's the whole creed.
Some banned crab champion is running tournaments on the road. The prize is your life.
Teodric Clackjaw
Clackjaw is the name. Don't ask him why he clacks. He has a very long answer.
He still thinks the pits are open. In a way, they are.
I heard his shell is made from the armour of eleven rivals.
A crab raider with a code is worse than a crab raider without.
There's a crab-pit champion loose in the south. I won't say his name; it clacks.
Out in the pits a fighter makes travellers duel.
A banned fighter with a shell. That's the whole of what I know.
Teodric Clackjaw
Clackjaw. Sounds like a joke until you meet him.
Teodric Clackjaw
Clackjaw is dead. They say you can still hear the clacking in the pits at night.
The champion lost the one fight he wasn't allowed to cheat in.
Teodric Clackjaw
Teodric Clackjaw's shell ended up on a post.
The crabbers are fighting each other now. For the title, no less.
Teodric Clackjaw
Clackjaw is in a cage and insists the match wasn't over. The guards have stopped arguing.
They caught the disgraced champion. He demands a rematch every dawn.
Teodric clacks his teeth against the bars. The sound is driving the prison mad.
A champion in chains. The crowd would pay to see it.
Maruka Tal-Khesh
Maruka Tal-Khesh makes you stand in the sun while she counts. Reaching forty is a boast.
She says she walks Kral's last stand every day. She's the only one who thinks it's joyful.
A cut for every sin, she says. Then a cut for every virtue. In the end it's just cuts.
Her blade is chipped and her patience isn't.
I heard her laugh once, at the sixtieth.
The Hundred Cuts. A Shek woman of Kral's creed. Stay clear of the stone roads.
Kral's followers are mostly bluster. Maruka isn't bluster.
She has a tally scarred on her own arm. Every notch is a stranger.
She doesn't rob. She only measures.
A Chosen who takes the legend as a recipe. The Kingdom is ashamed.
Out in the Shek roads is a woman who counts to a hundred on the living.
A Kral zealot, they say. Her name is a long one.
The Hundred Cuts. Never ask her what happens at ninety-nine.
A Shek legend turned into a habit. A bad habit.
The Hundred Cuts is dead. A hundred and one, they say, from the number of wounds.
Maruka fell in the stone roads. The Chosen buried her without a word.
She counted until the last. That's the part nobody wants to repeat.
The Kingdom has declared it a good death, which means it was a loud one.
Maruka is caged. She counts the bars out loud, over and over, until the guards weep.
The Hundred Cuts, alive and bound. The Kingdom asks to be told nothing.
She asked her jailer for a knife. He asked her why.
A Shek zealot behind bars. Some things shouldn't have lids.
Aldous Peel
Aldous Peel measures you with his eyes. Do not let him finish.
I know a man who met him and left in a better jacket. He didn't leave in the same skin.
The Tailor has a very polite way of speaking. Flat, like a floor. That's the worst of it.
They say he has a mirror in the ash, just so he can look at his coat.
A skin by the road is a signature. The Tailor doesn't sign twice.
Aldous Peel
Skin Bandits are a rumour to most. Peel is a name for those who have buried theirs.
I've never seen a man so careful with a knife.
Aldous Peel
Peel is a name from an old report. No one dares check it twice.
Aldous Peel
The ashlands don't lack monsters. Peel is one with a good tailor's eye.
A coat of skins. A hat of hair. I will not elaborate.
Out in the ashlands there's a tailor, they say, who works in skin. No one sends him orders.
A man in a coat of people. I don't tell this story twice.
Aldous Peel
Peel, the Tailor. A myth, they say. Myths don't leave scraps.
I heard the Skin Bandits have a name and a coat. I wish I hadn't.
The Tailor is unpicked. They say his coat was too heavy to burn, so they buried it.
Aldous Peel
They found Aldous Peel inside a coat of faces. It took three men to carry the coat out.
He came apart cleanly. Even the bandits clapped.
The ashlands are quieter, but I won't trust the quiet.
The Tailor is caged, and the jailers can't hold their breakfast down.
Aldous Peel
They have Peel in a cell. He asks to measure the guards.
Aldous Peel
Aldous Peel, alive and locked. Nobody wants to be the one to touch his coat.
I heard he sits very straight, very still, as if waiting for fabric.
Mister Tuppence
Mister Tuppence wears a hat. You laugh once. He asks you for the premium.
I paid his premium and the road was fine. A bandit with a conscience. It troubled me for weeks.
He keeps receipts. Receipts for everyone he has ever killed. It's the strangest ledger.
Mister Tuppence
Tuppence will never lie to you. He just says what he means in a way that's hard to survive.
Last week he stopped a Guild caravan and asked if the toll was fair. They said no. He apologised, and took it anyway.
A Skeleton bandit with a hat and a ledger. The pits are full of strange.
Mister Tuppence
Tuppence insures what he will later rob. At least he's honest about the interest.
He has a scale, a coin, and a very sharp stare.
Word is, his hat has a crossbow bolt through it. He just says, premium.
I'd pay the premium. Cheaper than the funeral.
There's a Skeleton in the pits who sells protection with a knife. Don't ask me why.
Mister Tuppence
Some bandit in a hat. Tuppence. Pays his debts and collects yours.
A polite Skeleton with a club. That's the whole story.
People say he issues receipts for the dead.
Mister Tuppence
Tuppence is scrap. His ledger shows the Guild still owes him two cats.
Mister Tuppence
Mister Tuppence fell, hat and all. They say the hat was the hardest part to finish.
I miss the receipts. They were the only honest part of the pits.
Skeleton protection has gone out of business.
Mister Tuppence
Tuppence is caged. He has already drafted the terms of his release.
The toll Skeleton is in irons. He asks every guard for his name and rank.
Mister Tuppence
They caught Mister Tuppence. He asks for a receipt of arrest.
A Skeleton in a hat behind bars. He demands to speak to whoever holds the ledger.
Ulla Weeper
Ulla Weeper starts low, like a kettle on a slow fire. Then it climbs. By the end you're on your knees.
Her mob stops when she stops. Her mob stops all at once. That's how you know to run.
They say she cries real tears, and the mob drinks them. I won't repeat what else.
She has a name for every voice in her head. She shouts them in turn.
I heard her scream from a mile away. Birds fell.
The shriekers have a mother now. Ulla something. Worse than before.
Ulla Weeper
Weeper is her name. A good name for a bad thing.
Her mob stands in a ring and screams until the target drops.
A woman in the swamp who won't stop crying, and a hundred who answer her.
I sleep with wax in my ears. It does not help. It never helps.
There's a screaming woman in the swamp and everyone near her screams too.
A shrieker queen. That's what the traders say, and they say it quietly.
Ulla, I think. She keeps a flock.
In the swamp a woman cries and the earth listens.
Ulla Weeper
Ulla Weeper is dead. The swamp is so quiet that the Swampers keep checking their ears.
The shriekers have stopped. For a day. Some say a night. Then they start again.
I heard she went silent at the end. Strange.
The mud has her now. The mud has everyone eventually.
Ulla is caged. She screams at the bars.
Ulla Weeper
They caught the Weeper alive. Her guards wear plugs.
Ulla Weeper
Ulla Weeper in a cell, crying. Her guards can't say if it's grief or tactics.
The swamp is quiet, and her cell isn't. That's justice, of a kind.
Dunmar Quell
Dunmar Quell wants the swamp. He says it to anyone who will listen, and a few who won't.
His Sabres wear red. The blood is new.
I paid his tax once. He gave me a receipt, signed Captain. I still have it.
Dunmar Quell
Quell thinks he is a king. He holds court in a mud hut.
He beat a man to death for calling him a boss. Captain, he said. Always Captain.
A bandit in the wet who calls himself Captain. The Red Sabres are his now.
Dunmar Quell
Quell, so I hear. Short temper, long ambition.
Every bandit wants to be a king.
The Sabres used to be a gang. Now they're an army, thanks to him.
I don't envy the Swampers. A Captain is worse than a thief.
There's a bandit king in the swamp. Red cloth, loud voice, bad manners.
A Red Sabre captain with big ideas. Do not offer him a hand.
Dunmar Quell
Quell, I think. He wants the whole wet.
I heard he gives speeches before he cuts.
Dunmar Quell
Dunmar Quell is dead. His Sabres squabble over the crown, which is only a bucket.
The Red Captain bled in the mud like everyone else. Nobody saluted.
They found his tally of taxes in his boot. The swamp isn't as poor as he claimed.
Dunmar Quell
Quell's kingdom lasted a season. That's long for the wet.
Dunmar Quell
Quell is caged. He insists on being addressed as Captain by his guards.
The Red Captain is in irons. His Sabres are plotting.
Dunmar Quell
Dunmar Quell in a cell. He gave a speech to the bars last night.
A captain with no crew. It's a sad thing, but I won't say it aloud.
Gammer Tuck
Gammer Tuck wants half your cart. He says it was grown by his grandfather, and so it's his.
He sings an old harvest song when he marches. The whole country knows when he's coming.
I saw him gut a tax-collector with a sickle. He wiped the sickle on his own hat.
Tuck claims every field in the green edge. He has a deed. It's written on a barn door.
He drinks rotgut for breakfast. Don't accept a cup.
A rebel old man calls himself the Plough Captain. He's very polite to women and children.
Gammer Tuck
Tuck, they call him. Gammer Tuck. A tax-collector's nightmare.
He charges your caravan a sack of grain for passage. Per beast.
The rebels follow him because he laughs. It's the strangest reason I've heard.
Funniest bandit in the green country.
There's an old man with a scythe leading farmers against the Cities.
A rebel in the green country sings as he kills.
Gammer something. A farmer who stopped farming. That's the whole of the tale.
A rebel with a scythe. He laughs a lot, they say.
Gammer Tuck
Gammer Tuck is dead. The farmers are weeping and singing, together.
The Plough Captain fell in a field, with a scythe in his hand. They buried him there, the old fool.
Even the Cities' tax-men attended the funeral. I don't know why.
The green country won't be as loud now.
Tuck is caged, singing his harvest song to anyone who will listen.
The Plough Captain is in a cell. The guards joined the chorus by the second night.
Gammer Tuck
Gammer Tuck in chains. He asked for rotgut. They gave it.
A rebel in a cage, laughing. The Cities don't know what to do.
Sayo leaves a grey ribbon tied around the wrist of her kill.
I found a ribbon on a magistrate's bed. He was still warm. The window was still shut.
She never speaks. She just stops being there.
I heard she was hired to kill her own teacher and did so for double. That is the kind she is.
If a gust of sand finds you in an empty room, count your fingers.
A sand ninja kills by contract. Grey Ribbon. Sayo. I fear for the Shek.
The Shek say the Grey Ribbon can't be bought.
Hired murder is a thing the Empire left us. Sayo continues it.
I heard she worked for a Shek lord and then killed him. Her fee was doubled.
A ribbon, a note, a grave. In that order.
There's a ninja in the desert who kills for hire. A grey ribbon is all she leaves.
A woman of the sand ninjas, they say, with no face and a fine knife.
Sayo, I think. The Grey Ribbon. A name for the hired.
Rumour says the ribbon arrives before the killer does.
The Grey Ribbon is dead. Someone found a ribbon in her own hand.
Sayo fell in the canyon. The wind took her ribbons.
No more ribbons. A hired killer, killed without a fee.
The dunes aren't so lonely now. The wind has moved on.
Sayo is caged. She doesn't speak. She hasn't slept. The guards are changing hourly.
The Grey Ribbon is in a cell. She stares at one guard at a time, until he leaves.
They caught the assassin alive. I'd rather they hadn't.
Sayo in irons. I hear the ribbons are still arriving in the city.
Cuddy Pell
Cuddy Pell sets a place for you at the roadside. A rotten plate, a bone fork. Sit.
He talks to the sack. The sack, I swear, answers him.
He will rob you, and then thank you, and then rob you again to say sorry.
I met him at a ford. He asked me for my name, my mother's name, and my boots.
Cuddy has one rule: nobody leaves hungry.
A mad Mongrel sits on the flood road and asks everyone to dinner. Don't go.
Pell, they call him. Cuddy. A cheerful sort of murderer.
He bows to his victims. Sings them off. Bad voice.
I never saw a bandit so happy at his work.
It's the sack that frightens me, honestly.
There is a man in the wet country who sets tables for travellers and does not let them leave.
A mad bandit with a sack and a song.
I heard a crazy man dines on the roads.
A song carries on the wind in the south. It's not a nice song.
Cuddy Pell
Cuddy Pell is dead. The roadside is quieter. The goat, they say, is still talking.
The Mongrel with the sack finally had his last supper.
I'm told he laughed. Of course he did.
The flood roads are safer. A pity, in a way.
Pell is caged. He sets his meal on the bars and invites the guards to join him.
Cuddy Pell
They caught Cuddy Pell alive. The sack is evidence now. Nobody has dared open it.
Cuddy in a cell, humming. The other prisoners asked to be moved.
A mad Mongrel in a cage. He thanks everybody. It's awful.
Tchik of Seven Voices
Tchik of Seven Voices speaks softly, in seven tones, one after another. Each of them says please.
His drones carry spears of bone, polished. They look lovingly cared for.
I tried to bargain with him. He smiled with six mouths and shook his head with one.
Tchik was hive once. Now he's everything the hive was afraid of: free.
The clicking stops when he's about to strike. It's like the world holding its breath.
A drone with seven voices. The Hivers won't discuss him.
Tchik, so I hear. He walks alone and not alone.
A hive-bandit swarm is nothing like a human one. They don't run.
He speaks politely. They all do. It's the horror of it.
The dark fingers are quiet for a reason.
In the desert a drone leads a swarm with seven voices. I don't wish to hear more.
A rogue Hiver. That's all anyone will say.
Tchik, they call him. It sounds like a joke until he speaks.
I heard the clicking from a mile away.
Tchik is dead. The clicking in the fingers stopped, and nothing replaced it.
The seven voices were silenced one by one, I heard. The last one asked for water.
A drone without a hive is a sad thing. A dead one is sadder.
The swarm that was Tchik is scattering. I wish them no luck, and no harm.
Tchik is caged. The seven voices argue among themselves.
They caught the drone alive. His guards say he has stopped clicking.
Tchik behind bars. He thanks the guards for the food, in seven tones.
A drone in a cage says please to the bars.
Elric Vosk
Elric Vosk rings a small brass bell. Hire him, and you hear it for the last time.
He still wears the Guild's colours. Cleaned and pressed. That's what I can't forgive.
He offered me escort across the hills for a fair rate. I said no. He bowed. I haven't slept right since.
He lost a daughter once, they say. He lost the rest of himself after.
A guard who kills clients is a mercenary who forgot why he took the work.
A deserter mercenary rings a bell at the crossroads.
Vosk, they say. Killed the whole caravan he guarded.
He gives a very reasonable rate. That is what makes it so awful.
The Guild is quietly hunting its own. That should tell you something.
A guard who turns on the herd. I won't travel near the crossroads.
A mercenary murdered a whole caravan and kept the bell.
Out on the desert tracks a guard offers escort.
Vosk. A killer in the Guild's colours.
There's a bell on the road. If you hear it, walk the other way.
Elric Vosk
Elric Vosk is dead, and the bell is lost. Some say it is buried with him.
He fell on the old desert track. A merchant took his boots and left the rest.
The Guild marked the contract complete. Nobody mourned.
No more brass bell on the road. It's very quiet.
Vosk is caged. He asks for the terms of his release, politely, daily.
The Guild's deserter sits behind bars, and the Guild would rather he hang than talk.
Elric Vosk
Elric Vosk in irons. He rings an imaginary bell. His guards pretend not to hear.
They have Vosk alive. I wonder what he will tell them.
Pyke Ludlow
Pyke Ludlow leaves a broken manacle on the chest of every one he kills. He calls it a receipt.
He asks one question: have you ever owned a person? The wrong answer is the truth.
I never traded anyone. He let me go. He still asked me twice.
Ludlow sat with a dying slaver for an hour and listened to him pray. Then he finished it.
The Anti-Slavers disown him, but nobody will say it to his face.
An Anti-Slaver turned executioner is working the roads. The Cities are embarrassed.
Ludlow. He believes in his cause. That's the problem.
He killed a farmer for owning a field-hand. Said the contract was fraud.
A fanatic with a righteous cause is the hardest kind to stop.
I support the cause. Not Ludlow.
A freedom fighter is killing slavers, and everyone who looks like one. His name is Ludlow.
An avenger walks the roads. The slavers fear him, so do the rest of us.
Pyke, I think. He hates chains more than people.
Some say he's a hero. Some say he's a butcher.
Pyke Ludlow
Pyke Ludlow is dead. The Anti-Slavers say nothing. The slavers say it was a mercy.
He fell with a manacle in his hand.
A good man, gone wrong, put down. I won't call it justice.
The roads are quieter. Not because of peace.
Ludlow is caged. He refuses to eat from a hand that locked him in.
They caught the avenger alive. The Anti-Slavers asked to see him.
Pyke Ludlow
Pyke Ludlow behind bars. A strange irony, isn't it?
He rattles the lock each night. Not to escape. To remember.
A Guild caravan went out toward the Shek towns and never arrived. The guard's name was Vosk, I think.
Wagons don't vanish. People take them. The Guild is quiet about it, which means it's angry.
There's a shopkeeper in the east still waiting on a delivery.
Guild contracts go one of two ways. The goods arrive, or someone pays. Right now it's someone.
The Guild promised my cousin iron plates. They never came. The shopkeeper has stopped asking.
A merchant at the gate said his wagons are overdue. He did not look angry. He looked like a man making a list.
Foreign guards watching foreign wagons. When it goes wrong, it goes wrong in our dust.
Whoever took that caravan, the Guild will find. They keep better books than we do.
Elric Vosk
Elric Vosk took a job guarding a caravan and walked off with it. I heard that on the road.
The Mercenary Guild hasn't said a word about Vosk. That's the loudest thing I've heard all week.
Merchants are nervous. A caravan guard turned thief makes every guard a suspect.
A guard who kills the master and keeps the bell. That isn't mercenary work. That's something else.
Vosk is dead. The Guild paid for it, I heard. Caravans are still nervous but the guards are less so.
The man who took the wagons is gone. The goods aren't found. The Guild writes it off and moves on.
A shopkeeper in the east got his iron after all. That's the Guild for you: slow, but they pay.
Elric Vosk
Elric Vosk finally paid his debts.
That guard who took the caravan, Vosk, is dead. The Guild has stopped complaining about it.
Elric Vosk
Somebody finally put down Elric Vosk. The roads are a little safer for hired guards.
A thief with a sword and a bell. Gone. Nobody will miss the bell.
A guard who turned thief is dead. Merchants will sleep a little easier, and hire a little warier.
Meat Lord
The hunters keep a list. The Meat Lord is at the top. Nobody has crossed him off yet.
Painted arms. That's how a hunter proves himself. A left one is for show. A right one is proof.
The nightmares never go away. We keep killing but they never go away.
Meat Lord
Meat Lord eats well. The hunters don't.
Meat Lord
The Meat Lord is somewhere out in the plains. The hunters want him dead. The rest of us want to stay far away.
Cannibal Hunters ask for painted arms as proof. I'd rather not know what they do with them.
Meat Lord
I met a hunter once who said the Meat Lord eats his own kind when there's nothing else. I believe him.
Don't take the cannibal road without a hunter's blessing. The plains don't forgive.
Meat Lord
The Meat Lord is dead. The hunters crossed him off the list and cut a notch in their belts.
A stranger brought a painted arm, and then a dead Lord. The hunters shake their heads and nod.
The plains are quieter. Don't be fooled. A new Lord is always hungry.
Word is, the hunters wept. I don't believe it. But I believe they stopped for a moment.
Meat Lord
The Meat Lord is dead. The cannibals of the plains have lost a leader. They will have another by spring.
Somebody finally ended the big cannibal. The hunters paid.
The painted tribe is angrier now. Be careful on the plains road.
Meat Lord
A Meat Lord is down and the plains aren't safer. The hunters say that's how it always goes.
Finch wants a CPU. Rhinobot's, specifically. The hunters are drawing lots.
Rhinobot wanted to help. That's the problem. A robot that helps with anything is dangerous.
The University pays for relics, not blood.
Iyo pays on delivery. Finch pays in lectures.
Machinists are after a robot's brain. It's a nice change from their usual books.
There's a bounty on a robot called Rhinobot. A robot, can you imagine.
Tech Hunters go into ruins and don't return. Rhinobot is a ruin that walks.
Mind the Ashlands. Old machines don't care who you are.
Rhinobot is down. The University got its core. I heard Finch cried. I don't believe it.
A robot that wanted to help is a pile of scrap. A stranger did it, for the Machinists.
Iyo paid in full. First time anyone has seen that.
The ruins are quiet. The scholars are loud.
People say a robot in the Ashlands is finished. The Machinists took its brain.
Rhinobot, the helpful one, is gone. I didn't know he was real.
Somebody has been dismantling the old machines. Somebody is getting paid for it.
The Machinists got their robot brain. I hope it was worth whatever they paid.
Pyke Ludlow
Pyke Ludlow hits the wagons and leaves the slaves loose. The Slave Traders want him found.
An Anti-Slaver turned killer. Even his own side doesn't like what he has become.
Guards come back cut and refuse to say who by. They say it anyway after a drink.
Ludlow has made more enemies than the whole of the Anti-Slavers.
Pyke Ludlow
Pyke Ludlow was one of us. Now he kills anyone who ever owned a chain. That isn't what we're for.
Ludlow is a stain on the cause. We would like him ended, but not by us.
A good man gone wrong. That's the worst kind.
The Anti-Slavers don't claim Ludlow. The Slave Traders have a price on his head. The two facts are related.
Pyke Ludlow
Pyke Ludlow is dead. The slavers say it was business. The Anti-Slavers say nothing.
A rogue Anti-Slaver ended. The wagons travel unguarded and nobody is happy about it.
Ludlow's gone. The Slave Traders paid someone. That someone isn't welcome in the pens.
The man who killed slavers and slaves alike has stopped. Few will say they miss him.
Pyke Ludlow
Pyke Ludlow is dead. The slaver wagons are moving again. That is the world.
Somebody killed Ludlow, the rogue. The Slave Traders paid. That sounds right and wrong at once.
A killer on the slave roads is down. The roads aren't safer, just quieter.
A killer who hunted the slave wagons is dead. Both sides pretend it was an accident.
A Shek shopkeeper told me he's still waiting on iron. Four plates, he said. Four plates is a thing to wait for.
The Guild is quiet when it loses a wagon. It is loud when it loses face. Right now it is loud.
I buy iron from the Guild. The price went up this month. They say it is the road. I think it is the thief.
Merchants lose caravans every year. It isn't the loss they remember. It's who took it.
A guard turned thief is the worst kind. He knows the route, the guards and the bell.
Vosk was a good hire once. That's how it starts.
I wouldn't take a caravan job this month. Not with Vosk loose on the road.
Caravan guards talk about Vosk the way a doctor talks about a disease that only attacks doctors.
Meat Lord
A hunter won't tell you where the Meat Lord eats until you show him a painted arm. Bring a right one.
I sold a painted arm to a hunter once. He paid in dried meat and said it was a fair price. I did not ask what he did with it.
The Cannibal Hunters judge you by what you carry, not what you say.
Fresh arms keep poorly. Come back quickly.
Meat Lord
Cannibals don't waste anything. A Meat Lord wastes less than the rest.
Painted ones leave bone fences around their camps. If you see a fence, turn around. If you see two, run.
The plains are quiet at night. That's when the hunters go in.
Nobody walks the plains for pleasure. Nobody walks them twice without a reason.
Iyo is the University's face to outsiders. He's polite, flat and very precise about what he pays for.
Finch doesn't leave the University. Iyo does the talking. Between them they decide what the world is worth.
Machinists pay late, but they pay. Tech Hunters bring them what the ruins give up.
The Tech Hunters' notes are free. The University's pay isn't.
Old machines still walk some ruins. They are not hostile. They are not friendly either. They simply do not understand you.
A robot that helps with anything is the most dangerous kind. It will help you into a grave.
Ruins keep their dead, and sometimes the dead keep their duties.
Hunters say the old machines remember. Remember what, no one will say.
Slave wagons have been getting hit on the open road. Guards come back cut and the wagons come back empty.
A man called Ludlow used to free slaves. Now he kills everyone near them. Slavers don't understand it.
The Slave Traders are paying extra for wagon guards. It doesn't help. The guards just die for more.
If you hear an Anti-Slaver talk about Ludlow, they do not use his name. They spit instead.
Shop trader here's short of bandages. The guards are coming back cut. He doesn't say by whom, but we all know.
The pens are quiet. When the pens are quiet, it means the guards are afraid.
Medical supplies cost more this month. The Slave Traders are buying all they can find.
A trader told me Ludlow knows our wagon routes.
The Inquisitors are asking questions in the confessionals. Someone has been feeding a heretic.
Ilsa Hearthmourn
They say there is a cell in the hills, and Hearthmourn's name is the first word in it. Do not say it loudly.
Seen a priest packing his scripture in the night. Maybe nothing. Maybe a name on the Inquisition's list.
Ilsa Hearthmourn
Faith has a rot in it these days. Hearthmourn used to be one of ours. Now we hunt our own.
A Paladin told me the cell is moving. He did not say where. He did not look well.
If the Inquisition comes for you, you have already lost. If they want a hired hand instead, you have a choice.
Ilsa Hearthmourn
Hearthmourn was a Pacifier. Now she is a sermon turned inside out. The Flame will not forgive her.
A priest in my district stopped sleeping. Said he heard things he cannot unhear. Then he stopped speaking at all.
The Nation loses a few every month to doubt. Better to lose them to the sword than to the whisper.
Ilsa Hearthmourn
Holy Nation is hunting its own again. A woman called Hearthmourn who won't pray the way she's told.
Heard the Inquisition is paying for an old Pacifier. Funny, they never pay for anything else.
Ilsa Hearthmourn
The Nation turns on itself eventually. Hearthmourn today, somebody else tomorrow.
There's a cell of the faithless out there, people say. Even the Flame can't keep everyone in line.
Ilsa Hearthmourn
Hearthmourn is dead. The Inquisition has quietly stopped asking questions at the temple doors.
They burned the cell's scripture in the square. Someone put the woman's ashes in with it, they say.
The Pacifier who forgot her prayer is gone. Funny how quiet the pews are now.
Ilsa Hearthmourn
Somebody took the Inquisition's coin and ended the Hearthmourn cell.
Holy Nation wiped out some heretic cell in the hills. Somebody paid for it, I heard.
The Nation's Inquisitors have one fewer name on their list.
Ilsa Hearthmourn
Word is the Flame's hounds got their woman. Hearthmourn, something.
The Holy Nation is quiet about some heretic they burned. That usually means a loud one.
Runaways keep turning up with the same story. A mistress who whips her own rows and never sleeps.
There's a slave farm that eats its workers. Grace runs it. The Anti-Slavers know and they can't reach her.
Heard a runaway crying in the camp last night, saying the same name over and over.
Someone has to end the Mistress. I would, but I have a family and a head I like attached.
The escaped are all talking about the same woman. Grace. They say she counts them every night.
I got out of a farm once. Not hers, thank the stars.
Ask a runaway what they fear most. Half of them will say the Mistress.
Whoever kills Grace won't need to buy a drink for a year, in the right camps.
Grace has the best output of any farm in the south. Efficient.
The Mistress wants three hundred hands by month's end. I wouldn't take that contract.
Someone is asking about Slave Mistress Grace. Wrong questions. The Anti-Slavers should keep their noses out of it.
Slave traders talk about Grace the way miners talk about a deep seam. With greed and with fear.
I heard Grace is dead. The farm is open and the rows are empty. Not all of them ran far.
Mistress Grace fell at her own gate. The Anti-Slavers put it about that it was a runaway's justice.
Somebody went into the rows and Grace didn't come out. Half the south is celebrating and the other half is counting losses.
A farm gone cold. A Mistress gone cold. I cannot say it hurts to see.
Slave Mistress Grace is dead, they say. The farm is losing money fast.
Grace is gone. The Slave Traders will name a new mistress by the next market, and it won't be an improvement.
Somebody opened a slave farm in the south. Not for coin, I think. The Mistress didn't live.
Heard a farm in the south went quiet. Slave Traders are blaming the Anti-Slavers. The Anti-Slavers are blaming luck.
Tora The Fearless
Tora still carries her blade. Every Shek knows it and none of us can look away.
Tora The Fearless
A warrior without horns is a warrior without a name. Yet Tora will not die quietly.
Esata the Stone Golem
There's talk of a duel. Honour wants it settled. The Stone Golem doesn't speak of it.
Gate guards turn their heads when her name is said. Shame is a heavy thing to carry.
Tora The Fearless
Shek have a disgraced warrior in the dust. Tora. She keeps her sword and her pride and nothing else.
Heard the Kingdom wants a duel. Foreigners only, of course. They wouldn't dirty their own hands.
A Shek without horns, still fighting. I wouldn't cross her road for a month's wages.
Tora The Fearless
Tora the Fearless, they used to call her. Now the Kingdom calls her something else.
Tora The Fearless
Tora is dead. They say it was a duel, clean. The Kingdom has gone quiet, which is its own kind of praise.
Gate guards say her name again. That's how you know it's over.
She died on a blade, in the open, like she wanted. That is more than most get.
The Kingdom didn't cheer. Shek don't cheer. But something in the walls loosened.
Tora The Fearless
Tora is dead. A foreigner did it, they say, and the Shek approved. I did not think they could.
Tora The Fearless
That disgraced Shek, Tora, finally fell. They say it was a fair duel. I didn't think Shek knew fair.
The wandering Shek with no horns is gone. Somebody met her sword.
A Shek duel ended well, for once. Even the Kingdom looked pleased, and that's saying something.
Boss Simion
Rebel Farmers burned another tax-wagon last week. Boss Simion sends the ashes back with a note.
Boss Simion
The Empire keeps asking for Simion's head. The Empire keeps not paying enough for it.
Loyal farmers pay their dues in fear now. The Rebels watch the road.
Boss Simion
I knew a man who joined Simion. Last I saw him he had a scythe and a stolen helmet.
Boss Simion
Boss Simion has a fort, a grudge and a lot of men. The Empire is nervous.
A peasant rebellion, they call it. Fires and dead tax-men. Hard to sell to either side.
Boss Simion
Don't take a contract from the Empire against Simion.
Boss Simion
Simion's captains are better armed than half the city watch. I'd stay away.
Boss Simion
Simion is dead. The Empire declared a holiday and the farmers declared nothing at all.
The Rebel Farmers lost their Boss. Some went home. Some went further into the hills, angrier.
I heard it was a stranger, not a soldier. The Empire will still take the credit.
No more tax-wagons burning, for now. The fields are quiet and nobody trusts it.
Boss Simion
Rebel Farmers lost their leader. Somebody killed Simion. The Empire will be insufferable.
That farmers' rebellion in the north-east went quiet. They say the Boss fell.
Boss Simion
Simion's gone. Whoever did it got paid by the Cities. It's a living.
Boss Simion
Fort Simion is leaderless. The Empire's tax-men are heading back out, and nobody is cheering.
Red Sabres took another cart on the south road. Their boss sits in the hideout and counts.
A score of Red Sabres around one fat man. You could tell the whole swamp where he's and it wouldn't matter.
Whoever kills the Red Sabre boss will drink free in every swamper bar. I'll pour the first one.
Red Sabres drink our rum and rob our roads. Their boss never walks out.
Red Sabres have a boss with a hideout somewhere in the mud. Everyone knows.
Swampers want the Red Sabre dead. They've been saying so for years.
I'd take a Red Sabre contract if the price were right. It never is.
Don't cross the swamp roads at night. Red Sabres don't care who you are.
The Red Sabre boss is dead. The roads through the wet are quiet, which makes the quiet itself nervous.
Somebody walked into the hideout and out again. The sabres don't know who to be afraid of.
A new Red Sabre will rise. They always do. But for now the wet can breathe.
Swampers poured one for the dead boss. Not out of love.
The Red Sabres lost their boss. Somebody went into the swamp and walked out again.
Heard the Red Sabre is dead. The swamp is a quieter place and a more nervous one.
Whoever killed the Red Sabre is a fool or a legend. In the swamp it's the same thing.
Red Sabres without their boss will do what bandits do: split, bicker, and rob in smaller numbers.
Elder
The Elder says we're free of flesh. I'm free of nothing.
Elder
Some Skeletons follow the Elder. Some don't.
Iron hall. Many followers. Many blades. I don't go there.
Elder
The Elder is loud. Loud draws attention.
Elder
The University has a question and the Elder is the answer. They don't like what it says.
A Skeleton leader who preaches against flesh, and a university of flesh that studies him.
Machinists pay well for Skeleton data. Better for a Skeleton leader's end.
Elder
The Elder's followers are no use to scholarship. They only fight. The scholars hate waste.
Elder

/LWRIVAL_1/ sat in that corner for an hour sharpening a blade, muttering your squad's name.
