Devolved from the ancient scholars, I say. The labs poisoned them and they forgot how to cook properly.
The cannibals are the best argument for a funded research station. Or a very large wall.
Of all the theories, I like the one with the poison best.
Some of my colleagues say the cannibals are older than the labs. Invaders. They ate the ancients. I find that comforting, in a bleak way.
The labs in the north have blood on every wall. Whose, we don't agree.
Invaders or heirs. The bones in the labs aren't decorated with the answer.
The cannibals have the labs now. Whoever had them first isn't in a position to object.
Machinists say cannibals are devolved scholars. Tech hunters say they're tribes that outlived the Ancients. Everyone agrees to avoid the plains.
I don't care where they came from. I care where they're going, and that's toward my dinner.
Descendants, invaders, devolved, born that way. They all eat the same.
Either the cannibals were clever once or the clever ones were food. Both are comforting in their way.
Whether they fell from clever people or outlasted them, they die the same under an arrow.
We have two enemies up here, the ones who burn you and the ones who eat you.
Some say they're the old clever ones gone wrong. Their arrows don't seem clever.
I don't care if they were scholars.
They do not eat us. They hate us anyway. I have a theory about that and I keep it to myself.
The cannibals hate us. We're the only ones who don't taste of anything.
Some of them look at us as if we remind them of something. We prefer to look away.
They fear us for something we don't remember. That's fair. We fear ourselves for the same reason.
Cannibals scream a name when they see us. It isn't ours. It might have been once.
Dhe glass place in dhe north. Some say we came from it. Some say we came to it.
Dhe old ones dhat were in dhe shiny place are quiet now.
Dhe shiny place is ours now. /CANNIBALHA/ Dhe ones before are not complaining.
Our elders say we were dhere first. Dhe odher elders say dhe opposite. Dhey argue with full mouths.
High Priest Varloo says the Hub can't be held while Narko's darkness covers it. He wants the first of her minions destroyed.
Every time we take the Hub we lose it within months. Varloo says Narko. I say walls take more than prayers.
Varloo says the first dark ones must fall before Narko's grip loosens. I say a wall must stand first.
Varloo wants the dark ones destroyed first. The Hub is an afterthought to him.
Narko shook the southern wall down, Varloo says. I saw the rubble.
High Priest Tyluig says it is not Narko. He says Okran's light wavers because we let our own house rot. Women forward, children shaming fathers.
Varloo blames the dark. Tyluig blames us. The priests haven't stopped arguing and the Hub hasn't stopped falling.
Tyluig says we must purify ourselves. The Hub falls anyway. Perhaps we are not pure enough yet.
Tyluig preaches purification. The Hub preaches silence. The Hub is winning.
Sentinels vanish at the Hub, voices in the walls, empty rooms. Say what you like about the reason. I will not stay a night.
They told us to retake the Hub. Nobody told us to stay.
The Hub keeps taking sentinels. We keep sending them. The priests call that faith.
Wraiths took a brother from us at the Hub. Nobody found a body. We were told to be calm.
The Hub is cursed, the report said. The report was approved.
We sacked the Hub and left it burning. Ask why we left. We do not answer.
The Hub holds nothing worth a warrior's death. We took what we wanted, and the place took something from us.
The Hub is a burnt place now. Ask no more.
We left the Hub and didn't look back. A warrior doesn't look back.
The Hub changes hands like a bad coin. Empire, Nation, Shek, and now the ruin belongs to whoever sleeps there.
The Hub was a good town. Then three banners learned it was good.
The Hub fell to the Empire, then to the Nation, then to nobody. Even the dust moved on.
Hub is a bad address. Rent is free and nobody collects.
Okran warms, Narko cools. Neither one asked for a throne.
The old women say the great father split in two so the world could breathe. I like that better than the sermon.
The Nation burns doubt. We feed it.
A god can have two halves. A village needs more than one.
I prayed to the light for the first thirty years. The dark answered, so I switched.
Heretic. They called me that for asking a question. I'd like the question answered.
Okran left the Nation. Or the Nation left Okran. We took his half of the sky and kept it.
I met a priest who asked me which half of god I preferred. I said the one that stops the fire.
I touch my neck when I think. Everybody says so. Nobody in this room has a better habit.
Freedom is a debt. Most of us are paying it forward and some of us are paying it back.
They laughed when we said we would burn the slave market down. Now they lock the doors.
Funny how the iron stays heavy after it comes off.
I'd love to explain. I'd also love to finish this chapter. One of us will lose.
The books say what they say. The ruins say what they say. The gap is my career.
Ancient isn't a word. Ancient what? When? Be specific, I charge by the adjective.
Someone else digs. I read what they bring. It's a very civilised arrangement.
Three weeks to reach the ruin. Nothing in it. The lady will wring my neck.
Anything buried can be sold. Everything else is weather.
Nobody comes back from the Ashlands. That is why the rumours are so good.
Spiders, mostly. They don't pay a wage.
The Empire took my farm. You have food. You see where this goes.
I don't hate you. I'm hungry. It makes me worse than hatred.
Boss Simion
Uncle Simion has a mouth full of dirt and a heart of gold, mostly.
We hit the roads, not the poor. That's the rule, even when the poor hit back.
Farmers with swords. That's all the Empire made us. Credit where it's due.
We planted wheat once. Now we plant ambushes.
Everybody in the Empire has a landlord. We just stopped paying ours.
My hands remember wheat. My knives remember the Empire.
They told us to farm or starve. We chose a third thing.
I never raise my voice. People hear me anyway.
Interest is a gentle word. I like gentle words.
I remember exactly what you owe.
A loan is a leash made of kindness.
Pay me in cats, or in favours. I prefer favours.
I don't break legs. I know people who do, and we're on good terms.
Debt is a family. You're always welcome to join.
I lend to anyone who can scare me. So far that's nobody.
Big Grim
Nobody here tells me what to do. Well, Grim does. But she is pretty about it.
Sit, drink. You look like you spent a fortune on fear.
No taxes, no chains, no sermons. Enjoy it before the knife arrives.
The nobles can keep their silk. I have a good stick and a better pipe.
I laughed at a priest once. He's still running. Best day of my life.
Free air smells like smoke and bad decisions.
Come back tomorrow and I'll deny this conversation. Also, buy me a drink.
Someone once offered me a title. I used it to light my pipe.
The hemp grows here. The sermons don't. That's the whole argument.
The beast-hunter in the fancy chair. Sixty-two of them, one chair.
Their Holy Lord is a man in a bright hat who burns people. We have no use for him.
A king the Nation keeps raising from the dead. We would have buried him twice.
Sixty-two lords in a row, and they haven't learned to hold a sword. That's the Nation.
Big wise dhing in dhe old days. Maybe edible. /CANNIBALHA/
Dhe tin ones say a big one gave all. Dhe big one was dhe best meat, maybe.
Tin ones say big one gave himself. We say we would have taken a bite. /CANNIBALHA/
Stobe? Dhey say dhe name and go quiet. Good meat for dhe shy. /CANNIBALHA/
People say Narko lies in the roots. I say the Nation keeps its own graves well tended and the rest of the garden poorly.
Roots and abyss and temptation. A very large sermon for a very small garden.
The great father split in two. The Nation kept one half and put the other under a tree.
Under the roots, people say. I say the Nation buries what it fears, and that's all I need to know.
Holy Lord lives long. Many Holy Lords. Dhey all taste dhe same? /CANNIBALHA/
Fire men say dhey are reborn. We say dhey are reheated.
Holy Lord Phoenix
Phoenix burn good. Many Phoenix burn. Dhe smell is always same. /CANNIBALHA/
Dhe big lord die and come back? Dhen we eat him twice. /CANNIBALHA/
I heard the Rebellion was a drought and a locked gate. They say the poor did it. They say the poor were right.
Don't talk about the old Emperor near an official. Don't talk about the new one either.
Red ground. That is what the Rebellion left. It is still there if you dig.
Drought, then nobles, then blood. In that order, every time.
A hundred swords closed on Kral and he still stood.
I fight to reach the other side. Do not call it a sickness. Call it a destination.
The ones who die well are waiting. I do not want to keep them long.
We don't hurry to Gateway.
The Emperor keeps what he must keep. A Vault is a reasonable thing for a reasonable state.
I don't know what's in the Vault. I know who isn't in it, and I'd like to stay on that side.
A Vault is a reasonable place. The Emperor is a reasonable man. That's what we say.
Order has costs. I don't ask who pays.
The Nation holds the Hub for a while and loses it. We've been here since before the last priest. Walls aren't our problem.
Varloo, Tyluig, whoever. They argue about why the Hub can't be held. We just hold it, and pour drinks.
The priests blame Narko, or blame themselves.
Priest blames the dark, priest blames the sinners. We pour.
Hive limbs came before the skeleton ones, people say. Odd for a people who don't talk about the past.
Economy arms are a hive trade. A hiver won't tell you the rest.
Skeleton limbs, hive limbs. Trade secrets travel with the supplier.
The bug men made the first limbs, people say. Their eyes tell you to stop asking.
There was a time hive and skeleton shared something. We don't say what.
A skeleton limb in a no-hive shop makes us uneasy. It should not. It does.
Hive and skeleton once shared a bench. Neither of us remembers who left.
We do not discuss the skeleton limbs in our shops. We repair them.
Some smells stay. Rust, sweat, fear. I sit at the edge of the room so I can leave.
I have forgotten the faces. I haven't forgotten the sound of the key.
The key made the worst sound in the world. I still flinch at doors.
I don't sit with my back to the room. Ask a former slave why.
Some things come off with the iron.
Rumour has it the sea once stood higher. Rumour has it that I'm paid enough.
If you find an old book, bring it here. If you find an old man, leave him there.
The lab at the northern end of the plains is the best-preserved crime scene in the world.
I asked a skeleton once if it remembered the old sea. It said it remembered boats, which is worse.
There's a Flotsam woman who spits at the mention of Okran. Nobody in the bar there argues with her.
Reva, they call her. Trained by the ninjas, angry with everything holy.
Saw a woman walk out of a Holy Nation sermon mid-prayer once. Reva, somebody said. She did not look back.
Hire Reva and you hire a temper. The sword comes free with it.
There's a Flotsam woman who sleeps outside walls and never in the beds. Digna. She doesn't like to talk about why.
Digna fights like she's paying off something. The kind of debt coin doesn't clear.
Heard Digna left home with her family chasing her. Didn't say who came back.
Hire Digna and you won't hear her complain. You'll hear her wake up at night.
Pia, the girl from Flotsam, jumps at a paladin's shadow. She's also the fastest thing on two legs I've seen.
Her sister died fighting paladins. Pia goes quiet when you say the name Naevia.
Pia wants three thousand cats to go with you. Cheap, for how fast she is.
Pia left the Holy Nation behind. She still checks every door for white cloaks.
Hamut is on the road again. Lost his wife to slavers and the Anti-Slavers would not take him in.
If you see a Greenlander killing slavers with no word at all, that's Hamut.
A widower with a blade. Hamut will fight beside you free, if you hate slavery as he does.
Hamut thinks the world owes him an answer. He seeks it in slavers' blood.
The White Ripper still walks. Bent like a cane now, but they say nobody fenced like him in the Cities.
Crumblejon, the old samurai. Complains about his back and could still cut you in half.
Nobles used him and dropped him. He walks a free road now, and grumbles every step.
If an old man offers you a fight, check his blade first. It might be Crumblejon's.
Old Hobbs will buy you a drink and talk until the rum is gone. Stories of banshees and talking cacti.
He swears he wrestled a gorillo with a bottle in his belly. Nobody has the heart to tell him the gorillo would have won.
Hobbs wants a partner for his wailing thing. If you ever go, take plenty of rum.
Mad as a hatter and kinder than most. Hobbs is the old man who talks to cacti and thanks them.
There's a woman who wanders. Riddly, her name. Wants an adventure, any adventure. Hire her and she's cheerful the whole way.
Friendly sword for hire. Riddly. Never settles, never complains, never turns down a road.
Met Riddly once. Said she was looking for someone to ask her along. Nobody had. Now I regret it.
A lone adventurer who actually smiles. Riddly. It's unsettling and nice.
Crab Town has a woman who prefers crabs to people. Lumi. Harmless unless you hurt a crab.
Lumi speaks to the crabs. They're said to listen. Don't ask me how I know.
Someone in Crab Town speaks fluent crab. I am not joking. Ask Lumi.
Lumi moved there because she dislikes crowds. Crab Town suits her. The crabs didn't object.
A young medic named Izumi wants a sponsor for her experiments. Smart as they come, and she knows it.
Izumi, the girl with the notes and the sharp tongue. Heals better than most doctors twice her age.
Hire her and she will lecture you the whole way. Cheaper than a bad bandage, though.
Heard a girl in the bar telling a noble that his research was nonsense. Izumi. Nobody argued.
Jewel is on the road, dry as bone and sharp as a razor. Not a fighter, but you won't like crossing her.
A Scorchlander woman named Jewel will patch you up and tell you what you did wrong.
Jewel doesn't boast and doesn't flinch.
Had an argument with Jewel over a bill once. I paid.
Soman from the fishing houses is looking for work. Strong hands, plain talk. Needs coin to settle some family business.
Her family is struggling. Soman will join you for the right price and not complain.
Quiet woman, good with her hands. Soman, they call her.
Soman needs thirty-five hundred cats. Sounds like a debt, not a dream.
There is a nervous Scorchlander at the fishing houses with a pocket full of seeds. Green Finger, they call him. Gentle, jumpy.
Green Finger would sooner farm than fight. He will fight if cornered. Apologises afterwards.
A man who plants things in the Scorch. Brave, or daft.
Hire him if you want a quiet, skittish companion. He talks to the plants more than to you.
Sadneil
There is a skeleton in Black Desert City so low-spirited it makes the others look cheerful. Sadneil.
Sadneil
Sadneil will join a party out of pure weakness, then complain at every step. Reliable in a gloomy way.
Sadneil
If a skeleton sighs at you, it's Sadneil.
Sadneil
Heard Sadneil say the gurglers were better company than people. He may be right.
A Shek retainer called Oron hungers for battle. Would pay to be free of their lord. Thirty-five hundred cats, I heard.
Oron is bored. A bored Shek is a dangerous Shek. Hire them before they do something drastic.
There's a warrior in the Shek lands who wants a fight more than a meal. Oron. They would follow you into a pit.
Oron won't stay a peasant much longer. The question is who gets the sword.
There's an escaped slave with a removed brand and a bad temper. Miu. She screams at spiders long before they show.
Miu swears like a miner and fights like a fiend. Sells nothing. Buys nothing.
Her friend died to a spider, so I hear. Miu hasn't forgiven the whole species.
Miu hates the Holy Nation, the Empire and spiders. In that order, depending on the day.
They say Luquin still lives in the Vault. Hold on to that if the Empire frightens you.
Emperor Tengu
Luquin, the farmer's son who killed a lord. They made him write a tribute to Tengu..
The Anti-Slavers still sing about Luquin. Some believe it, some don't.
If you find the Vault, ask for the thin man with a wry mouth.
Garret buys his slave a drink and calls it good business. Nobody in the bar is sure whether to laugh.
They called Garret a slave lover to his face once.
A dealer who pampers his stock. Garret. The Anti-Slavers hate the whole thing and him more.
Garret says a content slave is a profitable slave. Probably the nicest monster I know.
Emperor Tengu
Tengu has a tired little secretary named Koin. He decides who gets favours and who gets nothing.
Koin the diplomat smiles at everyone and trusts no one.
If you want an audience with the Emperor, Koin is the gatekeeper.
Emperor Tengu
They say Koin corrects Tengu's pronunciation and survives. I'd pay to see that.
There's a Hive squire at the Traders Guild who flinches at his own shadow. Yamdu.
Yamdu handles membership enquiries and dreads every one. Kindly man.
The noble's squire fears everything but never fails to help.
If you meet the nervous drone at Trader's Edge, buy something.
The Flotsam guard at the scout post escaped a cannibal cage years ago. Mani. He doesn't joke about cannibals.
Mani trades what he can and kills cannibals when he must. Both with the same face.
Heard Mani lost his friends to a cannibal camp and walked out alone.
If you hurt Flotsam, Mani remembers. If you help, he remembers that too.
Ells the rum thief raided the distillery again. Daft as a post, but nobody can catch him.
Someone put a bounty on a half-wit named Ells. For stealing rum. The world is a strange place.
Ells talks about himself like a stranger. Sweet, in a sad way. Feed him and he follows you anywhere.
Barkeeps hate him, guards beat him, and he still comes back for rum. Ells.
Emperor Tengu
There's a man in Tengu's Vault who calmly says what he did. Psycho, he's called. Nobody says it twice.
Psycho sits in his cell and smiles. The guards stopped speaking to him.
Word is, a martial artist in the Vault is in for disembowelling. Matter-of-fact. That's the frightening part.
Psycho was framed, he insists. Then he tells you what he did anyway.
Emperor Tengu
A Hive worker in Tengu's Vault wants out so badly he stares at the door all day.
Espher speaks little and means all of it.
I heard a South Hive drone sits in the Vault and counts the guards' steps. Espher.
If the Vault falls, Espher will be the first through the door.
Emperor Tengu
A Shek called Sinklyde sits in Tengu's Vault with his pride intact. They haven't broken him yet.
Sinklyde has been behind those bars long enough to learn every guard's name.
A Shek in the Vault? Sinklyde. He will tell you honour is worth more than freedom. Then ask you to break him out.
The Vault holds a Shek who hums battle songs. Sinklyde. Guards complain.
Emperor Tengu
Someone in Tengu's Vault never stops screaming. Screamy. Even the guards take their lunch elsewhere.
Screamy does nothing but scream. Nobody has asked why.
I heard you can hear Screamy from half a mile outside the Vault.
If a scream wakes you at night near the Vault, that's Screamy.
Harmothoe leads the Free Traders. Wealthy in cats, ruthless with thieves.
They sing about Harmothoe in the Free Trader camps. Not a gentle song.
A caravan leader who killed her old masters. Harmothoe. Keep your hands clean when you deal with her.
Harmothoe pays in coin and holds grudges in iron.
Yayoi trains the newer ninjas. Hard on them, fair on the sword.
People say Yayoi fights better than most Flotsam veterans. Few challenge her.
Yayoi walks without a sound. You only notice when it's too late.
Paladins fear Flotsam, and Yayoi is the reason.
White Eyebrow abandoned his duties and now they blame him for the Brown Drought.
Nobody believes one man could cause a drought. Nobody except the clan he left.
White Eyebrow has a camp somewhere in the sands. Wanted. Dangerous.
If the poster is true, he's a menace. If false, he's a scapegoat.
Dhe Fist is ours now. Gates broken, no one fix dhem. Why fix? Dhe door only keeps dhe dinner in.
Okranites built big walls. We live behind dhem. Dhey sleep in dhe ground, quiet, and we have dhe pit going.
Cooking pit in dhe Fist, torches on dhe posts. Holy folk made it nice for us. /CANNIBALTASTY/.
Dhe flame priests not come back. Dhe flame priests not come back anywhere.
We sit where dhey prayed. Sit, and wait. Dhe road bring someone every few days.
Okran's Fist is in cannibal hands. The Nation's own wall, and they are cooking inside it.
People say the Fist's gates hang broken and nobody in the Nation will go near.
No holy lord left to hold the Fist, and the hungry walked in. It is not a thing the scripture planned for.
My cousin served at the Fist. I stopped asking where he went. I hear the smoke from there now.
Pray for the Fist. Pray quietly. The smell is on the wind.
The cannibals took Okran's Fist. A fortress, and they walked in through the gates the Nation forgot to mend.
Heard the Holy Nation's Fist is a cannibal camp now. Don't take that road to save an afternoon.
Holy Lord Phoenix
Phoenix gone, the inquisitor gone, and the Fist went to the cannibals.
I wouldn't trade with anyone coming from the Fist.
The Fist is half in ruin since the leadership broke. The army patrols what still has a roof.
One of our lords is gone and the Fist feels it. Walls stand. Spirits do not.
Patrols at the Fist grow thinner. Nobody says why. Everybody knows.
The Fist keeps its lamps lit, and keeps its fears quieter.
Holy Lord Phoenix
The Fist is half in ruin since Phoenix fell. The army patrols what still has a roof.
Holy Lord Phoenix
Phoenix is gone, and the Fist feels it. Walls stand.
The Fist is bruised, not broken. We tell each other that every watch.
Stack is a Kingdom town now. The Inquisitor is gone and we walked in without drawing. Odd, to win by waiting.
Holy banners down in Stack, our gate guards up.
The flatskins in Stack sell us what they sold the Nation. Cats are cats. We count them just as hard.
Esata the Stone Golem
Esata keeps her word. The Nation broke theirs. So Stack is ours.
Esata the Stone Golem
Stack answers to the Chosen of Kral now. No Esata, no Seta. Just the ones who still remember the Last Stand.
Flying Bull took Stack while the Stone Golem lay cold. Say what you like. Somebody had to hold it.
We hold a Holy town and we don't pray in it. The stone doesn't mind.
Stack was the Nation's. Now it is Kral's. The flatskins in the market still bargain for peace.
Flying Bull
Stack is ruins. The Nation lost it, the Kingdom lost it, and the Bull lost it. Only the wind has a claim.
Nobody holds Stack. It had its gate, its market, its priests. Now it has a lot of empty buildings.
Went by Stack. A town with nobody in charge is just a pile of rooms. I didn't stay.
Flying Bull
I heard the Nation, the Kingdom and the Bull all failed in Stack. It's a rare thing to see all three lose.
Bad Teeth is under Kingdom spears. The pass is ours, and the Nation's door is open for the first time in ages.
A Holy gate town, and Shek patrol it. The priests say it is blasphemy. The priests are not here.
Warriors in the bar, warriors on the wall. Bad Teeth has not been this quiet in years.
Esata the Stone Golem
Seta is gone and the pass fell. Esata didn't even have to ask.
Bad Teeth belongs to Kral's Chosen now. With Esata and Seta gone, Flying Bull had the pass for the asking.
We hold Bad Teeth. We don't hold it politely.
The pass is ours, and so are the patrols. Flatskins who want passage can pay in cats or in manners.
Holy walls, Shek hands. Kral would laugh. Or not. He's hard to read in the Gateway.
Bad Teeth is a ruin. No Phoenix, no Seta, no Esata, no Bull. Nobody left to fight over the rubble.
Heard Bad Teeth is a husk. The pass stands open and nobody guards it. That should worry someone.
They emptied Bad Teeth the way you empty a fish. Everything good is gone and the rest is for the crows.
I used to buy there. Now I buy nowhere near it.
Holy Lord Phoenix
Bad Teeth is wounded. The Phoenix is gone and the Inquisitor has to hold the pass alone.
Half the town stands empty since the fall. We keep the gate. We do not sleep soundly.
Holy Lord Phoenix
Phoenix is gone. Seta lives. Bad Teeth waits to learn which of those matters more.
Bad Teeth bleeds. We bandage it with prayer and hope it is enough.
The Holy Mines have new owners since the Nation lost its leaders. Nobody asks the ore who it prefers.
Heard the Mines are not Holy any longer. Whoever holds them, the ore still comes out of the ground the same.
Holy Lord Phoenix
Phoenix and Seta gone, and the Mines passed to someone with a bigger spear. It's the oldest story there is.
Somebody holds the Holy Mines who doesn't pray there. That's all I know, and all I want to.
Esata the Stone Golem
Esata is gone and Mukai holds Squin. He isn't the Stone Golem. He stands in the same place all the same.
The Mountain keeps Squin. Warriors still obey. The Kingdom has a new back, if not a new head.
Esata the Stone Golem
Mukai doesn't talk about Esata. That tells you how much he thinks about her.
Mukai is a wall that walks. Squin is lucky to have him.
Squin is Kral's now. Mukai is dead, Esata is dead, and the Bull has the seat.
Flying Bull
Flying Bull took Squin without much argument. Nobody was left to argue.
A Shek town with no Shek queen. The Chosen keep the gate, and the gate keeps us.
Kral's colours in Squin. A year ago I would have laughed. Now I keep my head low.
Squin is a ruin. The berserkers sit in the empty rooms. I wouldn't go near it for any price.
The Kingdom lost Squin when Esata, Mukai and the Bull all went down. Berserkers moved into the mess.
Squin used to sell fine goods. Now it sells nothing, to nobody.
Squin is ash and berserkers. I wish I knew how to say it kindly.
Admag is a ruin and berserkers squat in it. Whatever the Kingdom was, it isn't that any more.
They say the Shek capital is empty halls now. A hard thing, for a people who value their seat.
Esata the Stone Golem
Esata held Admag, and Admag held the Kingdom. One is gone, so the other follows.
Admag, where the queen sat. Now the berserkers sit. The world is poorer for both.
High Inquisitor Valtena
Okran's Shield has changed hands. Valtena is gone, and whoever stands there now isn't Holy.
High Inquisitor Valtena
The eastern post stands, but not for the Nation. Valtena was the lock. The lock is gone.
High Inquisitor Valtena
I don't know who holds the Shield these days. I know it isn't Valtena.
The Shield has a new keeper. I won't guess who. Most of the answers are bad.
Drin is rubble. No Tengu, no Inaba, no Valtena. Nobody left to claim it.
They say Drin has no owner at all. A town with no owner is a town with no future.
I walked by Drin. I walked fast.
Drin is a husk now. Nothing left to rob and nobody left to rob it.
The hill is held by outlaws. Our own people, once. That's the worst of it.
Holy Lord Phoenix
Blister Hill fell without Phoenix. They say the houses are full of strangers.
I pray for the hill. The hill does not pray back.
They hold the hill and call it ours. It was ours.
Blister Hill belongs to outlaws now. The Nation's seat, and the Nation lost it to its own scum.
Heard the hill is held by Holy Outlaws. Don't mistake them for the old Nation. These people have no priest.
Holy Lord Phoenix
The Nation without Phoenix is a mob. Blister Hill is the proof.
A hill with no priest is a hill with no law. Keep your coins in your boots.
We keep a hill the Nation held. I still check the corners for them.
Flotsam holds the hill. Do not tell anyone how it feels to sleep in their beds.
The runaways keep the hill, and we guard it with the kind of care that comes from knowing what loses it.
The Nation built this hill. We use it. Nobody mentions that part at the table.
Rebirth is Flotsam's now. They say the doors stand open and the servants walk free.
I heard the Rebirth school has no master. I hope the people in there got out.
Phoenix, Seta, Valtena. All gone, and Rebirth went to the ones the Nation hated most. It's a fair joke.
Rebirth, held by the runaways. I wonder if they can stand to sleep in it.
Rebirth is empty. Outlaws squat in its halls. No Nation, no Flotsam.
Word is, you can hear nothing at Rebirth now. That's worse than screaming.
Nobody wants Rebirth. Not even the people who made it.
Rebirth is a husk with squatters. I'd sooner sleep in the sand.
Fort Simion is a ruin since Tengu fell. Rebel swordsmen camp in the broken parts.
The old fort has nobody in charge. The rebels live in it like rats in a granary.
Tengu is dead and Simion is wrecked. I don't know what the fort was before, and now I never will.
Boss Simion
Fort Simion is a cracked shell. I walked past once. I didn't look in.
Stoat belongs to us hunters now. Empire left, the desert came in, and we kept what we found.
We dig the ruins and we sell the finds. It's as good a government as Stoat ever had.
No lord to bow to. Just a market, a crowd, and our own pockets.
The hunters keep Stoat. It's a market with a gun behind it.
Lord Inaba
Stoat has no lord now. Inaba is dead and the Empire has other worries. Whoever grabs it, grabs it.
Heard Stoat is outlaw country since the lord fell. Don't carry anything you can't afford to lose.
Tengu gone, Inaba gone. Stoat is a plum with nobody guarding the tree.
Stoat has no lord, and the vultures know it. So do I.
Sho-Battai is quiet. Quiet is good. Quiet means dhe pit is full.
Dhe Empire had a wall. We have dhe pit. Dhe wall is still dhere. Dhe pit is just newer.
Dhere were lords here. Dhere are guests here.
Dhe gates are broken. We never fix. Dhe road is dhe door.
Sho-Battai is gone to the cannibals. A walled town, and now a pit. Nobody warned them in time.
Heard Lord Nagata is dead, and Simion too. Sho-Battai has no one left to bar the gate.
I used to buy hats in Sho-Battai. I don't know who sells them now.
Sho-Battai is quiet now. Quiet is the worst sound of all.
Catun belongs to the fish now. The smiths left, the Gurglers came, and the water is coming in.
Catun is a gurgler town. A pity. They made good steel there.
I heard Lord Shiro is dead. Catun went quiet, then it got bloody.
Catun is a sunken thing. The fish keep it company.
Crab Queen
Crab Town is held by the fish since the Crab Queen fell. The crabs don't mind.
Gurglers sit in Crab Town. They are no worse than the Raiders, and no better.
Without the Queen, Crab Town lost its spine.
Crab Town without its Queen is a fishmonger's dream and a trader's nightmare.
Lady Tsugi
Brink belongs to the Reavers now. Tsugi is dead and the Reavers have a town to hold. They don't hold it gently.
Heard Brink has Reaver patrols. Stay clear.
Lady Tsugi
Lady Tsugi gone and the Reavers took Brink in the same breath.
Brink was a Cities town. It's a Reaver town now. The cats still flow, to different hands.
Grayflayer is Band of Bones ground now. Gray is gone, Grim is gone, and we came down from the hills.
The swamp changes hands often. We hold this part. Don't take it personally.
We keep our bones close, and Grayflayer is a good place to keep them.
Bones keep Grayflayer. The swamp doesn't care who holds it.
Heft is a rebel town now. The Emperor is dead and the lords are scrambling. We keep our heads down and our knives sharp.
Emperor Tengu
No Tengu, no Emperor. Heft bar is full of people who don't know what happens next.
A revolution is a mess. This one is quiet so far. That's what worries me.
Heft changed owners without anyone noticing. Which is how the best changes happen.
Bark belongs to the peasants since Sanda fell. The farmers keep their own stores for once.
We eat what we grow. For the first time in memory, that's a sentence that works.
No lord in Bark. No overseer. I keep waiting for someone to come and fix that.
Bark is ours now. I never thought I'd say that.
Clownsteady belongs to the people since the slavers were dealt with. It is not rich. It is ours.
No more market master. No more Grace. Nobody said a word about it for a while.
We keep what's left. We share what we can. Don't mistake that for weakness.
Clownsteady changed. The cages aren't what they were.
Drifter's Last is a Free Trader town now. Merin is dead and Grace is dead.
No lady, no mistress. The Free Traders keep their ledgers and their gates.
We trade here without paying a lord. It isn't much, but it isn't nothing.
Free Traders keep Drifter's Last. We keep it fair, or we keep it gone.
Bark is half in ruins since Lady Sanda fell. The repairs are slow and the money is slower.
Sanda is gone and the town shows it. Cracked walls, empty stalls, and a long wait for relief.
I keep a bucket by the door. Everything leaks since Sanda.
Half of Bark is ruins now. The other half is busy ignoring it.
Lord Inaba
Stoat is half broken since Inaba fell. The Empire patches what it can.
Lord Inaba
No Lord Inaba, no steady hand. Stoat sells what is left and counts the losses.
Stoat isn't what it was. Come in, buy, and don't look too hard at the walls.
Stoat is half rubble. The rest holds on out of spite.
Lord Nagata
Sho-Battai is half in ruin since Nagata fell. The guards do what they can.
Lord Nagata
Lord Nagata is gone. The wall holds, mostly.
Lord Nagata
Half the shops closed since Nagata. I sell hats to the other half.
Sho-Battai is half broken. We call it half whole.
Drifter's Last is half in ruin since Merin fell. The stalls that remain charge twice.
The Lady is gone, and Drifter's Last is only a place to stop on the way somewhere better.
Merin kept this town in order. Now it keeps itself, badly.
Drifter's Last is half broken. The inn still pours.
All the lords are gone. The Emperor, Sanda, Tsugi, Inaba, Nagata, Yoshinaga. Who signs the cats now?
No nobles left in the Empire. Only clerks and guards. And the clerks are watching the guards.
The Empire without lords is a market without a floor. We're all waiting for it to drop.
I served a lord once. Now I serve a ledger. The ledger doesn't pay either.
Every lord of the Empire is dead. I didn't think I'd live to say that. Don't say it too loud.
No lords. No tax collectors. Just us, our farms, and the question of who comes next.
The nobles are gone. The farmers are still here. That is how it ends, in the long run.
Lords die. Wheat grows. That's the whole of history.
I hear the Empire has no lords left. A strange thing, an empire with only the people.
All the Empire's nobles are dead, people say. I wouldn't take work in the Great Desert just now.
A land without lords is a land open to whoever has the nerve.
The Empire has no noble left alive. I don't know how that ends. I'm not in a hurry to learn.
The northern masters are all dead. Grande, Haga, Ruben, Wada, Ren. Even Kana. Even Longen.
No masters in the north. The cages are full and the keys are in nobody's hands.
Without the northern masters the work camps are barely run. The overseers are fighting over who gives orders.
The Traders are headless in the north.
The northern masters are all dead. I won't say I'm sorry.
Every one of them, gone. The camps still stand.
No masters in the north. The next job is the cages.
The north has no masters. The cages need opening. I know a few who will.
The southern masters are dead. The Market Master and Grace both. The market has nobody to sell for.
No Grace, no Market Master. The south is quiet and the buyers have nothing to buy.
Slave Mistress Grace is dead. I hear the southern cages are empty. I did not hear who emptied them.
No Grace, no Market Master. The south is a market with nobody to sell to.
Merin, Grace and the Market Master. The south has no boss left. Someone is going to take it.
All the southern bosses are dead. A town without a boss is a town waiting to be taken.
No Merin, no Grace, no Market Master. The south is unmanaged, and the unmanaged don't stay that way.
The south has no bosses now. That's a gap, and gaps get filled.
Phoenix, Seta and Valtena. All fallen. The Nation has no head and no hands.
We still say the words. The words feel hollow.
Which of us leads? Nobody knows. Which of us follows? We all do.
The three pillars are down. We wait for the roof to follow.
Holy Lord Phoenix
The Phoenix and both Inquisitors are gone. The Nation is a body without a mouth. We keep quiet and watch.
I didn't think I'd live to see it. I won't say it out loud.
The Holy leaders are all dead. The soldiers don't know what to do with their hands.
The Nation lost every head it had. I drink to nobody, and I drink to everybody.
The Nation has no leaders left. Some would call this the time to strike. Nobody has called it yet.
The Holy lords are all dead. The old enemy has no face now. It is stranger than it sounds.
A people with no head still have teeth. Keep your guard up, flatskin or Shek.
The Nation is leaderless. A fallen enemy is still an enemy, /FLATSKIN/.
The Bugmaster and Phoenix are both dead. Two heads that ruled with fear, gone.
No Bugmaster, no Phoenix. I'm not sure whether to drink or to hide.
Everyone who feared the pair is now afraid of what follows.
Two tyrants gone. I'll wait to see what grows in the gap.
The thrall masters are defeated. Ponk and Screamer both. The machines have nobody to answer to.
I heard Ponk and Screamer are down. Their thralls will walk anyway, I suspect.
No Screamer, no Ponk. Someone walked into the ash and came out. That doesn't happen.
The thrall masters fell. The thralls don't know it yet. Or they do, and can't say.
Heft is held by the peasants since the Emperor died. Don't expect lords to come back.
Heft changed hands quietly. The lords didn't even notice until it was done.
Emperor Tengu
Tengu dead, and Heft belongs to the people. Odd to hear it said aloud.
I used to sell in Heft to the lords. Now I sell to whoever has cats. It's all the same.
Bark is run by peasants now. The farmers kept their own stores for once.
Emperor Tengu
Lady Sanda dead, Tengu dead. Bark goes on with farmers at the gate.
Bark is a peasant town. They sell wheat to anyone.
Heard Bark has no lord. No tax.
Sho-Battai is run by farmers now. No lord left, no Emperor.
The town is poorer, but it's ours.
Boss Simion
Simion keeps us fed. I don't ask where the food comes from.
We were afraid when the lords fell. Then we ate.
Trader's Edge is ours. The Empire is gone, and so are the old guards. We hold it with what we have.
A free town. No lord. No collar. Just us and the gate.
We keep the Edge for those who came here with scars on their wrists.
Free, and still poor. I'll take that over the alternative.
The Fist is half in ruin. The Nation lost a leader, and the walls started to crack.
I hear Okran's Fist is in trouble. The Nation doesn't say. The cracks do.
A Holy fortress with half its roof. The army holds what's left.
The Nation is thinner at the Fist now. Someone will notice, and that someone won't be friendly.
